'''Aundray Bruce''' (born April 30, 1966) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). As a [[college football]] player, he played [[defensive end]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]] before the [[Atlanta Falcons]] selected him with the [[List of first overall National Football League draft picks|first overall pick]] in the [[1988 NFL draft]]. He played in the NFL for the Falcons and [[Oakland Raiders|Los Angeles/Oakland Raiders]].

==Early life==
Bruce was born in [[Montgomery, Alabama]].  He attended [[George Washington Carver High School (Montgomery, Alabama)|George Washington Carver High School]] in Montgomery. A [[high school football|high school]] phenom, Bruce started at tight end and outside linebacker. He also returned kicks and played four additional positions on offense (quarterback, running back, wide receiver, offensive tackle) and four other positions on defense (defensive tackle, defensive end, nose guard, cornerback). While he excelled in football, basketball was Bruce's first love. He led [[George Washington Carver High School (Montgomery, Alabama)|George Washington Carver High School]] to the 4-A basketball state championship in both his junior and senior years. As a senior, he was named the state tournament's MVP and won an All-Star game dunk contest.

==College career==
Bruce was named [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] in 1986 and 1987, [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] in 1987, and [[Citrus Bowl]] [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]] in 1987.  He first garnered national attention in a game in 1987 against [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets football|Georgia Tech]] by intercepting three passes and returning one for a touchdown and making 10 unassisted tackles. Entering the NFL Draft, he was saddled with expectations of becoming the next [[Lawrence Taylor]], though once drafted was described as "unquestionably the least heralded No. 1 draft choice this decade."<ref name="s336">{{Cite web |last=George |first=Thomas |date=1988-07-10 |title=Falcons' Bruce Riding High And Promising Not to Fall |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/07/10/sports/falcons-bruce-riding-high-and-promising-not-to-fall.html |access-date=2024-12-04 |website=The New York Times}}</ref> He graduated from Auburn in 1988 as an education major.

==Professional career==
Bruce was drafted with the first overall pick in the [[1988 NFL draft]] by the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1988 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1988/draft.htm |access-date=2023-09-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/03/31/sports/sports-people-bruce-to-be-no-1.html|title= Sports People; Bruce to Be No. 1|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 31, 1988|access-date=September 16, 2007}}</ref> Bruce enjoyed his most prominent role on the Falcons 1991 playoff team when he saw spot duty on offense as a tight end as well as defense.  He signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders|Los Angeles Raiders]] as a free agent in 1992 and finished his career with the organization.<ref>{{cite web | title=Aundray Bruce Transactions | website=Pro Football Archives | url=https://profootballarchives.com/transactions/b/bruc00200.html | access-date=2025-07-06}}</ref> Bruce played in 151 games over his 11-season career, posting 32 sacks and 4 interceptions. While Bruce concluded his career with a 7-season tenure in Oakland, he is typically regarded as a draft bust. Despite being the #1 overall pick, he never made an All-Pro or Pro Bowl team, never had double-figure sack totals in a season, and only started 42 games. He only played for two playoff teams in his long career.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20080619164023/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/multimedia/photo_gallery/0804/nfl.draft.busts/content.2.html Top draft busts of the modern era]}}</ref>

'''Audray Glenn McMillian''' (born August 13, 1962), is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] for eight seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1985 to 1993 for the [[History of the Houston Oilers|Houston Oilers]] and [[Minnesota Vikings]]. McMillian played [[college football]] for the [[Houston Cougars football|Houston Cougars]] and was selected by the [[New England Patriots]] in the third round of the [[1985 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1985 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1985/draft.htm |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was a [[Pro Bowl]] selection in 1992 after leading the NFL, along with [[Henry Jones (football player)|Henry Jones]] of the [[Buffalo Bills]], with eight [[interception]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1992 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1992/probowl.htm |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Audray McMillian Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/McMiAu00.htm |access-date=March 21, 2024 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=2012 Awards Gala Tribute to Audray McMillian| date=April 30, 2012 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q_EWbmpMgD8|language=en|access-date=November 19, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Cougars NFL Draft History|url=https://uhcougars.com/sports/2021/3/29/cougars-nfl-draft-history.aspx|access-date=November 19, 2021|website=University of Houston Athletics|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Zachary McMillian - Football|url=https://uhcougars.com/sports/football/roster/zachary-mcmillian/1207|access-date=November 19, 2021|website=University of Houston Athletics|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Toledo Blade - Google News Archive Search|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=6G4xAAAAIBAJ&sjid=7gIEAAAAIBAJ&pg=6655,299982|access-date=November 19, 2021|website=news.google.com}}</ref>

'''Aundrae Akeem Allison''' (born June 25, 1984) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the fifth round of the [[2007 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[East Carolina Pirates football|East Carolina Pirates]].

He was also a member of the [[New York Jets]], [[Virginia Destroyers]], and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].

==Early life==
Allison attended [[A. L. Brown High School]] in [[Kannapolis, North Carolina]]. He was an [[Associated Press]] All-State selection during his senior season and earned All-Conference honors twice.

==College career==

===Georgia Military College===
Allison enrolled at Georgia Military College in Milledgeville, GA January 2003 after leaving Coffeyville JUCO. He made junior college all-American and also earned a two-year AAS degree from the prestigious school.

===East Carolina University===
Allison played [[college football]] at [[East Carolina University]] for two years.  In 2005, Allison was the first player in school history to pick up over 1,000 reception yards with 83 catches for 1,024 yards. He had seven touchdowns in 11 games that season. Allison's 83 receptions are second in all-time single-season school history. In addition, Allison averaged 12.3 yards per reception and 93.1 yards per game (second best in [[Conference USA]]) and had five 100-yard receiving games, which was the most in a single season at ECU. Allison led the conference and was 4th nationally in receptions per game with 7.55. At the conclusion of the season, Allison was named a first-team All-Conference USA selection. During the 2006 season his production went down a bit, finishing with 62 receptions for 708 and four touchdowns. After the 2006 season, Allison entered the NFL draft.

==Professional career==

===Minnesota Vikings===
Allison was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the fifth round (146th overall) of the [[2007 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

During his rookie season with the Vikings, Allison served as a wide receiver and kickoff returner. In Week 13 against the [[Detroit Lions]], Allison returned a kickoff 104 yards for a touchdown—a franchise record at the time.  Although not starting, he appeared in 11 of 16 regular season games. He caught a total of 8 passes for 122 yds, and returned 20 kicks for 574 yards.<ref name="NFL">{{cite web|title=nfl.com player gamelog|url=http://www.nfl.com/players/aundraeallison/careerstats?id=ALL709826|publisher=The Official Site of the National Football League|access-date=December 26, 2007}}</ref>

Allison recorded 10 receptions for 109 yards in 2008. After the team's failed attempts to trade him, Allison was waived by the Vikings on August 4, 2009.

===New York Jets===
Allison was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Jets]] on August 5, 2009.<ref>{{cite tweet |url=https://www.twitter.com/RosenhausSports/statuses/3152774893 |title=Congrats to Aundrae Allison who was claimed by the Jets today |number=3152774893 |last=Rosenhaus |first=Drew |user=DrewJRosenhaus |date=August 5, 2009 |access-date=August 31, 2022}}</ref> The team waived wide receiver [[Mario Urrutia]] to make room for Allison on the roster. Allison was sidelined for the 2009 season after suffering a torn ACL against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the Jets final preseason game. Allison recovered and was preparing to maintain a spot on the active roster.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/blog/posts/1643-allison-draws-motivation-from-all-around-him?rss_category=blog&rss_article_id=1643-allison-draws-motivation-from-all-around-him |title=Allison Draws Motivation All Around Him |last=Lange |first=Randy |date=May 31, 2010 |publisher=NewYorkJets.com |access-date=June 5, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100606034030/http://www.newyorkjets.com/blog/posts/1643-allison-draws-motivation-from-all-around-him?rss_category=blog&rss_article_id=1643-allison-draws-motivation-from-all-around-him |archive-date=June 6, 2010 |url-status=dead |df=mdy }}</ref> This effort would be cut short as Allison was waived on August 29, 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nfl/news/story?id=5509593 |title=Jets cut veteran WR Laveranues Coles |author=Cimini, Rich |date=August 29, 2010 |publisher=ESPN New York |access-date=August 29, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100901223616/http://sports.espn.go.com/new-york/nfl/news/story?id=5509593| archive-date= September 1, 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref>

===Virginia Destroyers (first stint)===
Allison was selected by the [[Virginia Destroyers]] in the fourth round (19th overall) of the [[2011 UFL draft]]. He signed with the team for the 2011 season on July 6, 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4243179 |title=UFL Transactions |date=July 6, 2011 |work=OurSports Central |access-date=July 6, 2011}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On August 14, 2011, Allison signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], but was waived on August 29.

===Virginia Destroyers (second stint)===
After being waived by the Buccaneers, Allison was re-signed by the Destroyers. The Destroyers, coached by NFL legend [[Marty Schottenheimer]], would become the UFL champions with Allison leading the team in all receiving categories.

==Personal life==
In 2010, Allison created the luxury fashion brand Wealthy War Intentions. The brand is co-owned by former [[New York Jets]] running back [[Chris Johnson (running back)|Chris Johnson]], whom Allison went to college with.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.thecityinsight.com/index.php/beauty/959-wealthy-war-intentions-officially-debuts-its-ultra-luxurymen-s-t-shirt-collection |title=Wealthy War Intentions Officially Debuts its Ultra Luxury Men¹s T-Shirt Collection |access-date=June 25, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130916190408/http://www.thecityinsight.com/index.php/beauty/959-wealthy-war-intentions-officially-debuts-its-ultra-luxurymen-s-t-shirt-collection |archive-date=September 16, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Austin Kirk Collie''' (born November 11, 1985) is a Canadian-born American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Brigham Young University Cougars football|BYU Cougars]] and was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the fourth round of the [[2009 NFL draft]]. Collie also played in the NFL for the [[New England Patriots]] and in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) for the [[BC Lions]].

==Early life==
Collie was born in [[Hamilton, Ontario]], Canada, to American parents Scott and Nicole Collie.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/players/austincollie/profile?id=COL397342 |title=Austin Collie Profile |publisher=NFL |access-date= June 13, 2012}}</ref><ref name="scott">{{cite web|url=https://byucougars.com/sports/football/roster/player/austin-collie|title=Austin Collie|publisher=[[BYU Cougars]]|access-date=30 Jan 2026}}</ref> Scott Collie also played football at [[Brigham Young University]] (BYU) from 1979 to 1982 and played professionally in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) for the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]] and briefly in the NFL for the San Francisco 49ers during the 1983 preseason.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Doyel |first=Gregg |date=August 23, 2012 |title=Why is concussion-prone Austin Collie still in NFL? He's like his dad |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/story/19883912/why-is-concussionprone-austin-collie-still-in-nfl-hes-like-his-dad |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120823231533/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/story/19883912/why-is-concussionprone-austin-collie-still-in-nfl-hes-like-his-dad |archive-date=August 23, 2012 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref>

Collie starred as a wide receiver at [[Oak Ridge High School (El Dorado Hills, California)|Oak Ridge High School]] in [[El Dorado Hills, California]], and garnered many awards. He was a PrepStar and SuperPrep All-American as well as being voted Northern California's Most Valuable Player. During his senior season, he recorded 60 receptions for a total of 978 yards and 18 touchdowns. In 2004, Collie became an [[Eagle Scout (Boy Scouts of America)|Eagle Scout]].<ref name="collieeagle">{{cite web|title=Before Football, Colts Wide Receiver Snagged Accolades in a Different Uniform |work=Scouting |url=http://blog.scoutingmagazine.org/2010/02/before-football-colts-wide-receiver-snagged-accolades-in-a-different-uniform.html |date=February 3, 2010 |access-date=February 9, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100209125706/http://blog.scoutingmagazine.org/2010/02/before-football-colts-wide-receiver-snagged-accolades-in-a-different-uniform.html |archive-date=February 9, 2010 |url-status=dead  }}</ref>

In December 2009, Collie's hometown newspaper, ''[[The Sacramento Bee]]'', named him Sacramento Area's Player of the Decade (2000–2009).<ref>{{cite news|last=Davidson |first=Joe |title=All decade team: This Collie a master of many tricks |url=http://www.sacbee.com/2009/12/27/2422210/all-decade-team-this-collie-a.html |access-date=November 25, 2010 |newspaper=Sacramento Bee |date=December 27, 2009 }}{{dead link|date=October 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

==College career==
In 2004, Collie was named MWC Freshman of the Year. He was also named the MVP of the [[2007 Las Vegas Bowl]] and named to the All-MWC first-team in 2008.

Collie set a series of records during his three-year career at BYU (2004, 2007–2008).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.byucougars.com/Profile.jsp?ID=2127 |title=Austin Collie Profile |publisher=BYUCougars.com |access-date=June 13, 2012 |archive-date=March 16, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080316172248/http://www.byucougars.com/Profile.jsp?ID=2127 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
Collie impressed [[Indianapolis Colts]] Head Coach [[Jim Caldwell (American football)|Jim Caldwell]] in the preseason and was placed third on the depth chart at the wide receiver position for the [[2009 NFL season|2009 season]], placing ahead of [[Pierre Garçon]] for the slot receiver position. However, Garçon jumped Collie on the depth chart shortly thereafter.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.colts.com/sub.cfm?page=depth|title=Colts.com Depth Chart Update|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090209020426/http://www.colts.com/sub.cfm?page=depth|archive-date=February 9, 2009}}</ref> Collie finished his rookie season in the [[National Football League|NFL]] among the top statistical leaders for all rookies at the wide receiver position.

Collie started his second year strong, making numerous touchdown catches and establishing himself as [[Peyton Manning]]'s "go-to guy" after [[Dallas Clark]] suffered a season-ending injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=5714509|title=Colts place Dallas Clark on IR for wrist|work=ESPN.com|date=October 22, 2010|access-date=August 3, 2015}}</ref> However, on November 7, 2010, Collie was involved in a collision against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], in which he was hit on both sides of his head by [[Quintin Mikell]] and [[Kurt Coleman]]. Collie was taken off the field on a stretcher. According to a televised [[ESPN]] update, Collie was seen sitting up and moving after several minutes working with medics.<ref>{{cite web|last=CBSSports.com wire reports|title=Colts wideout Collie carted off field with head injury|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/story/14257351|publisher=CBSSports.com|access-date=November 7, 2010}}</ref> Collie suffered a concussion as a result of the collision.<ref>{{cite news|last=Leahy|first=Sean|title=Colts' Austin Collie alert after concussion in scary hit vs. Eagles|url=http://content.usatoday.com/communities/thehuddle/post/2010/11/colts-austin-collie-alert-after-concussion-in-scary-hit-vs-eagles/1|access-date=November 9, 2010|newspaper=USA Today|date=November 7, 2010}}</ref> Coleman was penalized for unnecessary roughness for the hit on Collie, but neither player was fined, as the NFL later ruled that the contact that caused the injury was incidental as a result of Mikell's initial hit. On December 19, Collie was hit in the head by Jaguars linebacker [[Daryl Smith (linebacker)|Daryl Smith]] and was down for several minutes. It was his second concussion-related injury that year and ultimately ended his 2010 season.<ref>{{cite news|last=Chappell|first=Mike|title=With Collie recovering, Colts talk of crackdown on hits|url=http://www.indystar.com/article/20101109/SPORTS03/11090316/With-Collie-recovering-Colts-talk-of-crackdown-on-hits |access-date=November 9, 2010|newspaper=The Indianapolis Star|date=November 9, 2010}}</ref> Despite the fact that no fines were assessed, the highly visible injuries to Collie added to [[Concussions in American football|the debate about violent hits in football]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Wilson|first=Phillip|title=Repercussions from hit on Colts' Austin Collie|url=http://blogs.indystar.com/philb/2010/11/08/repercussions-from-austin-collies-hit/|access-date=November 9, 2010|newspaper=The Indianapolis Star|date=November 8, 2010|archive-date=November 10, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101110005635/http://blogs.indystar.com/philb/2010/11/08/repercussions-from-austin-collies-hit/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Bennett|first=Dashiell|title=Why Austin Collie's Injury Will Force Another NFL Rule Change|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/why-austin-collies-injury-will-force-another-nfl-rule-change-2010-11|access-date=November 9, 2010|newspaper=Business Insider|date=November 8, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101110212840/http://www.businessinsider.com/why-austin-collies-injury-will-force-another-nfl-rule-change-2010-11| archive-date= November 10, 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> On December 22, Collie was placed on [[injured reserve]].

Collie played in all 16 games, making 5 starts, during the 2011 regular season, but managed to only catch one touchdown pass among his 54 receptions.

During a 2012 preseason game against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], Collie suffered his third concussion of his career. During the third game of the 2012 season against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], Collie suffered a [[patellar tendon rupture|ruptured patellar tendon]] in his right knee, causing him to miss the rest of the 2012 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/8420967/austin-collie-indianapolis-colts-miss-season-knee-injury|title=Austin Collie ruptured knee tendon|work=ESPN.com|date=September 24, 2012}}</ref>

On February 15, 2013, Collie was told he would not be re-signed by the Colts.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tracking.si.com/2013/02/15/colts-release-dwight-freeney-austin-collie/|title=Report: Colts release Dwight Freeney, Austin Collie|publisher=SI.com|date=February 15, 2013|access-date=February 15, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130217150200/http://tracking.si.com/2013/02/15/colts-release-dwight-freeney-austin-collie/|archive-date=February 17, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/02/15/report-colts-wont-re-sign-dwight-freeney-austin-collie/|title=Report: Colts won't re-sign Dwight Freeney, Austin Collie|last=Alper|first=Josh|publisher=NBCSports.com|date=February 15, 2013|access-date=February 16, 2013}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On August 2, 2013, the [[San Francisco 49ers]] signed Collie to a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/austin-collie-san-francisco-49ers-sign-1-year-contract-0ap1000000225165|title=Austin Colie, San Francisco 49ers sign 1-year contract|last=Wesseling|first=Chris|work=NFL.com|date=August 2, 2013|access-date=August 2, 2013}}</ref> He was released on August 31, during final roster cuts.

===New England Patriots===
The [[New England Patriots]] signed Collie as a free agent on October 3, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.patspulpit.com/2013/10/3/4798390/patriots-sign-austin-collie|title=Patriots Sign Autin Collie|last=Shane|first=Alec|publisher=patspulpit.com|date=October 3, 2013|access-date=October 3, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nfl/story/_/id/9763203/new-england-patriots-sign-veteran-austin-collie|title=New England Patriots Sign Veteran Austin Collie|last=Yates|first=Field|work=ESPN.com|date=October 3, 2013|access-date=October 3, 2013}}</ref> He was signed for a one-year, veteran-minimum contract, which was $715,000 but prorated to $546,765. Due to Collie's previous injuries, the contract included an injury waiver, meaning that the Patriots could release him if he were injured and only owe him a "split" (50%) of the contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalfootballpost.com/Austin-Collies-minimum-Patriots-deal-includes-injury-waiver.html|title=Austin Collie's Minimum Patriots Deal Includes Injury Waiver|last=Wilson|first=Wilson|publisher=NationFootballPost.com|date=October 5, 2013|access-date=October 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131007022737/http://www.nationalfootballpost.com/Austin-Collies-minimum-Patriots-deal-includes-injury-waiver.html|archive-date=October 7, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released on November 5, because of a knee injury, after only 3 catches for 34 yards.<ref name="Collierelease">{{cite web |last=Yates |first=Field |author-link=Field Yates |date=November 5, 2013 |title=Source: Pats release Austin Collie |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nfl/story/_/id/9930895/new-england-patriots-release-receiver-austin-collie |access-date=November 5, 2013}}</ref> Collie was re-signed by the Patriots on December 5, to add depth as rookie wideouts [[Aaron Dobson]] and [[Kenbrell Thompkins]] dealt with nagging injuries.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2013 |title=Patriots Re-Sign Austin Collie - CBS Boston |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/patriots-re-sign-austin-collie/ |access-date=September 13, 2023 |website=cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was released once more on December 27, only to be re-signed on January 2, 2014. The Patriots released Collie again after the playoffs.

===BC Lions===
On January 29, 2015, the [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] announced they had signed Collie to a contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bclions.com/article/lions-sign-NFL-veteran-receiver-austin-collie|title=LIONS SIGN NFL VETERAN RECEIVER AUSTIN COLLIE|work=bclions.com|date=January 29, 2015|access-date=January 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150130023316/http://bclions.com/article/lions-sign-NFL-veteran-receiver-austin-collie|archive-date=January 30, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his only CFL season, Collie played in 16 games, catching 43 passes for 439 yards with 7 touchdowns. Collie also recorded a touchdown as a passer, throwing a 21-yard score to quarterback [[Jonathon Jennings]] on a trick play.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 4, 2015 |title=Jennings "like a video game" in win over Riders |url=https://www.bclions.com/2015/10/04/jennings-like-a-video-game-in-win-over-riders/ |website=BC Lions}}</ref>

On April 8, 2016, Collie announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2016/04/06/lions-announce-austin-collie-intends-retire/|title=Austin Collie intends to retire, Lions announce|website=CFL.ca|date=April 6, 2016|access-date=April 7, 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==

Collie took two years off BYU, 2005-2006, to serve a mission for [[the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] in Buenos Aires, Argentina.<ref name="scott"></ref>  Collie is married and has five kids.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BvaTSQOBPUM/ | title=Instagram }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BxBgYl9BkSI/ | title=Instagram }}</ref> After retiring from professional football Collie joined Cognitive FX, a concussion treatment center in [[Provo, Utah]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.ksl.com/article/39228748/ex-byu-and-nfl-player-focuses-new-career-on-concussions |title=Ex-BYU and NFL player focuses new career on concussions |last=Hollenhorst|first=John|publisher=ksl.com|date=April 7, 2016|access-date=October 1, 2022}}</ref>

Offensive assistant * Seattle Seahawks ({{NFL Year|2020|2021}})
Quarterbacks coach | highlights = * [[Burlsworth Trophy]] (2011) * [[Conerly Trophy]] (2011) * 2× Second-team All-[[Conference USA|C-USA]] ([[2010 Conference USA football season|2010]], [[2011 Conference USA football season|2011]]) | statlabel1 = [[Passing attempts]] | statvalue1 = 378 | statlabel2 = [[Passing completions]] | statvalue2 = 236 | statlabel3 = [[Completion percentage]] | statvalue3 = 62.4% | statlabel4 = [[Touchdown|TD]]–[[Interception|INT]] | statvalue4 = 13–12 | statlabel5 = [[Passing yards]] | statvalue5 = 2,548 | statlabel6 = [[Passer rating]] | statvalue6 = 80.4 | pfr = DaviAu00 }} '''Austin Davis''' (born June 2, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for seven seasons. He played [[college football]] for the [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles football|Southern Miss Golden Eagles]], where he began his career as a [[walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] before becoming a four-year starter. After going undrafted in the [[2012 NFL draft]], Davis signed with the [[St. Louis Rams]]. He started eight games for the Rams in 2014 and two games for the [[Cleveland Browns]] in 2015. He was also on the active rosters of the [[Denver Broncos]], [[Seattle Seahawks]] and [[Tennessee Titans]], and the [[practice squad]] of the [[Miami Dolphins]]. Davis was later the Seahawks' quarterbacks coach for two seasons. ==Early life== Davis was born on June 2, 1989. Davis attended [[West Lauderdale High School]] in [[Collinsville, Mississippi]], where he was coached by Stan McCain. He would become the winningest quarterback in the school's history. As a senior, Davis threw for 1,100 yards passing with 15 touchdowns, rushed for 600 yards with six touchdowns and recorded a 67 percent completion rating. He was a four-year [[Letterman (sports)|letterwinner]] and was named team MVP. During his career, Davis received all-area honors, was named best offensive back in the district and played in the Mississippi/Alabama All-Star game. Davis' cousin, [[Jason Smith (baseball)|Jason Smith]], had a nine-year career in [[Major League Baseball]]{{cite web|title=Austin Davis, Southern Mississippi, NFL Draft|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/historical/1265479|work=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=December 1, 2015}} and his brother, Bo, played [[baseball]] for the [[San Diego Padres]] organization and helped lead the [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles baseball|Southern Miss Golden Eagles]] to their first [[College World Series]] appearance. Davis was also an all-state baseball player in high school. ==College career== Davis' only football scholarship offer came from [[Southeastern Louisiana Lions football|Southeastern Louisiana]] of the [[Football Championship Subdivision]].{{cite news|last1=Bloomquist |first1=Bret |title=UTEP football: Southern MIss Eagles return to winning ways again |url=http://archive.elpasotimes.com/sports/ci_19212568/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208144831/http://archive.elpasotimes.com/sports/ci_19212568/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 8, 2015 |access-date=December 1, 2015 |work=[[El Paso Times]] |date=October 28, 2011 }} He chose instead to attend the [[University of Southern Mississippi]] on a baseball scholarship.{{cite news|last1=Jordan|first1=Jason|title=HS coach says Rams QB Austin Davis went a year without throwing a pick until the last practice|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2014/high-school-football-austin-davis-st-louis-rams-rams-austin-davis|access-date=December 1, 2015|work=[[USA Today]]|date=October 23, 2014}} Davis was a [[walk-on (sport term)|walk-on]] to the [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles football|Golden Eagles football]] program and redshirted the 2007 season.{{cite web |url=http://southernmiss.cstv.com/photos/schools/smis/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/09-mediaguide-section5.pdf |title=2009 Media Guide |publisher=[[University of Southern Mississippi]] |access-date=August 30, 2009 }}{{Dead link|date=May 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{cite news|last=Cleveland |first=Rick |url=http://www.hattiesburgamerican.com/article/20090903/SOUTHERNMISS/90902023/-1/NEWS17 |title=Golden Eagles poised for big year |newspaper=The Hattiesburg American |date=September 3, 2009 |access-date=March 26, 2015 }}{{dead link|date=October 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} For 2008, Davis was named the starting quarterback by head coach [[Larry Fedora]] and became the first freshman to be named the starting quarterback at Southern Miss since Tommy Waters in 1991.{{cite web|url=http://www.meridianstar.com/sports/local_story_340004034.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130128195020/http://www.meridianstar.com/sports/local_story_340004034.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 28, 2013 |title=Davis earns C-USA All-Academic honors |publisher=[[The Meridian Star]] |date=December 4, 2008 |access-date=August 30, 2009 }} Davis began the season with five 200-yard passing games, more than any other Southern Miss quarterback has put together, and nine altogether for the season, tying a school record for most in a season. For the year, Davis set a new school record with 3,128 passing yards and broke [[Brett Favre]]'s school record for most touchdown passes by a freshman with 23.{{cite news|last=Fauber |first=Gary |url=http://www.register-herald.com/sports/local_story_235001346.html?keyword=secondarystory |title=Running back Fletcher a weapon for Southern Miss |newspaper=[[The Register-Herald]] |date=August 23, 2009 |access-date=August 30, 2009}} He ended the year with a combined total of 15 school records for both game and single-season marks,{{cite web |url=http://blog.al.com/press-register-sports/2009/09/southern_miss_quarterback_aust.html |last=Heim |first=Mark |title=Southern Miss quarterback Austin Davis wants to build on last season's record-setting year |website=AL.com |publisher=Alabama Media Group |date=September 2, 2009 |access-date=March 26, 2015}} which included most passing yards in a game (461) and most rushing touchdowns in a contest (5) as well as total offense for a season (3,323). Davis was ranked 16th nationally in total offense (279.7) and 52nd in [[passing efficiency]] (128.6) in the [[Football Bowl Subdivision]] (FBS). His total offense average was the highest among freshmen quarterbacks in the country, ahead of the likes of [[Kellen Moore]] of [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State]] (265.9) and [[Robert Griffin III|Robert Griffin]] of [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor]] (244.5). In the [[2008 New Orleans Bowl]], Davis threw for 276 yards and two touchdowns and became the first freshman quarterback to lead the Golden Eagles to a bowl game victory. Davis was named to the All-Conference USA freshman team and a freshman All-American honorable mention by CollegeFootballNews.com.{{cite web |url=http://southernmiss.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/120908aab.html |title=Eleven Golden Eagles Earn All-Conference USA; Five Tabbed to All-Freshman Team |publisher=University of Southern Mississippi |date=December 9, 2008 |access-date=September 4, 2009 |archive-date=September 24, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100924012701/http://southernmiss.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/120908aab.html |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://southernmiss.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121208aaa.html |title=Brown, Davis Honored by CollegeFootballNews.com as Freshman All-America Selections |publisher=University of Southern Mississippi |date=December 12, 2008 |access-date=September 4, 2009}} Before the 2009 season, Davis was named on the [[Manning Award]] watch list.{{cite web |url=http://www.allstatesugarbowl.org/site.php?pageID=19&newsID=61#.VRPXTfnF-So |title=Allstate Sugar Bowl Announces Manning Award Watch List |publisher=Allstate Sugar Bowl |date=August 17, 2009 |access-date=March 26, 2015 |archive-date=April 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402163601/http://www.allstatesugarbowl.org/site.php?pageID=19&newsID=61#.VRPXTfnF-So |url-status=dead }} Davis got off to another great start in the 2009 season{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/15187/austin-davis |title=Austin Davis Stats |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 26, 2015}} by completing 108–156 passes (69%) for 1,165 yards and 10 touchdowns against just 2 interceptions. He gained some national notoriety following a 35–28 loss to nationally ranked Kansas, in which Davis matched All-American candidate Todd Reesing yard for yard.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/boxscore?gameId=292692305 |title=Southern Miss Golden Eagles vs. Kansas Jayhawks – Box Score |website=ESPN.com |date=September 26, 2009 |access-date=March 26, 2015}} However, his promising start was cut short by a broken foot suffered in the fifth game of the season against UAB.{{cite web |url=http://www.southernmiss.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/100409aaa.html |title=Austin Davis to Miss Remainder of the Season with Foot Injury |publisher=University of Southern Mississippi |date=October 4, 2009 |access-date=March 26, 2015 |archive-date=April 3, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403024043/http://www.southernmiss.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/100409aaa.html |url-status=dead }} Davis returned in 2010 and put up another good season, throwing for 3,103 yards with 20 touchdowns against just 6 interceptions while running for another 452 yards and 10 touchdowns. On November 30, Southern Miss went on the road to face the eventual C-USA and Liberty Bowl champion Central Florida and their highly rated defense. Davis responded by completing 21–34 passes for 264 yard and 4 scores, leading the Golden Eagles to a 31–21 road upset over the ranked Knights.{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=303172116 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101117193757/http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=303172116 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 17, 2010 |title=Southern Miss Golden Eagles vs. UCF Knights – Recap |website=ESPN.com |date=November 13, 2010 |access-date=July 8, 2016}} He delivered an encore the next week in an emotional game against the Houston Cougars. Following the shooting of three teammates, Davis responded with the best game of his career, completing 24 of 31 passes for 293 yards and 2 scores while running for 111 yards and 4 more scores as Southern Miss topped Houston 59–41.{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=303242572 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130125131512/http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=303242572 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 25, 2013 |title=Houston Cougars vs. Southern Miss Golden Eagles – Recap |website=ESPN.com |date=November 20, 2010 |access-date=March 26, 2015}} In the Papajohns.com Bowl against Louisville, Davis passed Brett Favre on the schools passing touchdown record with a 32-yard pass to Quentin Pierce in the first quarter. Davis would go on to throw another touchdown as well as catch one in the 31–28 loss.{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=303550097 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130124064254/http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=303550097 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 24, 2013 |title=Southern Miss Golden Eagles vs. Louisville Cardinals – Recap |website=ESPN.com |date=December 21, 2010 |access-date=March 26, 2015}} Heading into his senior season, Davis had either broken or was on the verge of breaking nearly every passing record in Southern Miss history. He passed Favre's yardage record in the second game of the season at Marshall.{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=312530276 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130124070029/http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=312530276 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 24, 2013 |title=Southern Miss Golden Eagles vs. Marshall Thundering Herd – Recap |website=ESPN.com |date=September 10, 2011 |access-date=March 26, 2015}} Davis had arguably his best career performance on October 8, at Navy.{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=312812426 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111012155118/http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=312812426 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 12, 2011 |title=Southern Miss Golden Eagles vs. Navy Midshipmen – Recap |website=ESPN.com |date=October 8, 2011 |access-date=March 26, 2015}} He completed 21 of his 23 passes for 283 yards and 3 scores as well as running for 75 yards and another score, posting a QB rating of 237.7. Davis led the Golden Eagles to a C-USA Eastern Division championship and a spot in the conference championship game against undefeated and 6th ranked Houston and their record setting quarterback [[Case Keenum]]. Despite being a 15-point underdog and being overshadowed by Keenum prior to the game, Davis outplayed Keenum, connecting on 17 of 34 passes for 276 yards and 4 touchdowns as he led Southern Miss to one of the biggest wins in school history.{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=313370248 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111205115104/http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=313370248 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 5, 2011 |title=Southern Miss Golden Eagles vs. Houston Cougars – Recap |website=ESPN.com |date=December 3, 2011 |access-date=March 26, 2015}} Davis finished his career with a 24–17 victory in the Hawaii bowl over Nevada.{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=313582572 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111226030423/http://espn.go.com/ncf/recap?gameId=313582572 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 26, 2011 |title=Nevada Wolf Pack vs. Southern Miss Golden Eagles – Recap |website=ESPN.com |date=December 24, 2011 |access-date=March 26, 2015}} Davis' last pass as a collegiate quarterback was a touchdown in the final minutes to secure the win. Davis ended the 2011 season throwing for 3,496 yards and 30 touchdowns, both school records, while also rushing for 352 yards and four touchdowns.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/team/stats/_/id/2572/year/2011/southern-miss-golden-eagles |title=Southern Miss Golden Eagles 2011 Statistics – Team and Player Stats |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 26, 2015}} At the conclusion of his senior season he was named the winner of the [[Conerly Trophy]], an award given annually to the best college football player in the state of Mississippi by the [[Mississippi Sports Hall of Fame]]. His final stats were: 933–1527 (61.1%) for 10,898 yards, 83 touchdowns against just 27 interceptions. He also ran the ball 460 times for 1,375 yards and 25 touchdowns. He also caught 2 passes for 25 yards and a touchdown. Davis accounted for 109 touchdowns in his four-year career.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/15187/type/college/austin-davis |title=Austin Davis Stats – Southern Mississippi |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 26, 2015}} ==Professional football career== ===Pre-draft=== Davis was rated the 13th best quarterback in the [[2012 NFL draft]] by NFLDraftScout.com.{{Cite web |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=74516&DraftYear=2012 |title=Austin Davis College Football Profile |website=DraftScout.com |access-date=August 29, 2016}} Prior to the Draft, [[Bleacher Report]]'s Tyler Ward named Davis as one of his eleven potential late-round sleepers. {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 1 5/8 | weight = 219 | dash = 4.76 | ten split = 1.63 | twenty split = 2.77 | shuttle = 4.11 | cone drill = 6.73 | vertical = 31 | broad ft = 9 | broad in = 1 | arm span = 31 3/4 | hand span = 10 3/8 | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]{{Cite web |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/austin-davis/32004441-5616-4136-9bee-ea74a2e54cbf |title=Austin Davis Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |website=NFL.com |access-date=July 9, 2024}} }} ===St. Louis Rams (first stint)=== [[File:Austindavis8-16-2013.jpg|thumb|Davis with the [[St. Louis Rams]] in 2013]] Davis went undrafted in the 2012 NFL draft and signed a free agent deal with the [[St. Louis Rams]]. On August 30, 2013, he was cut by the Rams.{{cite web |url=http://www.turfshowtimes.com/2013/8/31/4680164/nfl-roster-cuts-2013-st-louis-rams-53-man-backup-greg-mcelroy |title=NFL roster cuts 2013: Rams nearing 53 players |last=Van Bibber |first=Ryan |website=Turf Show Times |publisher=Vox Media |date=August 31, 2013 |access-date=March 26, 2015}} ===Miami Dolphins=== The [[Miami Dolphins]] signed Davis to their [[practice squad]] on September 10, 2013.{{Cite web |last=Salguero |first=Armando |date=September 10, 2013 |title=The latest from Dolphins camp right here |url=http://miamiherald.typepad.com/dolphins_in_depth/2013/09/the-latest-from-dolphins-camp-right-here.html |access-date=March 26, 2015 |website=Miami Herald}}{{cite web |website=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/miami-dolphins/post/_/id/589/dolphins-practice-report-will-davis-returns|title=Dolphins practice report: Will Davis returns |date=September 10, 2013 |access-date=October 22, 2013 |first=James |last=Walker}} He was released by the team on September 17, 2013.{{cite web | url=http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/austin-davis-player-transactions | title=AUSTIN DAVIS |work=foxsports.com | access-date=September 11, 2016}} ===St Louis Rams (second stint)=== Davis re-signed with the Rams on October 22, 2013, after an injury to [[Sam Bradford]].{{cite web |website=NFL.com |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/brady-quinn-austin-davis-sign-with-st-louis-rams-0ap2000000268158 |title=Brady Quinn, Austin Davis set to join St. Louis Rams |first=Chris |last=Wesseling |date=October 22, 2013 |access-date=October 22, 2013}} In the first week of the [[2014 NFL season]] against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], Davis entered the game at the start of the second half in relief of starter [[Shaun Hill]]. A week later, due to Hill's injury, Davis made his NFL starting debut on September 14, in a winning effort against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. Following the Rams' 28–26 upset win over the defending Super Bowl champion [[Seattle Seahawks]] in Week 7, former All-Pro quarterback and legend [[Brett Favre]] tabbed Davis as a potential [[Tom Brady]] or [[Kurt Warner]] of the future, both of whom won Super Bowls despite a bleak start to their NFL careers. During the victory, Davis completed 17-of-20 passes,{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/austindavis/2533349/gamelogs?season=2014|title=Austin Davis: Game Logs at NFL.com|website=[[NFL.com]]|access-date=May 18, 2019}} the best completion percentage in NFL history against a defending Super Bowl champion; the former Southern Miss QB also added 152 passing yards and two touchdowns, one of which ultimately sealed their victory after Davis successfully led an 80-yard drive. After two interceptions and a lost fumble in the 4th quarter against the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in early November, Davis was benched in favor of Hill.{{cite web |website=ProFootballTalk.com |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/11/12/report-rams-bench-austin-davis-shaun-hill-to-start-sunday/ |title=BReport: Rams bench Austin Davis, Shaun Hill to start Sunday |first=Michael |last=Smith |date=November 12, 2014 |access-date=November 12, 2014}} On September 5, 2015, Davis was released by the Rams.{{cite web|title=Rams Reduce Roster to 53 Players|url=http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Reduce-Roster-to-53-Players/bbb8735b-9b5a-4007-ae0f-b8e4cf251956|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729140810/http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Reduce-Roster-to-53-Players/bbb8735b-9b5a-4007-ae0f-b8e4cf251956|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 29, 2017|author=Simmons, Myles|website=TheRams.com|date=September 5, 2015|access-date=April 10, 2017}} ===Cleveland Browns=== [[File:Austin Davis Browns.jpg|thumb|Davis with the [[Cleveland Browns]] in 2015]] On September 7, 2015, Davis signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]].{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cleveland-browns-sign-qb-austin-davis-0ap3000000523606|title=Cleveland Browns sign QB Austin Davis|first=Marc|last=Sessler|date=September 7, 2015|access-date=September 7, 2015}} He signed a two-year, $4.137 million contract extension on September 30.{{Cite web |date=September 30, 2015|agency=Associated Press |title=Austin Davis signs 2-year extension with Cleveland Browns |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13776281/austin-davis-signs-2-year-extension-cleveland-browns |access-date=March 16, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}} Davis played in relief of an injured [[Josh McCown]] in the Week 12 game against the [[Baltimore Ravens]]. He completed 7 of 10 passes for 77 yards, drove for a game-tying touchdown, and led the Browns into position for a game-winning field goal, but the team lost when the field goal was blocked and '''Austen Douglas Lane'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austen Lane {{!}} MMA Fighter Page |url=https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/fighters/131141-austen-lane |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=Tapology |language=en}}</ref> (born November 9, 1987) is a retired American [[mixed martial artist]] and former professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] who last competed in the [[Light heavyweight (MMA)|light heavyweight]] division of the [[Ultimate Fighting Championship]] (UFC). He was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the fifth round of the [[2010 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Murray State Racers football|Murray State Racers]]. He was also a member of the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], [[Detroit Lions]], and [[Chicago Bears]].

==Early life==
Lane grew up in [[Iola, Wisconsin]].<ref>[https://www.mmafighting.com/2018/6/12/17373018/ex-nfl-player-austen-lane-is-ready-to-make-his-name-in-a-second-sport-and-at-greg-hardys-expense Austen Lane — the other guy in the Greg Hardy fight — is no joke - MMA Fighting] Retrieved November 7, 2018.</ref>

Lane made 14.5 sacks on defense and caught 31 passes for 717 yards and 13 touchdowns on offense his senior year at Iola-Scandinavia High School. He earned All-conference and All-region honors for defense and offense and was selected All-state as a defensive end and honorable mention All-state as a wide receiver. Additionally, he had five blocked punts, 77 solo tackles, 61 assisted tackles and four fumble recoveries his senior year. He also earned two letters as a member of the Thunderbirds' basketball team and was named Second-team All-conference in 2004–05.

==College career==
Lane started 40 of 43 games at [[Murray State]] of the [[Football Championship Subdivision]]. He holds school records with 29 sacks and 55 tackles for loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=#92 Austen Lane Bio - jaguars.com |url=http://www.jaguars.com/Team/Player.aspx?id%3D2951 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100428185927/http://www.jaguars.com/Team/Player.aspx?id=2951 |archive-date=April 28, 2010 |access-date=July 14, 2010}}</ref> Following his senior year, he was named as a finalist for the [[Buck Buchanan Award]], given to the top defensive player in FCS football. He was named as a FCS first-team All-American by the Associated Press and was selected as the [[Ohio Valley Conference]] Defensive Player of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/archive/1248296 |title=NFL Draft 2020 - Latest Draft News and Predictions - CBSSports.com |access-date=August 2, 2010 |archive-date=June 14, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200614212554/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft// |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2009 Lane was second in the FCS with 11.0 sacks and third in the FCS with 19.5 tackles-for-loss after leading the OVC in sacks and TFL. He also ended the year with intercepting a pass and returning it 21 yards for a touchdown in a victory over Austin Peay. For the season in 11 games, he had 64 total tackles, 32 solo stops, 19.5 tackles for loss, 11 sacks, 1 interception for 21 yards and  1 touchdown, 3 forced fumbles, 1 fumble recovery, 8 quarterback hurries, 2 pass breakups.

The previous season he played in all 12 games and recorded 63 tackles, ranked second in the country with 22 tackles-for-loss and set MSU single-season record with 12 sacks. In 2007 Lane started 10 games at defensive end and led all defensive linemen with 48 stops, including 28 solo stops. In 2006 as a true freshman he played in 10 games, making 34 tackles, including 11 solo stops. He also had 3.5 tackles for a loss,  finished with 2.5 sacks and had one pass break-up and blocked two kicks.

Lane was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the fifth round (153rd overall) in the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was reunited with his college coach Matt Griffin, who had previously been hired by the Jaguars as an offensive assistant.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1/29 Matt Griffin raw interview following Jacksonville Jaguars hiring | WPSD Local 6 - News, Sports, Weather - Paducah KY | Web Exclusive |url=http://www.wpsdlocal6.com/sports/web-exclusive/83077907.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718121616/http://www.wpsdlocal6.com/sports/web-exclusive/83077907.html |archive-date=July 18, 2011 |access-date=April 29, 2010}}</ref> Lane was signed to a contract on July 14, 2010. The deal was for four-years and $1.974 million, including a $184,190 signing bonus.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 14, 2010 |title=Jaguars Sign Rookie Defensive End Austen Lane |work=jaguars.com |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article.aspx?id=9063 |url-status=dead |access-date=July 14, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101216094723/http://jaguars.com/news/article.aspx?id=9063 |archive-date=December 16, 2010}}</ref>

===Amateur career===
In November 2015, Lane made his amateur MMA debut, in which he defeated Micah Cross by knockout in the first round. Over the next year, Lane increased his amateur MMA record to 5 wins against no losses with all of his wins coming via knockout.

===Professional career===
Lane made his professional MMA debut in April 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Reddick |first=Jay |date=July 20, 2017 |title=Former Jaguars lineman Austen Lane making waves in MMA |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/mixed-martial-arts/os-mma-austen-lane-jaguars-combat-night-20170720-story.html |access-date=June 13, 2018}}</ref> He won his debut via knockout in the first round. Over the following year and into 2018, Lane fought three more times and improved his professional MMA record to 4 wins against no losses with again all of his wins coming via knockout.

In April 2018, it was announced that Lane would face fellow former [[National Football League|NFL]] defensive end [[Greg Hardy]] at [[Dana White's Contender Series Season 2#Week 1 - June 12|Dana White's Contender Series 9]] on June 12.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Video: Are NFL vets Austen Lane, Greg Hardy UFC-ready? Sneak peek ahead of Contender Series clash |url=https://mmajunkie.com/2018/06/video-are-nfl-vets-austen-lane-greg-hardy-ufc-ready-get-sneak-peek-ahead-of-contender-series |website=MMAJunkie.com|date=June 12, 2018 }}</ref> He lost the fight via knockout in the first round.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Greg Hardy gets UFC deal after 57-second KO in pro MMA debut |url=http://www.espn.com/mma/story/_/id/23775957/greg-hardy-gets-ufc-deal-knocking-austen-lane-win-professional-mma-debut |website=ESPN.com|date=June 13, 2018 }}</ref>

Lane returned to the regional MMA circuit to gain more experience, amassing a record of 7 wins and 2 losses over the next four years. This earned him a second shot on Dana White's Contender Series in 2022. He faced Richard Jacobi on September 20, 2022. He won the fight via TKO in the first round and was awarded a UFC contract.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dana White's Contender Series 55 results: 17-year-old Raul Rosas Jr. among five to get contracts |url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/lists/dana-white-contender-series-55-live-results-ufc-contracts |work=MMA Junkie |date=20 September 2022}}</ref>

===Ultimate Fighting Championship===
Lane was scheduled to face [[Junior Tafa]] on February 11, 2023 at [[UFC 284]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Junior Tafa firma contrato con UFC, enfrenta a Austen Lane en UFC 284 |url=https://mma.uno/junior-tafa-firma-contrato-con-ufc-enfrenta-a-austen-lane-en-ufc-284/ |website=MMA.uno, #1 En noticias de Artes Marciales Mixtas (MMA) en Español. |access-date=16 January 2023 |language=es |date=16 January 2023 |archive-date=January 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230116172501/https://mma.uno/junior-tafa-firma-contrato-con-ufc-enfrenta-a-austen-lane-en-ufc-284/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he withdrew from the bout due to undisclosed reasons.<ref name="Acosta in">{{Cite web|url=https://mma.uno/cambio-de-planes-junior-tafa-enfrentara-a-waldo-cortes-acosta-en-ufc-284/|title=Change of plans: Junior Tafa will face Waldo Cortes-Acosta at UFC 284|publisher=mma.uno|author=Steve Duncan|date=2023-01-20|access-date=2023-01-20|archive-date=January 28, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230128235252/https://mma.uno/cambio-de-planes-junior-tafa-enfrentara-a-waldo-cortes-acosta-en-ufc-284/|url-status=dead}} {{in lang|es}}</ref>

Lane faced [[Justin Tafa]] on June 24, 2023 at [[UFC on ABC 5]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dey |first=Saurav |date=2023-05-03 |title=Austen Lane vs. Justin Tafa added to UFC Jacksonville card in June |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/mma/news-austen-lane-vs-justin-tafa-added-ufc-jacksonville-card-june |access-date=2023-05-05 |website=www.sportskeeda.com |language=en-us}}</ref> Less than thirty seconds into the bout, Lane eyepoked Tafa who was unable to continue, resulting in a no contest.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bitter |first=Shawn |date=2023-06-24 |title=UFC Jacksonville: Austen Lane vs. Justin Tafa Falls Apart Early Due to Eye Poke, Ruled No Contest |url=https://cagesidepress.com/2023/06/24/ufc-jacksonville-austen-lane-vs-justin-tafa/ |access-date=2023-06-25 |website=Cageside Press |language=en-US}}</ref>  The pair had a rematch on September 10, 2023 at [[UFC 293]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=UFC Matchmaking Bulletin (7/10-7/16): Charles Jourdain Returns Against Ricardo Ramos, Three Cancellations |language=en-us |work=MMA News {{!}} UFC News, Results & Interviews |url=https://www.mmanews.com/features/ufc-matchmaking-bulletin-charles-jourdain-against-ricardo-ramos-three-cancellations |access-date=2023-08-18}}</ref> Lane lost the fight via knockout in round one.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Jay |date=2023-09-09 |title=UFC 293: Another Eye Poke, but Justin Tafa Stops Austen Lane Early in Rematch |url=https://cagesidepress.com/2023/09/09/ufc-293-justin-tafa-vs-austen-lane/ |access-date=2023-09-10 |website=Cageside Press |language=en-US}}</ref>

Lane faced [[Jhonata Diniz]] on April 27, 2024, at [[UFC on ESPN 55]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sherdog.com |title=Jhonata Diniz Set for Octagon Debut Against Austen Lane at UFC Event on April 27 |url=https://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Jhonata-Diniz-Set-for-Octagon-Debut-Against-Austen-Lane-at-UFC-Event-on-April-27-192506 |access-date=2024-02-03 |website=Sherdog |language=en}}</ref> He lost the fight by knockout in the second round.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Jay |date=2024-04-28 |title=Jhonata Diniz Completes Second-Round Comeback with KO of Austen Lane at UFC Vegas 91 |url=https://cagesidepress.com/2024/04/27/jhonata-diniz-completes-second-round-comeback-with-ko-of-austen-lane-at-ufc-vegas-91/ |access-date=2024-04-28 |website=Cageside Press |language=en-US}}</ref>

Lane faced [[Robelis Despaigne]] on October 19, 2024 at [[UFC Fight Night 245]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2024/07/ufc-news-robelis-despaigne-vs-austen-lane|title=Robelis Despaigne returns from first UFC defeat, battles Austen Lane|publisher=mmajunkie.usatoday.com|author=Nolan King|date=2024-07-29|access-date=2024-07-29}}</ref> He won the fight by unanimous decision.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2024/10/19/ufc-vegas-99-austen-lane-out-wrestles-robelis-despaigne-for-first-ufc-win/|title=UFC Vegas 99: Austen Lane Out-Wrestles Robelis Despaigne For First UFC Win|publisher=cagesidepress.com|author=Jay Anderson|date=2024-10-19|access-date=2024-10-19}}</ref>

Lane faced promotional newcomer Mário Pinto on March 1, 2025 at [[UFC Fight Night 253]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fightmag.com/ufc-vegas-103-royval-vs-kape-full-fight-card-confirmed/|title=UFC Vegas 103 card confirmed with Royval vs Kape in main event & new bouts added|publisher=fightmag.com|author=Parviz Iskenderov|date=2025-01-24|access-date=2025-01-24}}</ref> He lost the fight by knockout in the second round.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2025/03/01/mario-pinto-crushes-austen-lane-with-brutal-right-hand-to-close-ufc-vegas-103-prelims/|title=Mario Pinto Crushes Austen Lane With Brutal Right Hand to Close UFC Vegas 103 Prelims|publisher=cagesidepress.com|author=Shawn Bitter|date=2025-03-01|access-date=2025-03-01}}</ref>

Lane faced [[Vitor Petrino]] on July 12, 2025, at [[UFC on ESPN 70]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-12 |title=Vitor Petrino elevates to UFC heavyweight division, faces Austen Lane in Nashville |url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2025/04/ufc-nashville-vitor-petrino-vs-austen-lane |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=MMA Junkie |language=en-US}}</ref> He lost the fight via a rear-naked choke submission in the first round.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2025/07/12/ufc-nashville-vitor-petrino-submits-austen-lane-in-heavyweight-debut/|title=UFC Nashville: Vitor Petrino Submits Austen Lane in Heavyweight Debut|publisher=cagesidepress.com|author=Jay Anderson|date=2025-07-12|access-date=2025-07-12}}</ref>

Lane faced [[Iwo Baraniewski]] on March 21, 2026, at [[UFC Fight Night 270]], in his light heavyweight debut.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Iwo Baraniewski wraca co oktagonu ufc – w drugiej walce jego przeciwnikiem bedzie Austen Lane|url=https://www.lowking.pl/iwo-baraniewski-wraca-co-oktagonu-ufc-w-drugiej-walce-jego-przeciwnikiem-bedzie-austen-lane/|date=2026-01-11|access-date=2026-03-22|publisher=lowking.pl|author=Bartlomiej Stachura}} {{in lang|pl}}</ref> He lost the fight by knockout early in the first round.<ref>{{Cite web|title=UFC London: Iwo Baraniewski shocks Austen Lane with quick finish|url=https://cagesidepress.com/2026/03/21/ufc-london-iwo-baraniewski-shocks-austen-lane-with-quick-finish/|date=2026-03-21|access-date=2026-03-22|publisher=cagesidepress.com|author=Patrick Danna}}</ref>

On May 26, 2026, it was reported that Lane retired from MMA and was subsequently removed from the UFC roster.<ref>{{cite web |last=Martin|first=Adam|title=UFC Removes 2 More Fighters From Roster|url=https://heavy.com/sports/ufc/ufc-removes-more-fighters-from-roster/|website=Heavy|access-date=27 May 2026|date=26 May 2026}}</ref>

'''Austin Spitler''' (born October 26, 1986) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the seventh round of the [[2010 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]] as a [[starting lineup|starter]] and [[captain (sports)|captain]].

==Professional career==

===Miami Dolphins===
Spitler was selected by the [[Miami Dolphins]] in the seventh round with the 252nd overall pick of the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
Spitler signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] on June 19, 2014.<ref>{{cite news|work=BaltimoreSun.com|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2014/06/19/ravens-signing-linebacker-austin-spitler-sources-say/|title=Ravens signing linebacker Austin Spitler, sources say|date=June 19, 2014|first=Aaron|last=Wilson|access-date=July 4, 2014}}</ref> The Ravens released Spitler on August 25, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Trim-Roster-Down-To-75/393025cc-1a69-4134-95a2-c2e561131580?mobile-id=848248&media-type=N |title=Ravens Trim Roster Down To 75 |access-date=August 25, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140828173348/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Trim-Roster-Down-To-75/393025cc-1a69-4134-95a2-c2e561131580?mobile-id=848248&media-type=N |archive-date=August 28, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
Spitler signed a future deal with the [[Washington Redskins]] on January 8, 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=Redskins sign linebackers Sapp, Spitler to futures contracts|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2015/01/08/redskins-sign-linebackers-sapp-spitler-to-futures-contracts/|last=Jones|first=Mike|date=January 8, 2015|accessdate=January 8, 2015}}</ref> He was waived by the Redskins on May 4.<ref>{{cite web|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/washington-commanders/post/_/id/17202/redskins-cut-13-players-start-adding-udfas|title=Redskins cut 13 players, start adding UDFAs|first=John|last=Keim|date=May 4, 2015|access-date=May 4, 2015}}</ref>

'''Austin Howard''' (born March 22, 1987)<ref name="nfl_dob">{{cite web | url=http://www.nfl.com/player/austinhoward/2507871/profile | title=Austin Howard, OT for the Oakland Raiders at NFL.com | work=[[NFL.com]] | access-date=January 14, 2016}}</ref> is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Northern Iowa Panthers football|Northern Iowa Panthers]], and was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2010. He was also a member of the [[Baltimore Ravens]], [[New York Jets]], [[Oakland Raiders]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], and [[Washington Redskins]].

==Early life==
Howard attended [[Davenport Central High School]] in [[Davenport, Iowa]].<ref name="Added"/>

==College career==
Howard signed with [[Northern Iowa Panthers football|Northern Iowa]] in 2005 as a [[tight end]].<ref>{{cite news |author=Newhoff, Doug |title=Panthers get some insurance |url=http://wcfcourier.com/sports/local/article_5eee6fed-71d9-5f73-a138-0d8092417a10.html |work=[[The Courier (Waterloo-Cedar Falls)|The Courier]] |date=February 3, 2005 |access-date=September 2, 2010}}</ref> He was [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] during the 2005 season.

He joined the school's basketball team in December 2005 as a [[Forward (basketball)|forward]],<ref name="Added">{{cite news |title=UNI Hosts #12 Iowa, UMKC This Week |url=http://www.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stories/120605abb.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060102223555/http://www.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stories/120605abb.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 2, 2006 |work=[[CSTV]] |date=December 6, 2005 |access-date=September 2, 2010}}</ref> and on December 22, he scored four points and blocked three shots in a game against [[Hawaii Pacific University#Athletics|Hawaii Pacific]].<ref>{{cite news |author=Coss, Matt |title=Scouts study Jacobson, Stout gets blocks record in UNI win |url=http://wcfcourier.com/sports/local/article_b5080ae0-1a2b-5932-b0b5-ab2a050d4710.html |work=[[The Courier (Waterloo-Cedar Falls)|The Courier]] |date=December 23, 2005 |access-date=September 2, 2010}}</ref>

On December 1, 2007 in a game against the [[2007 Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens football team|Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens]], Howard caught a touchdown pass from Eric Sanders to bring the Panthers within five points of Delaware, but the Blue Hens ended up winning the game, 39–27.<ref>{{cite news |author=Schmidt, Kent |title=Flacco Leads Delaware In Upset of No. 1 UNI |url=http://www.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/stories/120107aci.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071204185358/http://www.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/stories/120107aci.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 4, 2007 |work=[[CSTV]] |date=December 1, 2007 |access-date=September 2, 2010}}</ref> He started in all 13 games at tight end in 2007.<ref>{{cite news |title=Newcomers to UNI offensive line face heavy burden |url=http://wcfcourier.com/sports/uni/football/article_c1e8ec65-2a31-5d67-8365-08eef6c0a4f9.html |work=[[The Courier (Waterloo-Cedar Falls)|The Courier]] |date=August 22, 2008 |access-date=September 2, 2010}}</ref> He made five receptions for 38 yards.<ref name="Iowa"/>

Howard made the switch from tight end to [[offensive tackle]] during the 2008 offseason.<ref>{{cite news |author=Sullivan, Jim |title=Farley pleased with Panthers' first week of practice |url=http://wcfcourier.com/sports/local/article_da6d6c69-ca5b-5ac8-bb34-888c45fce358.html |work=[[The Courier (Waterloo-Cedar Falls)|The Courier]] |date=August 10, 2008 |access-date=September 2, 2010}}</ref> He earned MVFC offensive lineman of the week honors following a game against [[Missouri State Bears football|Missouri State]] on November 8, 2008.<ref>{{cite news |author=Sullivan, Jim |title=Farley fusses over playoff talk |url=http://wcfcourier.com/sports/local/article_b72d7d6d-aa0b-5842-9e91-e98fe9938f9a.html |work=[[The Courier (Waterloo-Cedar Falls)|The Courier]] |date=November 11, 2008 |access-date=September 2, 2010}}</ref>

Howard earned second-team All-[[Missouri Valley Football Conference]] honors following the 2008 and 2009 seasons.<ref>{{cite news |title=UNI's Ruffin named MVFC co-defensive player of year |url=http://wcfcourier.com/sports/college/uni/article_f0720022-d9ed-11de-a214-001cc4c002e0.html |work=[[The Courier (Waterloo-Cedar Falls)|The Courier]] |date=November 25, 2009 |access-date=September 2, 2010}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia Eagles===
Howard was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] following the [[2010 NFL draft]] on April 27, 2010.<ref>{{cite news |author=McLane, Jeff |title=Eagles add 11 rookies - 3 of them big blockers |url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/20100427_Eagles_add_11_rookies_-_3_of_them_big_blockers_1.html |work=philly.com |date=April 27, 2010 |access-date=September 1, 2010}}</ref> He made the 53-man roster and played in four games, starting at left tackle in one game. Howard made his NFL debut on October 24, 2010 against the [[Tennessee Titans]].

In order to better fit into new offensive line coach [[Howard Mudd]]'s system, Howard lost about 15 pounds to get down to 330 pounds.<ref>{{cite news |author=McLane, Jeff |title=Eagles' Howard working to stay fit, working for a roster spot |url=http://articles.philly.com/2011-07-09/sports/29755560_1_eagles-coach-andy-reid-linemen-eagles-howard |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716051830/http://articles.philly.com/2011-07-09/sports/29755560_1_eagles-coach-andy-reid-linemen-eagles-howard |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 16, 2011 |work=philly.com |date=July 9, 2011 |access-date=July 10, 2011}}</ref> However, he was waived during final roster cuts on September 3, 2011.

===Baltimore Ravens (first stint)===
Howard was signed to the [[Baltimore Ravens]]' [[practice squad]] on September 6, 2011.

===New York Jets===
The [[New York Jets]] signed Howard to their active roster off the Ravens' practice squad on November 25, 2011.<ref>{{cite web |title=T Howard Signed to Practice Squad |url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-1/T-Howard-Signed-to-Practice-Squad/e8198656-bdee-480a-b2d1-856f9aab989e |publisher=New York Jets |author=Jets Media Relations Department |date=November 25, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111129023247/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-1/T-Howard-Signed-to-Practice-Squad/e8198656-bdee-480a-b2d1-856f9aab989e |archive-date=November 29, 2011 |access-date=November 27, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On August 23, 2012, head coach [[Rex Ryan]] made the decision to bench [[Wayne Hunter]], giving the starting Right Tackle job to Howard.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Right Tackle Wayne Hunter Benched; Austin Howard To Replace Him As Starter|url=http://newyork.cbslocal.com/2012/08/23/jets-right-tackle-wayne-hunter-benched-austin-howard-to-replace-him-as-starter/|publisher=CBS News New York|access-date=August 24, 2012}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders===
Howard signed a five-year, $30 million contract with the [[Oakland Raiders]] on March 12, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Howard, Oakland Raiders strike five-year deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/austin-howard-oakland-raiders-strike-five-year-deal-0ap2000000333263 |author=Wesseling, Chris |date=March 12, 2014 |publisher=National Football League |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312212904/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000333263/article/austin-howard-oakland-raiders-strike-fiveyear-deal |archive-date=March 12, 2014 |access-date=March 12, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 7, 2014, Howard made his first career start at [[Guard (American and Canadian football)|right guard]], as well as his [[Oakland Raiders]] debut against the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Jets-Raiders: 9 Things to Know|url = http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-randylangefb/Jets-Raiders-9-Things-to-Know/a0e9e131-ab79-4ea9-baba-0ade89bb6803|website = www.newyorkjets.com|access-date = December 20, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151222085353/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-randylangefb/Jets-Raiders-9-Things-to-Know/a0e9e131-ab79-4ea9-baba-0ade89bb6803|archive-date = December 22, 2015|url-status = dead}}</ref>

==== 2014 season ====
On September 14, 2014, against the [[Houston Texans]], Howard (started at right guard) and his offense gained 364 total yards, and the offensive line did not allow a sack for the first time that season.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Texans vs. Raiders - Team Statistics - September 14, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/matchup?gameId=400554284|website = ESPN.com|access-date = December 20, 2015}}</ref> On September 21, 2014, against the [[New England Patriots]], Howard and his offensive line prevented a sack for the second straight game.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Raiders vs. Patriots - Box Score - September 21, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=400554250|website = ESPN.com|access-date = December 20, 2015}}</ref> On October 12, 2014, against the [[San Diego Chargers]], Howard and his offense gained a season high 396 total yards and the offensive line did not allow a sack for the third time that season.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Chargers vs. Raiders - Team Statistics - October 12, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/matchup?gameId=400554302|website = ESPN.com|access-date = December 20, 2015}}</ref> On October 26, 2014, against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Howard and his offense gained 387 yards, which included quarterback [[Derek Carr (American football)|Derek Carr]]'s first career 300+ yards passing game.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Raiders vs. Browns - Team Statistics - October 26, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/matchup?gameId=400554306|website = ESPN.com|access-date = December 20, 2015}}</ref> On November 9, 2014, against the [[Denver Broncos]], Howard and his offensive line that allowed zero sacks for the fourth time in the 2014 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Broncos vs. Raiders - Box Score - November 9, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=400554396|website = ESPN.com|access-date = December 20, 2015}}</ref> On November 20, 2014, against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], Howard and his offense paved the way for a season high 179 rushing yards, which included running back [[Latavius Murray]]'s first career 100+ yards rushing game.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Chiefs vs. Raiders - Team Statistics - November 20, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/matchup?gameId=400554293|website = ESPN.com|access-date = December 20, 2015}}</ref> On December 7, 2014, against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], Howard and his offense gained 330 total yards, which included quarterback [[Derek Carr (American football)|Derek Carr]] posting a season-high quarterback rating of 140.2.<ref>{{Cite web|title = 49ers vs. Raiders - Game Recap - December 7, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=400554431|website = ESPN.com|access-date = December 20, 2015}}</ref>

==== 2015 season ====
On October 11, 2015, in a game against the Denver Broncos, Howard attempted a chop block on Denver Broncos' linebacker Von Miller but missed, allowing Miller to sack Raiders quarterback Derek Carr, forcing Carr to fumble and changing the momentum of a game that ultimately ended in a Raiders loss. On December 19, 2015, Howard was placed on injured reserve with a knee injury, after starting 13 games with the Raiders at right tackle.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Austin Howard placed on season ending injured reserve, Tevin McDonald activated|url = http://www.silverandblackpride.com/2015/12/19/10627578/austin-howard-placed-on-season-ending-injured-reserve-tevin-mcdonald|website = SilverAndBlackPride.com| date=December 19, 2015 |access-date = December 20, 2015}}</ref>

==== 2016 season ====
Howard played in 11 games with 10 starts with the Raiders at right tackle, having dealing with an ankle injury that caused him to miss five games.

On July 28, 2017, Howard was released by the Raiders.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders Sign Andrew East; Release Austin Howard, Taiwan Jones|url=http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-Andrew-East-Release-Austin-Howard-Taiwan-Jones/46c86d8f-4cbe-4539-a1df-100c2d40371d|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171231203723/http://www.raiders.com/news/article-1/Raiders-Sign-Andrew-East-Release-Austin-Howard-Taiwan-Jones/46c86d8f-4cbe-4539-a1df-100c2d40371d|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 31, 2017|website=Raiders.com|date=July 28, 2017}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens (second stint)===
On August 4, 2017, Howard signed a three-year, $16 million contract with the Ravens after significant injuries to the team's offensive line during training camp.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens sign OT Austin Howard to three-year deal|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000825724/article/ravens-signing-austin-howard-to-threeyear-deal|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805062549/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000825724/article/ravens-signing-austin-howard-to-threeyear-deal|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 5, 2017|author=Shook, Nick|website=NFL.com|date=August 4, 2017}}</ref> He started all 16 games at right tackle for the Ravens in 2017.

On March 13, 2018, the Ravens declined the option on Howard's contract, making him a free agent.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Ravens will not pick up OT Austin Howard's option|url=https://www.baltimorebeatdown.com/2018/3/13/17113886/report-ravens-will-not-pick-up-ot-austin-howards-option|website=BaltimoreBeatdown.com|date=March 13, 2018|access-date=March 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313202232/https://www.baltimorebeatdown.com/2018/3/13/17113886/report-ravens-will-not-pick-up-ot-austin-howards-option|archive-date=March 13, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On May 9, 2018, Howard signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Sign Veteran Tackle Austin Howard|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-veteran-tackle-austin-howard-20641128|website=Colts.com|date=May 9, 2018}}</ref> He was released on September 1, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Announce Final 2018 Roster Cuts|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-announce-final-2018-roster-cuts|author=Walker, Andrew|website=Colts.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
Howard was signed by the [[Washington Redskins]] on November 5, 2018, following season ending injuries to starting offensive linemen [[Brandon Scherff]], and [[Shawn Lauvao]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/roundup-scherff-lauvao-richardson-out-for-year-0ap3000000984880|title=Roundup: Scherff, Lauvao, Richardson out for year|last=Shook|first=Nick|date=November 5, 2018|work=NFL.com}}</ref> He played in five games, starting one at right guard, before being placed on injured reserve with a hip injury on December 21.<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Sign Timon Parris To The Active Roster, Place Austin Howard On Injured Reserve|url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-sign-timon-parris-to-the-active-roster-place-austin-howard-on-ir|website=Redskins.com|date=December 21, 2018}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Howard has two brothers, Marcel and Aaron, who both played college football for the [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State Cyclones]], and two sisters Amy and Ashley.<ref name="Iowa">{{cite news |author=Doxsie, Don |title=UNI lineman hopes family's mark vs. Iowa remains perfect He also has two older sisters,, Amy Howard and Ashley Howard. Both of his sisters reside in Thornton, Colorado. |url=http://wcfcourier.com/news/breaking_news/article_a1b7e25e-8849-5e87-bfdc-2cca526caeba.html |work=[[The Courier (Waterloo-Cedar Falls)|The Courier]] |date=September 3, 2009 |access-date=September 2, 2010}}</ref>
