'''Austin Pettis''' (born February 8, 1989<ref>{{cite web|last=Pettis|first=Austin|title=Proof!!! 2/8/89 but thanks for all the luv lol|url=https://twitter.com/Austin_Pettis/status/331468219267293185|publisher=Twitter|access-date=May 6, 2013}}</ref>) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] for the [[St. Louis Rams]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State Broncos]] and was selected by the Rams in the third round of the [[2011 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Pettis attended [[Lutheran High School of Orange County|Orange Lutheran High School]] in [[Orange, California]]. He was part of the [[high school football|football]] team and had 72 receptions for 1,079 yards and 13 [[touchdowns]] as a senior. He was named First-team All-league and All-county and Third-team All-state  and was also named to the All-Southern Section Team while helping team to state championship. As a sophomore, he was named Second-team All-league as well as being named top sophomore on team.  He lettered in football three times, basketball three times, and track and field twice.

==College career==
Pettis finished his Boise State career as the school's all-time leader in both receptions (229) and touchdown catches (39). His 2,838 receiving yards rank second on the all-time list. He was a four-year starter in the Broncos' high-powered offense.  Pettis set career highs with 71 receptions and 951 yards and 10 touchdowns as a senior and earned First-team All-Western Athletic Conference honors for the second consecutive year.

As a junior, in 2009, Pettis had 63 receptions for 855 yards and 14 touchdowns and was a First-team All-[[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] selection. Pettis was named Second-team All-WAC after his sophomore season (2007), catching 49 passes for 567 yards, averaging 11.6 yards per catch and nine touchdowns. He was also named to the All-WAC academic team. In 2007 as a true freshmen, he finished season second on team with 46 receptions and finished second on team with six touchdown receptions and third with 465 yards receiving.

Pettis also finished sixth in the 60-yard shuttle (11.14 seconds) and 11th in the 3-cone drill (6.68 seconds).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://voices.idahostatesman.com/2011/02/27/ccripe/former_boise_state_wr_austin_pettis_sets_record_shuttle_run |title=Austin Pettis |date=February 27, 2011 |access-date=April 28, 2011 |publisher=Idaho Statesmen.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715203154/http://voices.idahostatesman.com/2011/02/27/ccripe/former_boise_state_wr_austin_pettis_sets_record_shuttle_run |archive-date=July 15, 2012 }}</ref>

Pettis was drafted in the third round with the 78th overall pick in the [[2011 NFL draft]] by the [[St. Louis Rams]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=February 26, 2019}}</ref> On July 29, 2011, Pettis signed a four-year contract with the Rams that included a $614,000 signing bonus. In a week 7 loss against the [[Green Bay Packers]] in 2012, Pettis caught his first NFL touchdown pass, a 3-yard reception. He was waived on October 20, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|last1=David Smith|first1=Michael|title=Rams waive Austin Pettis|date=October 20, 2014 |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/10/20/rams-waive-austin-pettis/|publisher=Pro Football Talk|access-date=October 20, 2014}}</ref>

Pettis was signed by the [[San Diego Chargers]] on January 9, 2015.<ref name="u596">{{cite web | last=Williams | first=Eric D. | title=Chargers sign receiver Austin Pettis | website=ESPN.com | date=2015-01-09 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles-chargers/post/_/id/9397/chargers-sign-wr-austin-pettis | access-date=2025-01-01}}</ref> He was released by the team on September 5, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Byrne |first=Connor J. |date=September 4, 2015 |title=Chargers Release Austin Pettis |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2015/09/chargers-release-austin-pettis |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Austin William Pasztor''' (born November 26, 1990) is a Canadian former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[Tackle (American and Canadian football)|offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers football|Virginia Cavaliers]] and was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] as an undrafted free agent in 2012.

==Early life==
Pasztor attended [[Glendale High School (Tillsonburg)|Glendale High School]] before transferring to [[Fork Union Military Academy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dertinger |first=Jeff |date=December 17, 2012 |title=Austin Pasztor plays first NFL game |url=http://www.delhinewsrecord.com/2012/12/17/austin-pasztor-plays-first-nfl-game |access-date=March 13, 2018 |website=Delhi News Record |language=en-CA}}</ref>

== College career ==
Pasztor finished his college eligibility with the [[Virginia Cavaliers]].<ref name="b071">{{cite web | title=Austin Pasztor: Enjoying The Ride | website=Virginia Cavaliers Athletics| date=2011-09-26 | url=https://virginiasports.com/news/2011/09/26/austin-pasztor-enjoying-the-ride/ | access-date=2024-09-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/austin-pasztor-1.html |title=Austin Pasztor College Stats |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref> He was selected fourth overall by the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] in the [[2012 CFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cfl.ca/draft-tracker/2012/ |title=2012 CFL Draft |website=CFL.ca |language=en-US |access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref> He was ranked as the fourth best player in the [[Canadian Football League]]'s Amateur Scouting Bureau final rankings for players eligible in the 2012 CFL draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CFL Scouting Bureau - April 2012 |url=http://www.cfl.ca/cfl-scouting-bureau-april-2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425090023/http://www.cfl.ca/cfl-scouting-bureau-april-2012 |archive-date=2012-04-25 |access-date=2024-09-17 |website=CFL.ca}}</ref>

== Professional career ==

=== Minnesota Vikings ===
On April 29, 2012, Pasztor signed with the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref name="j449">{{cite web | last=Garda | first=Andrew | title=Tracking Minnesota Vikings' 2012 NFL Undrafted Free Agent Signings | website=Bleacher Report | date=2012-04-30 | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1167238-tracking-minnesota-vikings-2012-nfl-undrafted-free-agent-signings | access-date=2024-09-17}}</ref> On August 31, 2012, as the Vikings reduced their roster down to league maximum of 53 players, he was released.<ref name="m693">{{cite web | last=Craig | first=Mark | title=Chris Carr, Sage Rosenfels surprises among Vikings' final cuts | website=Star Tribune | date=2012-09-01 | url=https://www.startribune.com/chris-carr-sage-rosenfels-surprises-among-vikings-final-cuts/168227606 | access-date=2024-09-17}}</ref>

=== Jacksonville Jaguars ===
Pasztor was signed to the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] practice squad on September 17, 2012. He was promoted to the active roster on December 14. He started three games for the Jaguars in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PaszAu00/gamelog/2012/ |title=Austin Pasztor 2012 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref>

On October 2, 2013, the Jaguars announced that they had traded starting left tackle [[Eugene Monroe]] to the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 1, 2013 |title=Jaguars trade Eugene Monroe to Ravens for draft picks |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jaguars-trade-eugene-monroe-to-ravens-for-draft-picks-0ap2000000254395 |access-date=March 13, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Monroe's left tackle position was filled by [[Luke Joeckel]], paving the way for Pasztor to become the team's starting right tackle despite the fact he had been primarily used at guard in the past. Overall, in the 2013 season, he appeared in 15 games and started 13.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PaszAu00/gamelog/2013/ |title=Austin Pasztor 2013 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref> In the 2014 season, he appeared in and started eight games.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PaszAu00/gamelog/2014/ |title=Austin Pasztor 2014 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref>

He was released by the Jaguars on September 5, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Marks-to-active-roster-as-Jaguars-move-to-53/702f793f-8ae8-4cce-8109-cb0627d3f620|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107030330/https://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Marks-to-active-roster-as-Jaguars-move-to-53/702f793f-8ae8-4cce-8109-cb0627d3f620|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 7, 2017|title=Marks to active roster as Jaguars move to 53|author=Oehser, John|website=Jaguars.com|date=September 5, 2015}}</ref>

=== Cleveland Browns ===
Pasztor was claimed off waivers by the [[Cleveland Browns]] on September 6, 2015.<ref name="j291">{{cite web | last=Pokorny | first=Chris | title=Browns Claim OT Austin Pasztor from Jaguars | website=Dawgs By Nature | date=2015-09-06 | url=https://www.dawgsbynature.com/2015/9/6/9269539/browns-claim-ot-austin-pasztor-from-jaguars | access-date=2024-10-11}}</ref> On March 22, 2016, Pasztor was offered a one-year tender. He signed his tender on April 4.<ref>{{cite web|work=ClevelandBrowns.com|url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-5/Browns-sign-restricted-free-agents-and-exclusive-rights-players/25b7656a-a143-4555-a005-89b7fc6bde37|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107004416/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-5/Browns-sign-restricted-free-agents-and-exclusive-rights-players/25b7656a-a143-4555-a005-89b7fc6bde37|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 7, 2017|title=Browns sign restricted free agents and exclusive rights players|date=April 4, 2016|access-date=April 10, 2016}}</ref> Overall, in the 2015 season, he appeared in all 16 games and started four.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PaszAu00/gamelog/2015/ |title=Austin Pasztor 2015 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref> In the 2016 season, he appeared in and started all 16 games.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PaszAu00/gamelog/2016/ |title=Austin Pasztor 2016 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref>

=== Atlanta Falcons ===
On August 19, 2017, Pasztor signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons Sign Former Cleveland Browns Tackle Austin Pasztor, Waive OL Marquis Lucas|url=http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/Falcons-sign-former-Cleveland-Browns-tackle-Austin-Pasztor-waive-OL-Marquis-Lucas/735e679c-ce60-403a-b56b-96cddc87587d|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229004533/http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/Falcons-sign-former-Cleveland-Browns-tackle-Austin-Pasztor-waive-OL-Marquis-Lucas/735e679c-ce60-403a-b56b-96cddc87587d|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 29, 2017|author=McFadden, Will|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=August 19, 2017}}</ref> In the 2017 season, he appeared in seven games.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PaszAu00/gamelog/2017/ |title=Austin Pasztor 2017 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref>

On March 13, 2018, Pasztor signed a one-year contract extension with the Falcons.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons sign Leon McFadden and Austin Pasztor to one-year extensions|url=http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/transactions/article-1/Falcons-sign-Leon-McFadden-and-Austin-Pasztor-to-one-year-extensions/f61d72c9-c833-447e-a4b4-95bc3aa6869b|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180315022939/http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/transactions/article-1/Falcons-sign-Leon-McFadden-and-Austin-Pasztor-to-one-year-extensions/f61d72c9-c833-447e-a4b4-95bc3aa6869b|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 15, 2018|author=McFadden, Will|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=March 13, 2018}}</ref> He was released on August 31, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McFadden |first=Will |date=August 31, 2018 |title=Falcons waive Ron Parker, Austin Pasztor; agree to injury settlement with Leon McFadden |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-waive-ron-parker-austin-pasztor-agree-to-injury-settlement-with-leon-mcf |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref> He was re-signed on October 24, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McFadden |first=Will |date=October 24, 2018 |title=Falcons place Brandon Fusco on IR, sign two offensive linemen |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-place-brandon-fusco-on-ir-sign-two-offensive-linemen |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref> He was released again on November 8, 2018.<ref name="m064">{{cite web | last=Chambers | first=Matthew | title=Falcons waive Austin Pasztor to make room for Bruce Irvin | website=The Falcoholic | date=2018-11-08 | url=https://www.thefalcoholic.com/2018/11/8/18076010/falcons-waive-austin-pasztor-to-make-room-for-bruce-irvin | access-date=2024-09-17}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On December 11, 2018, Pasztor was signed by the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=December 11, 2018 |title=Titans Place TE Jonnu Smith, RT Jack Conklin on Injured Reserve; Team Adds TE Wick, OL Pasztor to 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-place-te-jonnu-smith-rt-jack-conklin-on-injured-reserve-team-adds-te-wick |access-date=2024-09-17 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref> He was released on August 31, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Roster Moves: Titans Trim Roster to 53 Players While Also Trading WR Taywan Taylor to Browns |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/roster-moves-titans-trim-roster-to-53-players-while-also-trading-wr-taywan-taylo |access-date=2024-09-17 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
During the 2018 and 2019 offseasons, Pasztor hosted Pasztor's Principles Football Camp and Combine, a free skills camp for students from seventh grade to high school in Brantford, Ontario. Every offseason since 2017, Pasztor has been working toward earning his master's degree in business.<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Pasztor|url=https://www.titansonline.com/team/players-roster/austin-pasztor/|author=Wyatt, Jim|date=August 2, 2019|website=TitansOnline.com|access-date=August 2, 2019}}</ref>

'''Austin Edward Seferian-Jenkins''' (born September 29, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the second round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Washington Huskies football|Washington Huskies]]. He also played for the [[New York Jets]] and [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].

== Early life ==
Seferian-Jenkins attended [[Gig Harbor High School]] in [[Gig Harbor, Washington]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelley |first=Mason |date=August 16, 2010 |title=Gig Harbor tight end Austin Seferian-Jenkins chooses Washington |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/gig-harbor-tight-end-austin-seferian-jenkins-chooses-washington/ |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=The Seattle Times |language=en-US}}</ref> He played [[high school football|football]] for the Gig Harbor High School Tides.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelley |first=Mason |date=September 1, 2010 |title=Washington recruit Austin Seferian-Jenkins is part of talented senior class |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/washington-recruit-austin-seferian-jenkins-is-part-of-talented-senior-class/ |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=The Seattle Times |language=en-US}}</ref> He had 126 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] during his career and played in the 2011 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]]. His mother is of [[Armenians|Armenian]] descent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins strives to seize day after reckless night |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/austin-seferian-jenkins-strives-to-seize-day-after-reckless-nig-0ap2000000346786 |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Brummer |first=David |date=2018-02-28 |title=Reflections from the field – NFL stars visit Israel |url=https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/reflections-from-the-field-nfl-stars-visit-israel-543851 |access-date=2026-03-01 |website=The Jerusalem Post}}</ref>

Regarded as a four-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Seferian-Jenkins was ranked as the second-ranked [[tight end]] prospect in his class, behind [[Nick O'Leary]] and ahead of [[Jace Amaro]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins, 2011 Tight End |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/austin-seferian-jenkins-18546?view=pv |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He chose his home-state school, The [[University of Washington]], over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami (FL)]], [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]], [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma]], [[USC Trojans football|Southern California]], and [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]] because Washington was the only big school to offer him the opportunity to play both [[basketball]] and football.

==College career==
As a [[true freshman]] in the 2011 season, Seferian-Jenkins started 10 of 13 games and had 41 receptions for 538 yards and six [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/austin-seferian-jenkins-1/gamelog/2011 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In addition to football, he played basketball as a freshman.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Percy |date=January 9, 2012 |title=Washington tight end Austin Seferian-Jenkins will play basketball |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/washington-tight-end-austin-seferian-jenkins-will-play-basketball/ |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=The Seattle Times |language=en-US}}</ref> In his sophomore season, he recorded 69 receptions for 852 yards and seven touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/austin-seferian-jenkins-1/gamelog/2012 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished third in the [[John Mackey Award|Mackey Award]] voting.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2012 |title=ND's Eifert wins Mackey Award over Seferian-Jenkins, Ertz ===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
====2014 season====
Seferian-Jenkins was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the second round with the 38th overall pick in the 2014 NFL draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In his rookie season, Sefarian-Jenkins played in nine games making 21 catches for 221 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SefeAu00/gamelog/2014 |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> On October 26, he caught his first career touchdown, which was a seven-yard pass from [[Mike Glennon]], against the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - October 26th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201410260tam.htm |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> He caught his second and last touchdown of the season, a one-yard pass from [[Josh McCown]], against the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - November 9th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411090tam.htm |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> His season was cut short by an injury, landing him on the team's [[injured reserve]] list.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mello |first=Igor |date=December 15, 2014 |title=Bucs place Austin Seferian-Jenkins, Louis Murphy on IR |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/bucs-place-austin-seferian-jenkins-louis-murphy-on-ir/ |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>

====2015 season====
In the 2015 season, with rookie quarterback and first overall pick [[Jameis Winston]], Seferian-Jenkins looked to expand on his rookie season. He had a career day in a season opening loss to the [[Tennessee Titans]]. He had five receptions for 110 yards and two touchdowns, which were a five-yard reception in the second quarter and a 41-yard reception in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - September 13th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201509130tam.htm |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> Both of Seferian-Jenkins's touchdowns were the first touchdown passes of Winston's NFL career. Seferian-Jenkins's remainder of his 2015 season would not have the success he had in the season opener. He only scored two more touchdowns on the season, which were a nine-yard reception from Winston against the [[St. Louis Rams]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at St. Louis Rams - December 17th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512170ram.htm |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> and a 43-yard reception from Winston against the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - December 27th, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512270tam.htm |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> He played in seven games with 338 receiving yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SefeAu00/gamelog/2015 |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref>

====2016 season====
Seferian-Jenkins played in the season opener against the Falcons at the [[Georgia Dome]]. He had one reception for 30 yards and a touchdown,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Atlanta Falcons - September 11th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110atl.htm |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> which would be his only one of the 2016 season. He played one more game with the Buccaneers on September 18, which was against the [[Arizona Cardinals]] at the [[University of Phoenix Stadium]]. He had two receptions for 14 yards in the 40–7 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Arizona Cardinals - September 18th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609180crd.htm |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> On September 23, 2016, Seferian-Jenkins was arrested on a DUI charge and was released by the Buccaneers later that day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Orr |first=Conor |date=September 23, 2016 |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins arrested on DUI charge |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/austin-seferian-jenkins-arrested-on-dui-charge-0ap3000000708050 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 23, 2016 |title=Buccaneers Waive TE Austin Seferian-Jenkins |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/buccaneers-waive-te-austin-seferian-jenkins-17748792 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>

===New York Jets===

====2016 season====
On September 26, 2016, Seferian-Jenkins was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Eric |date=September 26, 2016 |title=Jets Claim TE Austin Seferian-Jenkins |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-claim-te-austin-seferian-jenkins-17769825 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

Seferian-Jenkins recorded 10 total receptions for 110 yards in seven games with the Jets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SefeAu00/gamelog/2016 |access-date=July 29, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref>

====2017 season====
On March 15, 2017, Seferian-Jenkins was suspended the first two weeks of the 2017 season for violating the NFL Policy and Program for Substances of Abuse.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=March 15, 2017 |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins suspended two games by NFL |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/austin-seferian-jenkins-suspended-two-games-by-nfl-0ap3000000793306 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

During Week 6 against the [[New England Patriots]], Seferian-Jenkins was thought to have fumbled inches from the [[endzone]], resulting in a touchback. The call was controversial, since he retained possession going to the ground and only momentarily appeared to shift the ball as he crossed the [[Goal line (gridiron football)|goal line]], but ultimately the error loomed large, as the Jets lost the game 17–24.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Slater |first=Darryl |date=October 16, 2017 |title=Ref says overturning Jets' TD vs. Pats was 'obvious' |url=https://www.nj.com/jets/2017/10/here_is_referees_explanation_for_controversial_aus.html |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=NJ.com |language=en}}</ref> He played in 13 games, of which he started ten, in the 2017 season. He finished with 50 receptions for 357 receiving yards and three receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SefeAu00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On March 15, 2018, Seferian-Jenkins signed a two-year, $10 million contract with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=March 15, 2018 |title=Jaguars sign ex-Jets TE Austin Seferian-Jenkins |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jaguars-sign-ex-jets-te-austin-seferian-jenkins-0ap3000000921554 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=March 15, 2018 |title=OFFICIAL: Seferian-Jenkins signs |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-seferian-jenkins-signs-20457749 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on October 9, 2018, after aggravating a core muscle injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiRocco |first=Michael |date=October 9, 2018 |title=Jags to put Corey Grant, Austin Seferian-Jenkins on IR |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/24931906/jacksonville-jaguars-put-corey-grant-austin-seferian-jenkins-ir |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 9, 2018 |title=Jaguars sign running backs Jamaal Charles and Dave Williams, promote tight end David Grinnage to active roster |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-sign-running-backs-jamaal-charles-and-dave-williams-promote-tight-end-da |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He played in five games in the 2018 season. He recorded 11 receptions for 90 receiving yards and one touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SefeAu00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On February 18, 2019, the Jaguars declined the option on Seferian-Jenkins' contract, making him a free agent at the start of the new league year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=February 18, 2019 |title=Jaguars decline option for Austin Seferian-Jenkins |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/02/18/jaguars-decline-option-for-austin-seferian-jenkins/ |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=ProFootballTalk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On April 10, 2019, Seferian-Jenkins signed a one-year contract with the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=April 10, 2019 |title=Patriots sign TE Austin Seferian-Jenkins to 1-year deal |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001025923/article/patriots-sign-te-austin-seferianjenkins-to-1year-deal |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410184033/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001025923/article/patriots-sign-te-austin-seferianjenkins-to-1year-deal |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 10, 2019 |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was released on June 4, 2019, citing personal issues.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 6, 2019 |title=Patriots Release Tight End Austin Seferian-Jenkins |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-release-tight-end-austin-seferian-jenkins |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=Patriots.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On March 9, 2013, Seferian-Jenkins was cited for driving under the influence in the [[University District, Seattle|University District]] of [[Seattle, Washington|Seattle]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carter |first=Mike |date=March 10, 2013 |title=UW football tight-end Seferian-Jenkins arrested for DUI | The Today File | Seattle Times |url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/today/2013/03/uw-football-tight-end-seferian-jenkinsa-arrested-for-dui/ |access-date=August 30, 2016 |website=Seattle Times}}</ref> In July 2013, he pleaded guilty to DUI and served a day in jail.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jude |first=Adam |date=July 25, 2013 |title=Report: UW's Seferian-Jenkins has served his day in jail | Husky Football Blog | Seattle Times |url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskyfootball/2013/07/25/report-uws-seferian-jenkins-has-served-his-day-in-jail/ |access-date=August 30, 2016 |website=Seattle Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Watson |first=Graham |date=March 10, 2013 |title=Washington star tight end Austin Seferian-Jenkins arrested for DUI |url=http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaaf-dr-saturday/washington-star-tight-end-austin-seferian-jenkins-arrested-183313343--ncaaf.html |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=Yahoo! Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> The football team suspended Seferian-Jenkins for one game, the [[2013 Washington Huskies football team|Huskies' 2013 season]] opener against [[2013 Boise State Broncos football team|Boise State]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Axson |first=Scooby |date=August 30, 2013 |title=Report: Washington TE Austin Seferian-Jenkins suspended for Boise State game |url=https://www.si.com/si-wire/2013/08/30/washington-austin-seferian-jenkins-suspended-one-game |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=Sports Illustrated}}</ref>

In addition, Seferian-Jenkins was cited for DUI on the morning of Friday, September 23, 2016. He was released by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on the same day of the incident.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bonesteel |first=Matt |date=September 23, 2016 |title=Buccaneers cut tight end Austin Seferian-Jenkins after second DUI |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/early-lead/wp/2016/09/23/bucs-te-austin-seferian-jenkins-gets-another-dui/ |access-date=February 13, 2023 |newspaper=Washington Post |language=en-US}}</ref>

In May 2017, Seferian-Jenkins opened up regarding his struggles with alcohol, and indicated that he had sought help by attending rehab on an outpatient basis.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cimini |first=Rich |date=May 30, 2017 |title=Jets' Austin Seferian-Jenkins sought help for drinking problem |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/19499429/new-york-jets-te-austin-seferian-jenkins-admits-seeking-help-drinking-problem |access-date=January 22, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Seferian-Jenkins was arrested for DUI for a third time on March 9, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=March 16, 2020 |title=Austin Seferian-Jenkins arrested again |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/16/austin-seferian-jenkins-arrested-again/ |access-date=May 3, 2020 |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref>

On January 31, 2022, Seferian-Jenkins was arrested for fourth-degree assault, felony harassment and interfering with the reporting of domestic violence.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Glenn |first=Stacia |date=January 31, 2021 |title=Former NFL player charged in Pierce County with beating ex-girlfriend, making threats |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/news/local/crime/article257899398.html |access-date=February 13, 2023 |website=The News Tribune}}</ref>

'''Austin Johnson''' (born June 16, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Fullback (American football)|fullback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]].

==Early life==
Johnson played football and baseball at [[Hickory High School (North Carolina)|Hickory High School]] in [[Hickory, North Carolina]]. He was an all-state selection for football in 2006 and 2007.<ref name="C">{{Cite web |title=Austin Johnson |url=http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/johnson_austin00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161024194233/http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/johnson_austin00.html |archive-date=October 24, 2016 |access-date=September 8, 2014 |website=University of Tennessee Athletics}}</ref> He recorded 692 rushing yards and 18 rushing touchdowns on 108 attempts his senior year. Johnson also recorded 35 receptions and 470 receiving yards.<ref name="C" /> He finished his high school career with 580 tackles.<ref name="B">{{Cite web |title=Austin Johnson |url=http://www.neworleanssaints.com/team/roster/austin-johnson/d3b4c85b-85fd-45a1-99e7-ba7dfa728b7a |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140908225148/http://www.neworleanssaints.com/team/roster/austin-johnson/d3b4c85b-85fd-45a1-99e7-ba7dfa728b7a |archive-date=September 8, 2014 |access-date=September 8, 2014 |website=New Orleans Saints}}</ref>

==College career==
Johnson played for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]] from 2008 to 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Johnson - Football |url=https://utsports.com/sports/football/roster/austin-johnson/1570 |access-date=March 8, 2024 |website=University of Tennessee Athletics |language=en}}</ref> He was an Academic All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] selection in 2008, 2009, and 2010.<ref name="C" />

([[Richland, New Jersey]]) | college = [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]] (2012–2015) | draftyear = 2016 | draftround = 2 | draftpick = 43 | pastteams = * [[Tennessee Titans]] ({{NFL Year|2016|2019}}) * [[New York Giants]] ({{NFL Year|2020|2021}}) * [[Los Angeles Chargers]] ({{NFL Year|2022|2023}}) * [[Buffalo Bills]] ({{NFL Year|2024}}) * [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] ({{NFL Year|2025}}) | status = | highlights = * Second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten]] ([[2015 All-Big Ten Conference football team|2015]]) | statweek = 18 | statseason = 2025 | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Total tackles]] | statvalue1 = 272 | statlabel2 = [[Quarterback sack|Sacks]] | statvalue2 = 9.5 | statlabel3 = [[Fumble|Forced fumbles]] | statvalue3 = 3 | statlabel4 = [[Fumble|Fumble recoveries]] | statvalue4 = 2 | statlabel5 = [[Pass deflections]] | statvalue5 = 13 | pfr = JohnAu01 }} '''Austin Hunter Johnson''' (born May 8, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive tackle]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]], and was drafted by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the second round of the [[2016 NFL draft]]. Johnson has also played for the [[New York Giants]], [[Los Angeles Chargers]], and [[Buffalo Bills]]. ==Early life== Johnson was born in [[Galloway Township, New Jersey]] to parents Austin and Tammy Johnson, the third of four children – he has two older sisters and one younger sister. Johnson attended [[St. Augustine Preparatory School]] in [[Richland, New Jersey]] with plans to play basketball in hopes of someday playing in college. He played basketball and earned all-state accolades as a senior. However, the football coach convinced Johnson to try out for the football team, and he did. Subsequently, Johnson was recruited by Penn State defensive line coach [[Larry Johnson (coach)|Larry Johnson]], who convinced him not only to commit to Penn State, but to keep his commitment after crippling sanctions were announced in wake of the [[Penn State child sex abuse scandal]], as well as the arrival of new coach [[Bill O'Brien (American football)|Bill O'Brien]].{{Cite news |last=Juliano |first=Joe |date=October 2, 2013 |title=Penn State's Johnson happy he chose football |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121613aab.html |url-status=dead |access-date=September 28, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180706191301/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121613aab.html |archive-date=July 6, 2018}} ==College career== "An unheralded prep player from New Jersey who spent as much time on the basketball court as the football field," Johnson [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his freshman season, but entered [[training camp]] in 2013 eager to make an impact on the [[defensive line]], establishing himself as a candidate to start opposite [[DaQuan Jones]], Penn State's star [[defensive tackle]] that season.{{Cite news |last=Hockensmith |first=Dustin |date=March 29, 2013 |title=Penn State football: A look at Austin Johnson's unheralded past and 'bright future' |work=[[The Patriot News]] |location=[[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania]] |url=http://www.pennlive.com/pennstatefootball/index.ssf/2013/03/penn_state_football_who_is_aus.html |access-date=September 28, 2014}} Mentored by Larry Johnson, Jones, and [[Jordan Hill (American football)|Jordan Hill]], Austin Johnson proved himself early in the season, and earned a spot in the rotation at defensive tackle with Jones and Kyle Baublitz. At the end of the 2013 season, Johnson was named a member of the freshman all-conference teams by both [[ESPN.com]], and the [[Big Ten Network]].{{Cite web |date=December 16, 2013 |title=Eight Nittany Lions earn All-Big Ten honors from ESPN.com and BTN.com |url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121613aab.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180706191301/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121613aab.html |archive-date=July 6, 2018 |access-date=September 28, 2014 |website=GoPSUSports.com - Penn State Official Athletic Site |publisher=Penn State Intercollegiate Athletics}} Entering his redshirt sophomore season firmly established on the defensive line along with converted [[defensive end]] [[Anthony Zettel]], Johnson sought to "lead by example". Penn State defensive coordinator [[Bob Shoop]] asserted that he was a consummate Penn State defensive tackle, drawing comparisons to Jones and [[Jack Crawford (American football)|Jack Crawford]], among others.{{Cite news |last=Snyder |first=Audrey |date=April 30, 2014 |title=Man in the middle: Penn State DT Austin Johnson continues coming into his own |work=The Patriot News |location=Harrisburg, PA |url=http://www.pennlive.com/pennstatefootball/index.ssf/2014/04/man_in_the_middle_penn_states.html |access-date=September 28, 2014}} ''The Patriot News'' columnist Bob Flounders rated Johnson among the most important components to Penn State's team entering the 2014 season.{{Cite news |last=Flounders |first=Bob |date=July 21, 2014 |title=Breaking down Penn State's most important players: No. 14 DT Austin Johnson |work=The Patriot News |location=Harrisburg, PA |url=http://www.pennlive.com/pennstatefootball/index.ssf/2014/07/breaking_down_penn_states_most_11.html |access-date=September 28, 2014}} Early in the season, he did not compile many defensive statistics, but Penn State coach [[James Franklin (American football coach)|James Franklin]] commented, "[Johnson is] probably the most athletic 315-pound guy I've been around. The thing I like the most about him is every time I see him when he walks in the building or he's out at practice, he's got a huge smile on his face," going onto note that Johnson had the ability to "wreck" an opponent's game.{{Cite news |last=Bodani |first=Frank |date=September 24, 2014 |title=Penn State's Austin Johnson is Nittany Lions' low-key game-wrecker |work=[[York Daily Record]] |url=http://www.ydr.com/psu/ci_26598852/penn-states-austin-johnson-is-nittany-lions-low |url-status=dead |access-date=September 28, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141001034301/http://www.ydr.com/psu/ci_26598852/penn-states-austin-johnson-is-nittany-lions-low |archive-date=October 1, 2014}} Four games into Penn State's season, they had the best rush defense in the country, which Franklin attributed largely to the efforts of Johnson.{{Cite news |last=Juliano |first=Joe |date=September 27, 2014 |title=Penn State's Austin Johnson a terror on defense |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/penn_state/20140927_Penn_State_s_Austin_Johnson_a_terror_on_defense.html |access-date=September 28, 2014}} Johnson majored in [[business administration]] at Penn State. ==Professional career== ===Pre-draft=== Coming out of Penn State, most scouts and analysts projected Johnson to be a second round pick. He was invited to the [[NFL Combine]] and was able to complete all the drills and positional workouts. Scouts and representatives from 31 NFL teams attended Penn State's [[pro day]] to evaluate Johnson, [[Christian Hackenberg]], [[Jordan Lucas]], [[Anthony Zettel]], [[Carl Nassib]], and eight other prospects. '''August Onorato Curley''' (born January 24, 1960) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] who played four seasons with the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the Lions in the fourth round of the [[1983 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Southern California]].

==Early life and college==
August Onorato Curley was born on January 24, 1960, in [[Little Rock, Arkansas]].<ref name="pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/c/curl00400.html | title=August Curley | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He attended Southwest High School in [[Atlanta, Georgia]].<ref name="pfa"/>

He was a member of the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]] of the [[University of Southern California]] from 1978 to 1982 and a three-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1980 to 1982.<ref name="sr"/><ref name="pfa"/> The [[1978 USC Trojans football team|1978 Trojans]] were named [[Coaches Poll]] national champions. He recorded one interception in 1980.<ref name="sr"/> He totaled 115 tackles and one interception his junior year in 1981.<ref name="tcdb">{{cite web | url=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/9197/cid/14861946/1986-McDonald's-Detroit-Lions-NNO-August-Curley | title=#NNO - August Curley DP - Detroit Lions | publisher=tcdb.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He opened his senior season in 1982 with a 22-tackle game against the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]].<ref name="tcdb"/> However, he suffered an injury the next week that caused him to miss the rest of the season.<ref name="tcdb"/> Curley also had one interception in 1982.<ref name="sr">{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/august-curley-1.html | title=August Curley | publisher=sports-reference.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Curley was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the fourth round, with the 94th overall pick, of the [[1983 NFL draft]].<ref name="pfr"/> He officially signed with the team on June 1.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in ten games for the Lions during his rookie year in 1983 before being placed on injured reserve with a knee injury on November 9, 1983.<ref name="pfr"/><ref name="transactions"/><ref name="tcdb"/> The next year, he was placed on the [[physically unable to perform]] list on July 22, 1984, after re-aggravating his knee injury.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="tcdb"/> He was later activated on October 24 and appeared in eight games during the 1984 season.<ref name="pfr"/><ref name="transactions"/> Curley played in all 16 games, starting 14, for the Lions in 1985, recording 51 solo tackles, 24 assisted tackles, two pass breakups, and one forced fumble.<ref name="pfr"/><ref name="tcdb"/> The Lions finished the year with a 4–11–1 record.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/det/1984.htm | title=1984 Detroit Lions Rosters | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 1, 1986, and later activated on November 1, 1986.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in four games in 1986.<ref name="pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CurlAu20.htm | title=August Curley | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref> He became a free agent after the season.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/c/curl00400.html | title=August Curley NFL Transactions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=24 December 2024}}</ref>

'''Austin MacGinnis''' (born May 4, 1995) is an American former [[American football|football]] player. He played [[college football]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats football|Kentucky Wildcats]].

== College career ==
MacGinnis was a consensus first-team selection to the [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-SEC]] team from 2014 to 2018.<ref name="d383">{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2014 |title=The 2014 AP All-SEC football team |url=https://www.secsports.com/news/2014/12/the-2014-ap-all-sec-football-team |access-date=2025-01-19 |website=Southeastern Conference}}</ref> He broke the school single season record for field goals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lintner |first=Jonathan |date=November 29, 2014 |title=UK kicker MacGinnis has record day vs. Cards |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2014/11/29/kentucky-kicker-austin-macginnis-record-day-louisville/19673633/ |access-date=January 10, 2024 |website=The Courier-Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> MacGinnis was chosen by Phil Steele first-team preseason All-SEC for 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2, 2015 |title=Five Wildcats Named Preseason All-SEC by Phil Steele CFB |url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/060215aaa.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626100729/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/060215aaa.html |archive-date=June 26, 2015 |access-date=June 25, 2015}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
=== Memphis Express ===
After attending the [[Chicago Bears]] rookie camp in 2018 and trying out for the team again in January 2019, MacGinnis returned to pro football when he was signed by the [[Memphis Express]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]] on February 27, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Terry |first=Derek |date=April 29, 2018 |title=Austin MacGinnis signs rookie camp deal with Bears |url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/article/kentucky-football-austin-macginnis-signs-rookie-camp-deal-with-bears-117818061/ |access-date=March 3, 2019 |publisher=[[247Sports.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fisher |first=Chris |date=February 28, 2019 |title=Austin MacGinnis signs with AAF's Memphis Express |url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/Kentucky-football-Austin-MacGinnis-signs-with-Memphis-Express-of-AAF-129575929/ |access-date=March 3, 2019 |publisher=[[247Sports.com]]}}</ref> In his debut against the [[San Diego Fleet]], he kicked four field goals, including the game winner to secure a 26–23 Memphis win.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sullivan |first=Josh |date=March 2, 2019 |title=Former Kentucky kicker's pro debut perfect, including the game-winner |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/ex-cats/article227042289.html |access-date=March 3, 2019}}</ref> He was eventually named AAF Player of the Week for Week 4.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stuchbery |first=Fran |date=March 5, 2019 |title=Farrow, Memphis Pair Earn AAF Honors for Week Four |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/farrow-memphis-pair-earn-aaf-honors-for-week-four/n-5454653 |access-date=March 5, 2019 |publisher=Our Sports Central}}</ref> The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

=== Dallas Renegades ===
MacGinnis was selected by the [[Dallas Renegades]] in the [[2020 XFL draft|2020 XFL supplemental draft]] on November 22, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Talbot |first=Damond |date=October 16, 2019 |title=XFL Draft Phase 5: The Final Rounds of the Draft, Find out who was selected |url=https://www.nfldraftdiamonds.com/2019/10/xfl-draft-8/ |access-date=October 22, 2019 |publisher=NFL Draft Diamonds}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |access-date=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Rams ===
On April 13, 2020, MacGinnis signed a contract with the [[Los Angeles Rams]] of the [[National Football League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 13, 2020 |title=Rams agree to terms with kickers Austin MacGinnis and Lirim Hajrullahu |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-agree-to-terms-kickers-austin-macginnis-lirim-hajrullahu |website=therams.com}}</ref> He was waived on September 4, 2020, after losing the kicker job to rookie [[Sam Sloman]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Stu |date=September 4, 2020 |title=Rams waive 17 players ahead of 53-man roster deadline |url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-waive-17-players-ahead-of-53-man-roster-deadline |access-date=January 10, 2024 |website=TheRams.com}}</ref> He was re-signed to the Rams' practice squad on October 28, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=October 28, 2020 |title=Rams put Burgess on IR and designate Noteboom to return, among other roster moves |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2020/10/28/rams-roster-moves-burgess-noteboom-macginnis/ |access-date=November 11, 2020 |work=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on December 10 for the team's week 14 game against the [[New England Patriots]], and reverted to the practice squad after the game.<ref>{{Cite news |last=DaSilva |first=Cameron |date=December 10, 2020 |title=Rams promote Austin MacGinnis from practice squad with Matt Gay questionable |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2020/12/10/rams-austin-macginnis-matt-gay-kicker-week-14/ |access-date=January 26, 2021 |work=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> On January 18, 2021, MacGinnis signed a reserve/futures contract with the Rams.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams sign 14 players to reserve/future contracts|url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-sign-14-players-to-reserve-future-contracts|author=Jackson, Stu|website=TheRams.com|date=January 18, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on August 17, 2021.

===New Orleans Breakers===
MacGinnis was selected in the 32nd round of the [[2022 USFL draft]] by the [[New Orleans Breakers (2022)|New Orleans Breakers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/usfl-draft-2022-picks-results-rosters/kfjtmrpdeztksutjassswllz|website=[[Sporting News]]|title=USFL Draft tracker: Complete results, rosters for new football league|date=February 23, 2022|author=Camenker, Jacob}}</ref> He was transferred to the team's inactive roster on May 5, 2022,<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLBreakers |title=Roster Updates |number=1522124264853282817 |date=May 5, 2022 |access-date=May 5, 2022}}</ref> and moved to the team's "did not report" list on May 8.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLBreakers |title=Transferred to inactive/DNR roster |number=1523360736734367744 |date=May 8, 2022 |access-date=May 9, 2022}}</ref>

'''Austin Manuel Hooper''' (born October 29, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[tight end]] for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford Cardinal]] and was selected by the Falcons in the third round of the [[2016 NFL draft]]. Hooper has also played for the [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Tennessee Titans]], [[Las Vegas Raiders]], and [[New England Patriots]].

==Early life==
Hooper attended [[De La Salle High School (Concord, California)|De La Salle High School]] in [[Concord, California]], where he played for the [[high school football|football]] team. He was rated by [[Rivals.com]] as a three-star recruit and committed to [[Stanford University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Hooper, 2013 Weakside Defensive End |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2013/austin-hooper-12048 |access-date=November 16, 2022 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2013 |title=Stanford football receives commitment from top tight end |url=http://www.paloaltoonline.com/news/2013/01/14/stanford-football-receives-commitment-from-top-tight-end |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=Palo Alto Online}}</ref> Hooper was listed as a [[defensive end]] by Rivals and also by [[ESPN]] who had him rated as a four-star recruit and the #261 player overall in the nation regardless of position.

==College career==
After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his first year at Stanford in 2013, Hooper played in all 13 games as a redshirt freshman in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=FitzGerald |first=Tom |date=July 31, 2014 |title=Austin Hooper is man to beat at tight end for Stanford |url=http://www.sfgate.com/collegesports/article/Austin-Hooper-is-man-to-beat-at-tight-end-for-5658582.php |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=SFGate.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=FitzGerald |first=Tom |date=December 17, 2014 |title=Hooper helping re-establish tight end position at Stanford |url=http://www.sfgate.com/collegesports/article/Hooper-helping-re-establish-tight-end-position-at-5961563.php |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=SFGate.com}}</ref> He finished the season with 40 [[football catch|receptions]] for 499 yards and two [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Hooper 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/austin-hooper-1/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=December 26, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2015, Hooper had 34 receptions for 438 yards for six touchdowns, including a career best 79 yards and a touchdown in an upset of then #6 [[USC Trojans football|USC]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Hooper 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/austin-hooper-1/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=December 26, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Stanford at Southern California Box Score, September 19, 2015 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2015-09-19-southern-california.html |access-date=December 26, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was a finalist for the [[John Mackey Award]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2015 |title=College football: Christian McCaffrey, Joshua Garnett, Austin Hooper and Michael Carrizosa finalists for awards |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/sports/ci_29163440/college-football-christian-mccaffrey-joshua-garnett-austin-hooper |access-date=February 15, 2026 |website=Mercury News |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> and First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12 Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 31, 2016 |title=Austin Hooper highlights: Talented tight end looking to make an impact on Sundays |url=http://pac-12.com/videos/austin-hooper-highlights-talented-tight-end-looking-make-impact-sundays |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171228171910/http://pac-12.com/videos/austin-hooper-highlights-talented-tight-end-looking-make-impact-sundays |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 28, 2017 |access-date=December 28, 2017 |website=Pac-12 |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
On January 4, 2016, it was announced that Hooper would forfeit his last two years of eligibility and enter the [[2016 NFL draft]]. The draft class was notably thin at [[tight end]] and his draft stock was high after coming off an impressive season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 4, 2016 |title=Stanford TE Austin Hooper declares for draft |url=https://wtop.com/nfl/2016/01/stanford-te-austin-hooper-declares-for-draft/ |access-date=December 20, 2017 |website=wtop.com |agency=Associated Press}}{{Dead link|date=December 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Hooper was one of 15 tight ends to receive an invitation to the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sharp |first=Katie |date=February 11, 2016 |title=Here's the complete list of players invited to the 2016 NFL Combine, led by 14 from Ohio State |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2016/2/11/10967624/2016-nfl-scouting-combine-invited-players-list-ohio-state |access-date=December 20, 2017 |website=SBNation.com}}</ref> He had an overall impressive performance, finishing third among all tight ends in the [[40-yard dash]], fourth in the [[bench press]], fifth in the [[three-cone drill]], and finished sixth among his position group in the vertical.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brady |first=James |date=February 27, 2016 |title=NFL Combine 2016 results: Full times, measurements for tight ends |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2016/2/27/11126486/2016-nfl-combine-results-tight-end-drills |access-date=December 20, 2017 |website=SBNation.com}}</ref> 

On March 17, 2016, Hooper opted to participate at Stanford's [[Pro Day]], performing only positional drills for scouts and team representatives that included [[San Francisco 49ers]] head coach [[Chip Kelly]] and [[Oakland Raiders]] offensive coordinator [[Bill Musgrave]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 16, 2016 |title=Pro Day on Tap |url=http://www.gostanford.com/news/2016/3/16/210809488.aspx |access-date=December 20, 2017 |website=GoStanford.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mazeika |first=Vytas |date=March 23, 2016 |title=Stanford football: NFL Draft hopefuls impress scouts at pro day |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2016/03/23/stanford-football-nfl-draft-hopefuls-impress-scouts-at-pro-day/ |access-date=December 20, 2017 |website=MercuryNews.com}}</ref> 

Throughout the pre-draft process, Hooper attended private workouts and visits with the [[Miami Dolphins]], [[Atlanta Falcons]], [[Denver Broncos]], and [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lambert |first=Terry |date=March 24, 2016 |title=2016 NFL Draft: Titans visit with tight end prospects Austin Hooper, Stephen Anderson |url=https://www.musiccitymiracles.com/2016/3/24/11296594/titans-visit-with-two-tight-end-prospects-2016-nfl-draft-austin-hooper-stephen-anderson |access-date=December 20, 2017 |website=Musiccitymiracles.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Klis |first=Mike |date=April 21, 2016 |title=BRONCOS DRAFT PREVIEW: TIGHT ENDS |url=http://www.9news.com/mobile/article/sports/nfl/denver-broncos/mike-klis/broncos-draft-preview-tight-ends/147817875 |access-date=December 20, 2017 |website=9news.com}}</ref> Hooper was projected to be a second or third round pick by [[NFL draft]] experts and scouts. He was ranked the second best tight end prospect in the draft by NFLDraftScout.com and the third best tight end by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' and NFL analyst [[Mike Mayock]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=*Austin Hooper, DS #2 TE, Stanford |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=127324&draftyear=2016&genpos=TE |access-date=December 20, 2017 |website=NFLDraftScout.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Burke |first=Chris |date=April 12, 2016 |title=2016 NFL Draft Position Rankings |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2016/04/12/nfl-draft-2016-position-rankings-players-prospects |access-date=December 20, 2017 |website=si.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayock |first=Mike |date=April 27, 2016 |title=Mike Mayock's 2016 NFL Draft position rankings 5.0 |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000656285/article/mike-mayocks-2016-nfl-draft-position-rankings-50 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428120518/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000656285/article/mike-mayocks-2016-nfl-draft-position-rankings-50 |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 28, 2016 |access-date=December 20, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>
