'''Austin Corbett''' (born September 5, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for the [[Buffalo Bills]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Corbett played for Reed High School in [[Sparks, Nevada|Sparks]], [[Nevada]]. Starting as a walk on, he played [[college football]] for the [[Nevada Wolf Pack football|Nevada Wolf Pack]].

==Early life==
Corbett graduated from [[Edward C. Reed High School]] in [[Sparks, Nevada|Sparks]], [[Nevada]], where he was a member of two regional championship teams in 2012 and 2013. He was a First team All-Region and All-State in 2012. Besides football, he lettered in [[wrestling]], [[basketball]] and [[track and field]], he was even a First team All-State in [[shot put]] in 2013. He was a member of the National Honor Society and freshman mentor council.<ref "NevadaWolfPackBio">{{cite web |title=Nevada Wolf Pack Bio for Austin Corbett |url=https://nevadawolfpack.com/sports/football/roster/austin-corbett/299 |website=Nevada Wolf Pack Athletics |date=2017 |access-date=30 Jan 2026}}</ref>

==College career==
Before the 2017 season, Corbett had more experience than any other [[offensive lineman]] on the Wolf Pack.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/college/nevada/2017/04/04/wolf-pack-looks-make-union-great-again/100027592/|title=Wolf Pack looks to make 'The Union' great again|author=Murray|first=Chris|date=April 4, 2017|work=Reno Gazette Journal}}</ref> After the season, he received several team honors including being named the Basalite Big Blocker and a team captain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/college/nevada/2017/11/26/ty-gangi-wins-wolf-packs-golden-helmet-award-team-mvp/896585001/|title=Ty Gangi wins Wolf Pack's Golden Helmet Award as team MVP|author=Murray|first=Chris|date=November 26, 2017|work=Reno Gazette Journal}}</ref> Overall, Corbett was a 4-year starter at left tackle for Nevada, taking over for his future Cleveland Browns teammate [[Joel Bitonio]] as Nevada's starting left tackle as a [[redshirted|redshirt]] freshman.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Corbett - Football |url=https://nevadawolfpack.com/sports/football/roster/austin-corbett/299 |access-date=July 8, 2024 |website=University of Nevada Athletics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Zierlein |first=Lance |title=Austin Corbett Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/austin-corbett/3200434f-5200-8097-d4cb-2bd53a7e3b55 |access-date=September 22, 2025 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Following his senior season, Corbett was named as a semifinalist for the 2017 [[Burlsworth Trophy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/college/nevada/2017/11/07/nevadas-austin-corbett-one-10-semifinalists-burlsworth-trophy/840380001/|title=Nevada's Austin Corbett one of 10 semifinalists for Burlsworth Trophy|author=Murray|first=Chris|date=November 7, 2017|work=Reno Gazette Journal}}</ref> He was also invited to the [[2018 Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mwwire.com/2017/11/21/2018-senior-bowl-nevadas-austin-corbett-earns-invite/|title=2018 Senior Bowl: Nevada's Austin Corbett Earns Invite|author=Mauss|first=Jeremy|date=November 21, 2017|work=Mountain West Wire}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
The [[Cleveland Browns]] selected Austin Corbett in the second round (33rd overall) of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=April 27, 2018 |title=Browns draft Austin Corbett, Nick Chubb in Round 2 |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/browns-draft-austin-corbett-nick-chubb-in-round-2-0ap3000000929496 |access-date=March 25, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On May 6, Corbett signed a four-year deal worth $7.568 million featuring a $3.584 million signing bonus.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=May 6, 2018 |title=Browns sign potential Thomas replacement Corbett |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/browns-sign-potential-thomas-replacement-corbett-0ap3000000931685 |access-date=March 25, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cabot |first=Mary Kay |date=May 7, 2018 |title=Browns sign draft picks Austin Corbett, Damion Ratley and Simeon Thomas |url=https://www.cleveland.com/browns/index.ssf/2018/05/browns_sign_3_draft_picks.html |access-date=July 26, 2018 |website=The Plain Dealer}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
The Browns traded Corbett to the [[Los Angeles Rams]] on October 15, 2019, in exchange for the Rams' fifth-round pick in the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 15, 2019 |title=Browns trade OL Austin Corbett to Rams |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-trade-ol-austin-corbett-to-rams |access-date=December 15, 2023 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Cabot |first1=Mary Kay |title=Browns trade 2018 No. 33 overall pick Austin Corbett to the Rams for a 5th-round draft pick in 2021 |url=https://www.cleveland.com/browns/2019/10/browns-trade-austin-corbett-to-the-rams-for-an-undisclosed-draft-pick.html |publisher=Cleveland.com |date=October 15, 2019}}</ref> In 2019, Corbett started in 7 of 8 games after his trade to the Rams. In 2021–22, Corbett started all 17 regular season games. Corbett also started in every playoff game, including [[Super Bowl LVI]], as the Rams went on to win the game 23–20, playing at home, against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schwartz |first=Paul |date=February 13, 2021 |title=LA Rams defeat Cincinnati Bengals to win Super Bowl 2022 |url=https://nypost.com/2022/02/13/la-rams-defeat-cincinnati-bengals-to-win-super-bowl-2022/ |access-date=March 25, 2023 |website=New York Post}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On March 16, 2022, Corbett signed a three-year, $26.25 million contract with the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=March 18, 2022 |title=Guard Austin Corbett officially signs with Panthers |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/guard-austin-corbett-officially-signs-with-panthers |access-date=March 25, 2023 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> In the season finale against the [[New Orleans Saints]], he suffered a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]].<ref name="o842">{{cite web | last=Gantt | first=Darin | title=Austin Corbett suffers torn ACL in season finale | website=Panthers.com | date=January 9, 2023 | url=https://www.panthers.com/news/austin-corbett-suffers-torn-acl-in-finale | access-date=January 1, 2025}}</ref>

On August 29, 2023, Corbett was placed on the team's reserve/physically unable to perform list which would require him to miss the first four games of the 2023 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-make-moves-en-route-to-53-man-roster-limit|work=Panthers.com|title=Panthers make moves en route to 53-man roster limit|date=August 29, 2023|accessdate=August 30, 2023|first=Darin|last=Gantt}}</ref> He was activated on October 24.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2023 |title=Panthers place three on IR, activate one, agree to terms with two |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-place-three-on-ir-activate-one-agree-to-terms-with-two |access-date=December 15, 2023 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> He suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 11 and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on November 22.<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Corbett, Dicaprio Bootle placed on injured reserve|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/austin-corbett-dicaprio-bootle-placed-on-injured-reserve|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=November 22, 2023}}</ref>

Corbett entered the 2024 season as the Panthers starting center. He started the first five games before suffering a torn biceps in Week 5, ending his season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marquis Haynes, Ian Thomas added to active roster|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/marquis-haynes-ian-thomas-added-to-active-roster-austin-corbett-injured-reserve|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=October 12, 2024}}</ref>

On March 12, 2025, Corbett re-signed with the Panthers on a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Panthers agree to terms with center Austin Corbett |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-agree-to-terms-with-center-austin-corbett-offensive-line |access-date=March 8, 2025 |website=Panthers.com |language=en-US}}</ref> In Week 2 against the [[2025 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]], Corbett suffered a Grade 3 [[medial collateral ligament|MCL]] injury in his left knee; he was placed on injured reserve on September 15.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Carolina Panthers to place Robert Hunt, Austin Corbett on IR|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46272978/carolina-panthers-place-robert-hunt-austin-corbett-ir|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> He was activated on October 18, ahead of the team's Week 7 matchup against the [[2025 New York Jets season|New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Panthers activate two from injured reserve, place one on IR|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-activate-two-from-injured-reserve-place-one-on-ir-jalen-coker-austin-corbett-patrick-jones-ii|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=Panthers.com|language=en}}</ref> He started 11 games at center and both guard spots in 2025.

===Buffalo Bills===
On March 26, 2026, Corbett signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]] on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Glab |first1=Maddy |last2=Ciano |first2=Sydney |title=Buffalo Bills sign C Lloyd Cushenberry, WR Trent Sherfield and C/G Austin Corbett to one-year contracts |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/buffalo-bills-sign-c-lloyd-cushenberry-wr-trent-sherfield-and-c-g-austin-corbett-to-one-year-contracts |website=BuffaloBills.com |access-date=27 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Austin Mitchell Seibert''' (born November 15, 1996) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[placekicker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]], where he was named the 2018 [[Big 12 Special Teams Player of the Year]], and was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the fifth round of the [[2019 NFL draft]]. Seibert was also a member of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[Detroit Lions]], [[New York Jets]], [[New Orleans Saints]], and [[Washington Commanders]]. He holds the Commanders' franchise record for field goals made in a game with seven.

==Early life==
Seibert was born on November 15, 1996, in [[Belleville, Illinois]], later attending [[Belleville High School-West]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seibert's High School Football Stats |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/austin-seibert/T2ref_TuEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/football/stats.htm |access-date=October 1, 2019 |website=MaxPreps.com |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Seibert attended and played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]]. He contributed to the football team as a [[placekicker]] and a [[punter (football)|punter]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seibert College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits  |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/austin-seibert-1.html |access-date=October 1, 2019 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was named the 2018 [[Big 12 Special Teams Player of the Year]].

===Cleveland Browns===
Seibert was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the fifth round (170th overall) of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gribble |first=Andrew |date=April 27, 2019 |title=Cleveland Browns select Oklahoma K Austin Seibert with No. 170 pick in 2019 NFL Draft |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/cleveland-browns-select-oklahoma-k-austin-seibert-with-no-170-pick-in-2019-nfl-d |access-date=April 29, 2019 |website=[[Cleveland Browns]]}}</ref> Seibert signed his rookie contract with the Browns on May 3, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pokorny |first=Chris |date=May 3, 2019 |title=Cleveland Browns sign 5th round draft pick, K Austin Seibert |url=https://www.dawgsbynature.com/2019/5/3/18528924/cleveland-browns-sign-5th-round-draft-pick-k-austin-seibert |access-date=October 1, 2019 |website=Dawgs By Nature}}</ref>

Seibert made the Browns' 53-man roster out of [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]]. He made his NFL debut in the Browns' 2019 regular season opener against the [[Tennessee Titans]]. He converted one of two extra point attempts in the 43–13 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Cleveland Browns - September 8th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201909080cle.htm |access-date=October 1, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He scored his first career field goal during the Browns' Week 2 game against the [[New York Jets]], where he kicked three field goals in a Browns' 23–3 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at New York Jets - September 16th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201909160nyj.htm |access-date=October 1, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> As a rookie, he converted 30 of 35 extra point attempts and 25 of 29 field goal attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seibert 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SeibAu00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was named to the PFWA All-Rookie Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2019.htm |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Seibert was waived by the Browns on September 14, 2020, after missing a field goal and extra point in a 38–6 loss to the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in Week 1.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns waive kicker Austin Seibert, sign Cody Parkey |url=https://www.wkyc.com/article/sports/nfl/browns/browns-waive-seibert-sign-parkey/95-7186573b-7cca-49a7-8f19-de7ae4b274b4 |access-date=September 16, 2020 |website=wkyc.com|date=September 14, 2020 }}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
Seibert was claimed off waivers by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on September 15, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 15, 2020 |title=Bengals Make Player Moves Ahead Of Week 2 Game Against The Browns |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-make-player-moves-ahead-of-week-2-game-against-the-browns |access-date=September 30, 2020 |website=Bengals.com}}</ref> Seibert played in four games during the 2020 season with the Bengals making six of nine field goals and all eight of the extra points he attempted.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seibert 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SeibAu00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2021, after losing out the starting kicker job to [[Evan McPherson]] in training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2021 |title=Bengals Reduce 2021 Roster To 53 Players |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-reduce-2021-roster-to-53-players |website=Bengals.com |accessdate=August 31, 2021}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On September 1, 2021, the [[Detroit Lions]] claimed Seibert off waivers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2021 |title=Lions announce roster moves |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-roster-moves-hodge-seibert-beckett |website=DetroitLions.com |accessdate=September 1, 2021}}</ref> On September 23, 2021, Seibert was placed on the [[COVID-19]] reserve list. He was replaced on the active roster by kicker [[Ryan Santoso]], who had just been signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Birkett |first=Dave |date=September 23, 2021 |title=Detroit Lions place K Austin Seibert on COVID list, WR Tyrell Williams on injured reserve |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2021/09/23/detroit-lions-austin-seibert-covid-list-tyrell-williams-injured-reserve/5828562001/ |access-date=September 27, 2021 |website=Detroit Free Press |language=en-US}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on November 13 with a hip injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schlitt |first=Erik |date=November 13, 2021 |title=Detroit Lions elevate kicker Ryan Santoso vs. Steelers, place Austin Seibert on IR |url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/2021/11/13/22779719/detroit-lions-elevate-kicker-ryan-santoso-steelers-austin-seibert-on-ir |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=Pride of Detroit |publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>  He appeared in six games in the 2021 season. He converted all five extra point attempts and 10 of 12 field goal attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seibert 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SeibAu00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Seibert was waived by the Lions on October 6, 2022, after the team signed [[Michael Badgley]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=October 7, 2022 |title=Lions waive Austin Seibert |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/lions-waive-austin-seibert |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBCSports.com}}</ref> In the 2022 season, he converted all 12 extra point attempts and three of five field goal attempts in three games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Seibert 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SeibAu00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=August 28, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Jets (first stint)===
On September 16, 2023, Seibert was signed to the [[New York Jets]] practice squad following an injury to kicker [[Greg Zuerlein]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Greenberg, Ethan |date=September 16, 2023 |title=Jets Sign QB Tim Boyle to Active Roster, Release WR Irvin Charles |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-qb-tim-boyle-to-active-roster-release-wr-irvin-charles |access-date=March 18, 2026 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He was released on September 30.<ref name="k938">{{cite web | last=Greenberg | first=Ethan | title=Jets Sign DL Tanzel Smart to Practice Squad, Release K Austin Seibert | website=New York Jets | date=2023-09-30 | url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-dl-tanzel-smart-to-practice-squad-release-k-austin-seibert | access-date=2024-12-03}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On November 28, 2023, Seibert was signed to the [[New Orleans Saints]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=November 29, 2023 |title=Saints add K Austin Seibert to practice squad |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/saints-add-k-austin-seibert-to-practice-squad |access-date=30 November 2023 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref> He was released on December 7.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 December 2023 |title=Austin Seibert: Cut by New Orleans |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/austin-seibert-cut-by-new-orleans/ |access-date=7 December 2023 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref>

===New York Jets (second stint)===
On December 27, 2023, Seibert was signed to the Jets practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=December 27, 2023 |title=Jets Place OL Duane Brown on Injured Reserve; Sign TE Zack Kuntz |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-ol-duane-brown-on-injured-reserve-sign-te-zack-kuntz |access-date=2024-09-18 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 8, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=January 8, 2024 |title=Jets Sign Nine Players to Reserve/Future Contracts |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-nine-players-to-reserve-future-contracts-01-08-2024 |access-date=2024-09-18 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He was released on August 27, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Final Cuts {{!}} Jets Move 37 to Get Their Roster to 53 Players |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-53-man-roster-2024-season |access-date=2024-09-18 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

===Washington Commanders===
On September 10, 2024, Seibert signed with the [[Washington Commanders]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Selby |first=Zach |date=10 September 2024 |title=Commanders sign K Austin Seibert to active roster, add T Anim Dankwah to practice squad |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-sign-k-austin-seibert-to-active-roster-add-t-anim-dankwah-to-practice-squad |access-date=10 September 2024 |website=Commanders.com}}</ref> In Week 2, he was named the [[2024 NFL season#Players of the Week / Month|NFC Special Teams Player of the Week]] after kicking a franchise-record seven field goals in his Washington debut, accounting for all of the team's points in a 21–18 victory over the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Jhabvala |first=Nicki |date=15 September 2024 |title=Commanders’ new kicker bails them out in sloppy win over Giants |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2024/09/15/commanders-giants-austin-seibert/ |work=The Washington Post |location= |access-date=15 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=18 September 2024 |title=Austin Seibert named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/austin-seibert-named-nfc-special-teams-player-of-the-week |access-date=18 September 2024 |website=Commanders.com}}</ref> Seibert was placed on [[injured reserve]] for a hip injury on November 26, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Keim |first1=John |title=Commanders put Austin Seibert on IR after missed kicks vs. Dallas |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/42628616/commanders-put-austin-seibert-ir-missed-pats-vs-dallas |website=ESPN |access-date=27 November 2024 |date=27 November 2024}}</ref>

'''Austin Cutting''' (born October 27, 1996) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[long snapper]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Air Force Falcons football|Air Force Falcons]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 28, 2019 |title=Austin Cutting to serve his country with Air Force but still could be Vikings' long snapper |url=https://www.twincities.com/2019/04/27/austin-cutting-to-serve-his-country-with-air-force-but-still-could-be-vikings-long-snapper/ |access-date=April 28, 2019 |website=Twin Cities |language=en-US}}</ref> and was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the seventh round of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=OConnell |first=Jim |date=April 27, 2019 |title=Air Force long snapper Austin Cutting drafted by Minnesota Vikings |url=https://gazette.com/air-force-long-snapper-austin-cutting-drafted-by-minnesota-vikings/article_75309796-693c-11e9-a5cd-d3881843d9c0.html |access-date=April 28, 2019 |website=Colorado Springs Gazette |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Cutting was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the seventh round (250th overall) of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters, Craig |date=April 27, 2019 |title=Vikings Cap 2019 Draft by Selecting Receiver and Long Snapper |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-select-air-force-ls-austin-cutting-in-the-7th-round-of-the-nfl-draft |website=Vikings.com |access-date=June 7, 2019 |archive-date=August 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811155758/https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-select-air-force-ls-austin-cutting-in-the-7th-round-of-the-nfl-draft |url-status=dead }}</ref> There had been precedent, such as [[Joe Cardona]] of the [[2015 NFL draft]], for military school graduates to be allowed to defer their 24-month service policy,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tomasson, Chris |date=April 29, 2019 |title=Austin Cutting to serve his country with Air Force but still could be Vikings' long snapper |url=https://www.twincities.com/2019/04/27/austin-cutting-to-serve-his-country-with-air-force-but-still-could-be-vikings-long-snapper/ |access-date=September 8, 2019 |website=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]]}}</ref> but the [[United States Secretary of Defense]] rescinded the policy in 2017 to allow military service academy student-athlete graduates to delay their assignments to explore professional sports opportunities. In June 2019, [[US President]] [[Donald Trump]] requested that a policy be established to facilitate athletic pursuits and Cutting was the first to sign a professional contract following the new policy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartsell, Jeff |date=August 14, 2019 |title=Trump decision could help West Ashley's Brett Toth get Army's permission to play in NFL |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/trump-decision-could-help-west-ashley-s-brett-toth-get/article_32bc7672-beb5-11e9-bcea-33c79aedbc11.html |access-date=September 8, 2019 |website=[[The Post and Courier]]}}</ref>

Cutting was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on November 10, 2020,<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 10, 2020 |title=Vikings Activate LB Todd Davis from Reserve/COVID-19; Announce Roster Moves |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/todd-davis-activate-reserve-covid-19-announce-roster-moves |access-date=December 17, 2020 |work=Vikings.com}}</ref> and activated four days later.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Peters, Craig |date=November 14, 2020 |title=Vikings Activate Austin Cutting, Waive Pat Elflein |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/pat-elflein-wavie-austin-cutting-activate-reserve-covid19 |access-date=December 17, 2020 |work=Vikings.com}}</ref> He was waived on December 1, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=December 1, 2020 |title=Vikings waive Austin Cutting, Hardy Nickerson |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/vikings-waive-austin-cutting-hardy-nickerson |access-date=2025-06-07 |work=NBCSports.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Austin Schlottmann''' (born September 18, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for the [[Tennessee Titans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU Horned Frogs]]. Schlottmann signed as an undrafted free agent with the [[Denver Broncos]] after the [[2018 NFL draft]], and has also played in the NFL for the [[Minnesota Vikings]].

==Early life==
Schlottmann was born and raised in [[Brenham, Texas]], where he became a football star at [[Brenham High School]], earning All-State honors in 2013<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2013 |title=The 2013 Texas Sports Writers Association's All-State Football Teams |url=http://txswa.org/allstate-football13.php |website=Texas Sports Writers Association}}</ref> while helping lead the Cubs to the Class 4A Championship game at [[AT&T Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 22, 2013 |title=Brenham can't slow Aledo in state title game |url=https://www.theeagle.com/brazos_sports/football/brenham-can-t-slow-aledo-in-state-title-game/article_0eb4e91a-2c98-52bd-a80e-fc6f117499b5.html |website=Bryan/College Station Eagle}}</ref> A 3-star offensive tackle recruit, he signed a [[national letter of intent]] to play [[college football]] at [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU]] on February 5, 2014, over offers from [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State]], [[Houston Cougars football|Houston]], [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech]], [[New Mexico Lobos football|New Mexico]], [[Northern Colorado Bears football|Northern Colorado]], [[Rice Owls football|Rice]], [[Texas State Bobcats football|Texas State]], [[Tulsa Golden Hurricanes football|Tulsa]], and [[UCF Knights football|UCF]].<ref name="247sports">{{Cite web |title=Austin Schlottmann |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Austin-Schlottmann-23442/high-school-37391/ |access-date=September 14, 2019 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Schlottmann - Denver Broncos - Interior Offensive Line |url=https://www.on3.com/rivals/austin-schlottmann-8691/ |access-date=2026-02-11 |website=Rivals |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Schlottmann enrolled at [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU]] in the summer of 2014, and played in all 13 of the Frogs' games that fall as [[true freshman]]. That season, the team won a [[Big 12 Conference]] championship and ranked third in the final polls after blowing out [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss]] 42–3 in the [[2014 Peach Bowl|Peach Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2014 |title=Scorned Frogs: TCU crushes Ole Miss in Peach Bowl |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/2014/12/31/no-6-tcu-crushes-no-9-ole-miss-42-3-in-peach/21118491/ |website=USAToday.com}}</ref>

Schlottman was named second-team All-Big 12 as a junior in 2016,<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2016 |title=2016 All-Big 12 Football Awards Announced |url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=211345089 |website=Big12Sports.com}}</ref> and honorable mention All-Big 12 as a senior in 2017. Overall in his college career, he played in 51 games, starting 29 of them (19 at center and 10 at right guard).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-29 |title=Austin Schlottmann - Football |url=https://gofrogs.com/sports/football/roster/austin-schlottmann/1020 |access-date=2026-02-11 |website=TCU Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
After going undrafted in the [[2018 NFL draft]], Schlottmann signed as an undrafted free agent with the [[Denver Broncos]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 26, 2018 |title=Denver Broncos undrafted rookie spotlight: OT Austin Schlottmann |url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/2018/05/26/denver-broncos-undrafted-rookie-spotlight-ot-austin-schlotmann/ |website=USA Today}}</ref> which reunited him with high school teammate [[Courtland Sutton]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2019 |title=Broncos' OL Austin Schlottmann rising on depth chart with position flexibility |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2019/08/23/broncos-austin-schlottmann-nfl-preseason/ |website=Denver Post}}</ref>  He spent the entire 2018 season on the Broncos' [[practice squad]].

In the 2019 season, he made the active roster as second-string left guard coming out of training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2019 |title=First Look At The Denver Broncos 2019 Roster |url=https://denver.cbslocal.com/2019/08/31/denver-broncos-final-2019-roster/ |website=CBS 4 Denver}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lynch |first=Tim |date=2019-09-03 |title=Broncos release first regular season depth chart |url=https://www.milehighreport.com/2019/9/3/20844241/broncos-depth-chart-2019 |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=Mile High Report |language=en}}</ref> Schlottman made his regular season debut on September 9, 2019, against the [[Oakland Raiders]] on ''[[Monday Night Football]]''. He was named the starting right guard in Week 14 after starter [[Ronald Leary]] was out for the rest of the season; second-string right guard [[Elijah Wilkinson]] was moved to right tackle to fill in for starting RT [[Ja'Wuan James]] out with a knee injury.

On August 31, 2021, Schlottmann was waived by the Broncos and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla, Aric |date=August 31, 2021 |title=Broncos make series of roster transactions to reach 53-man limit |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-make-series-of-roster-transactions-to-reach-53-man-limit |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla, Aric |date=September 1, 2021 |title=Broncos sign 14 players to their practice squad |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-14-players-to-their-practice-squad |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 9.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla, Aric |date=November 9, 2021 |title=Broncos promote G Austin Schlottmann to active roster, place G Graham Glasgow on IR |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-promote-g-austin-schlottmann-to-active-roster-place-g-graham-glasgow-on- |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
On March 16, 2022, Schlottmann signed with the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters, Craig |date=March 16, 2022 |title=Vikings Agree to Terms with G/C Austin Schlottmann |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/austin-schlottmann-guard-center-agree-to-terms |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] with a left fibula fracture on January 3, 2023;<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ragatz, Will |date=January 3, 2023 |title=Vikings Place Brian O'Neill, Austin Schlottmann on IR; Sign C Greg Mancz, OT Bobby Evans |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/vikings/news/vikings-place-brian-oneill-austin-schlottmann-ir-sign-c-greg-mancz-ot-bobby-evans |website=SI.com}}</ref> [[Greg Mancz]] was signed to take Schlottman's place, but was released 11 days later.

Schlottmann re-signed with the Vikings on March 17, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=March 17, 2023 |title=Austin Schlottmann & Vikings Agree to Terms for Return |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/austin-schlottmann-offensive-lineman-agree-to-terms |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On March 15, 2024, Schlottmann signed a two–year deal with the [[New York Giants]].<ref name="g218">{{cite web | last=Traina | first=Patricia | title=New York Giants Add Two Interior O-linemen | website=Sports Illustrated | date=2024-03-15 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/giants/gm-report/new-york-giants-add-two-interior-o-linemen | access-date=2024-09-14}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 27.<ref>{{cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=August 29, 2024 |title=Giants sign TE/FB Jakob Johnson to 53-man roster; C Austin Schlottmann to IR |url=https://www.giants.com/news/jakob-johnson-practice-squad-roster-austin-schlottmann-injury-elijah-garcia-art-green-duke-shelley |access-date=October 4, 2025 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> He was activated on December 28.

===Tennessee Titans===
On March 12, 2026, Schlottmann signed a two-year, $7 million contract with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wyatt |first1=Jim |title=Titans Sign Center Austin Schlottmann |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-center-austin-schlottmann |website=TennesseeTitans.com |access-date=13 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Austin Jackson''' (born August 11, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Miami Dolphins]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]] and was selected by the Dolphins in the first round of the [[2020 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Jackson grew up in [[Phoenix, Arizona]] and attended [[North Canyon High School]], where he played defensive and offensive line on the school's football team and also was a member of the basketball and track and field teams.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barnett |first=Josh |date=January 27, 2017 |title=Meet Austin Jackson, the nation's most low-key recruit |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/austin-jackson-arizona-state-washington-usc-football-recruiting |access-date=December 9, 2019 |website=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> Jackson was rated a five-star recruit and the best collegiate prospect in Arizona as a senior and committed to play [[college football]] at the [[University of Southern California]] over offers from Washington and Arizona State.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Johnson |first=Chris |date=January 31, 2017 |title=USC lands commitment from five-star offensive tackle Austin Jackson |url=https://www.si.com/college/2017/01/31/austin-jackson-usc-trojans-national-signing-day |access-date=December 9, 2019 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Jackson played in all 14 of the Trojans games as a true freshman, appearing as a reserve offensive lineman and playing [[special teams]] on the field goal unit where he played on both sides and blocked a kick against [[2017 Colorado Buffaloes football team|Colorado]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Russell |date=November 7, 2019 |title=Austin Jackson:Left TAckle on the Rise |url=https://www.cover1.net/austin-jackson-left-tackle-on-the-rise-usc/ |access-date=December 2, 2019 |website=Cover1.net}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 12, 2017 |title=No. 11 USC pulls away from Colorado |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/football-ncaa-colorado-southerncaliforni/no-11-usc-pulls-away-from-colorado-idUSMTZEDBCBG598I |access-date=April 24, 2020 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> He was named USC's starting left tackle going into his sophomore year and started all 12 of the team's games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trevino |first=Chris |date=July 25, 2019 |title=Helton: OT Austin Jackson working his way back to full strength |url=https://247sports.com/college/usc/Article/USC-football-Austin-Jackson-bone-marrow-transplant-2019-season--133917662/ |access-date=December 2, 2019 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref>

Jackson missed part of the summer practices going into his junior season due having surgery to donate bone marrow to his sister, who has [[Diamond–Blackfan anemia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kartje |first=Ryan |date=August 3, 2019 |title=USC's Austin Jackson calls bone marrow donation to sister 'a godsend' |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/story/2019-08-03/usc-football-austin-jackson-bone-marrow-donation |access-date=December 9, 2019 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> He returned to practice in early August and worked his way back to playing shape in time to begin the season as the Trojans starting left tackle.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 3, 2019 |title=USC's Jackson returns to practice after donating bone marrow |url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-football/story/usc-s-jackson-returns-to-practice-after-donating-bone-marrow-080319 |access-date=December 9, 2019 |website=[[FoxSports.com]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> Jackson was named the [[Pac-12 Conference]] Offensive Lineman of the Week for Week 2 after his performance, which included blocking a 43-yard field goal attempt, in a 45–20 win over #23 [[2019 Stanford Cardinal football team|Stanford]] on September 7, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2019 |title=USC's Austin Jackson wins Pac-12 Football Offensive Lineman of the Week honors |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/uscs-austin-jackson-wins-pac-195810000.html |access-date=December 9, 2019 |website=[[Yahoo! Sports]]}}</ref> He was named first-team All-Pac-12 at the end of his junior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trevino |first=Chris |date=December 10, 2019 |title=USC Football: NFL mock drafts tabs OT Jackson at Top 15 pick |url=https://247sports.com/college/usc/Article/FOX-NFL-Mock-draft-tabs-Austin-Jackson-as-top-15-pick--140247792/ |access-date=December 11, 2019 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref>  Following the 2019 season, Jackson announced that he would forgo his senior year and declared for the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 15, 2020 |title=USC's Austin Jackson says he'll forgo senior year, enter draft |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/28492816/usc-austin-jackson-says-forgo-senior-year-enter-draft |access-date=January 19, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Jackson played in all 39 of USC's games during his collegiate career with 25 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Angelo |first=Tom |date=April 24, 2020 |title=Dolphins NFL Draft: First-round pick OT Austin Jackson calls his ceiling 'incredibly high' |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/nfl/2020/04/24/dolphins-nfl-draft-first-round-pick-ot-austin-jackson-calls-his-ceiling-rsquoincredibly-highrsquo/112274970/ |access-date=April 24, 2020 |website=[[The Palm Beach Post]]}}</ref>

Jackson was selected by the [[Miami Dolphins]] with the 18th overall pick in the first round of the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref name="maiorana">{{Cite web |last=Maiorana |first=Sal |date=April 23, 2020 |title=3 things to know about Miami Dolphins No. 18 overall pick Austin Jackson |url=https://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/sports/football/nfl/bills/2020/04/23/austin-jackson-miami-dolphins-nfl-draft-2020-pick-usc-ot-three-things-know/5155537002/ |access-date=April 23, 2020 |website=[[Rochester Democrat and Chronicle]]}}</ref> The Dolphins previously traded defensive back [[Minkah Fitzpatrick]] to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] to acquire the pick. Jackson made his NFL debut on September 13, 2020, in the season opener against the [[New England Patriots]], starting at left tackle and playing all of the team's offensive snaps.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schad |first=Joe |date=September 16, 2020 |title=What impressed coaches most about Austin Jackson's debut |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/nfl/2020/09/16/what-impressed-coaches-most-austin-jacksons-debut/5816722002/ |access-date=October 9, 2020 |website=[[The Palm Beach Post]]}}</ref> Jackson was placed on injured reserve on October 9 after suffering a foot injury in Week 4 against the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wolfe |first=Cameron |date=October 9, 2020 |title=Dolphins put rookie first-round LT Austin Jackson on IR with foot injury |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/30078763/dolphins-put-rookie-first-round-lt-austin-jackson-ir-foot-injury |access-date=October 9, 2020 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> He was activated on November 7.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 7, 2020 |title=Activated Austin Jackson, Elevated Kirk Merritt |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/activated-austin-jackson-elevated-kirk-merritt |access-date=December 9, 2020 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> 

Jackson entered the 2022 season as the Dolphins' starting right tackle. On September 16, 2022, Jackson was placed on short-term injured reserve with an ankle injury he suffered in Week 1.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jackson |first=Barry |date=September 16, 2022 |title=Dolphins' Jackson to miss at least four games. An update on where offensive line stands |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/barry-jackson/article264819434.html |access-date=May 30, 2023 |website=Miami Herald}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Louis-Jacques |first=Marcel |date=September 16, 2022 |title=Miami Dolphins RT Austin Jackson out at least four games after being placed on injured reserve |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/34604377/miami-dolphins-rt-austin-jackson-headed-short-term-injured-reserve-least-four-games |access-date=May 30, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Miami activated Jackson on November 1.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 1, 2022 |title=Miami Dolphins make roster moves |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-make-roster-moves-x4110 |access-date=November 1, 2022 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> He was placed back on injured reserve on December 5.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Louis-Jacques |first=Marcel |date=December 5, 2022 |title=Dolphins sign OT Eric Fisher, put OT Austin Jackson on IR |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/35189619/sources-dolphins-signing-ot-eric-fisher-ot-austin-jackson-ir |access-date=May 30, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Jackson returned as the Dolphins' right tackle in 2023. After starting every game protecting the blindside of [[Tua Tagovailoa]], he signed a three-year, $36 million contract extension with $20.7 million guaranteed.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins, Austin Jackson agree to three-year extension|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/dolphins-austin-jackson-agree-to-three-year-extension|author=Simmons, Myles|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=December 7, 2023}}</ref>

Jackson started 8 games for the Dolphins in 2024, and logged one fumble recovery. On November 12, 2024, it was announced that Jackson would miss the remainder of the season after undergoing knee surgery.<ref name="c718">{{cite web | last=Louis-Jacques | first=Marcel | title=Dolphins RT Jackson set for surgery; season over | website=ESPN.com | date=2024-11-12 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/42352633/dolphins-austin-jackson-set-knee-surgery-season-over | access-date=2025-01-01}}</ref>

Jackson started the 2025 season as Miami's starting right tackle. In the team's season opener against the [[2025 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]], Jackson suffered a toe injury that caused him to be placed on injured reserve on September 13, 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dolphins place right tackle Austin Jackson on IR|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46246728/dolphins-place-right-tackle-austin-jackson-ir|access-date=October 17, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> He was activated on November 29, ahead of the team's Week 13 matchup against the [[2025 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dolphins activate TE Darren Waller, OT Austin Jackson|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/dolphins-activate-te-darren-waller-ot-austin-jackson|access-date=December 9, 2025|website=nbcsports.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jackson's grandfather, [[Melvin Jackson (American football)|Melvin Jackson]], also played offensive line at USC and played in the NFL for the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patterson |first=Chip |date=February 1, 2017 |title=USC's huge National Signing Day push anchored by blue-chip OT Austin Jackson |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/uscs-huge-national-signing-day-push-anchored-by-blue-chip-ot-austin-jackson/ |access-date=December 9, 2019 |website=[[CBSSports.com]]}}</ref> In the summer of 2019, Jackson donated bone marrow to his younger sister Autumn, who had a rare form of anemia.<ref name=maiorana/>

He is currently dating McKayla Rain whom he shares one son with, born in 2023.{{citation needed|date=December 2023}}

'''Austin Mack''' (born August 31, 1997) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[Edmonton Elks]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He most previously played for the [[Montreal Alouettes]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]]. He signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] with the [[New York Giants]] in 2020.

==Early life==
Mack grew up in [[Fort Wayne, Indiana]], and attended [[Bishop Luers High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Woodard |first=Adam |date=October 7, 2015 |title=Character, values led Austin Mack to select U.S. Army All-American Bowl |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/character-values-led-austin-mack-to-select-u-s-army-all-american-bowl |website=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> He had 69 receptions for 1,062 yards and 15 touchdowns and was the runner up to Indiana's Mr. Football award as a junior.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Donohue |first=Tyler |date=May 8, 2015 |title=4-Star WR Austin Mack High on Ohio State: 'Columbus Is Buzzing Right Now' |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2458089-4-star-wr-austin-mack-high-on-ohio-state-columbus-is-buzzing-right-now |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref> In his senior season he caught 41 passes for 805 yards and six touchdowns and had to move to running back midway through the season due to injuries on the team and rushed for 718 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Axelrod |first=Ben |date=March 29, 2016 |title=Ohio State Freshman Austin Mack Can Be the Buckeyes' Next Great Receiver |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2628539-ohio-state-freshman-austin-mack-can-be-the-buckeyes-next-great-receiver |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref> Rated a four-star recruit and the best collegiate prospect in Indiana by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Mack committed to play [[college football]] at [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State]] going into his senior year over offers from [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]], [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]], and [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McMillen |first=Gabrielle |date=June 7, 2015 |title=Ohio State lands four-star recruit Austin Mack |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-football/news/ohio-state-lands-four-star-recruit-austin-mack-verbal-commitment-football/1o0ntc5okycmv1oqkm642kro0a |website=[[Sporting News]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Mack was a member of the Ohio State Buckeyes for four seasons and joined the team as an early enrollee. Mack played mostly on special teams as a true freshman with two receptions for 15 yards on offense. As a sophomore, he caught 24 passes for 343 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Landis |first=Bill |date=July 14, 2018 |title=Top 50 Ohio State football players for 2018: No. 10, Austin Mack |url=https://www.cleveland.com/sports/erry-2018/07/ab1b53dde8819/top-50-ohio-state-football-pla.html |access-date=April 29, 2020 |website=[[The Plain Dealer]]}}</ref> Mack scored his first collegiate touchdown on September 16, 2017, against [[Army Black Knights football|Army]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tamanini |first=Matt |date=September 20, 2017 |title=Following his first career touchdown, Austin Mack could be Ohio State's go-to receiver |url=https://www.landgrantholyland.com/2017/9/20/16339338/ohio-state-news-austin-mack-jt-barrett-go-to-receiver |website=LandGrantHolyLand.com |publisher=[[SB Nation]]}}</ref> He had 26 receptions for 331 yards and one touchdown before suffering a season ending ankle injury eight games into his junior season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patterson |first=Chip |date=October 23, 2018 |title=Ohio State WR Austin Mack out indefinitely after foot injury suffered in Purdue loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/ohio-state-wr-austin-mack-out-indefinitely-after-foot-injury-suffered-in-purdue-loss/ |access-date=April 29, 2020 |website=[[CBSSports.com]]}}</ref> As a senior, Mack caught 27 passes for 361 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marini |first=Glenn |date=April 24, 2020 |title=Luers grad Mack eager for NFL opportunity |url=https://www.wane.com/sports/local-sports/luers-grad-mack-eager-for-nfl-opportunity/ |access-date=April 29, 2020 |website=WANE.com}}</ref> He finished his collegiate career with 79 receptions, 1,050 yards and six touchdowns.<ref name="g256">{{cite web | last=Murphy | first=Patrick | title=Breaking down Buckeyes in 2020 NFL Draft: Austin Mack | website=247Sports | date=2020-04-22 | url=https://247sports.com/college/ohio-state/Article/Breaking-down-Ohio-State-Buckeyes-football-in-2020-NFL-Draft-Austin-Mack-146318921/ | access-date=2024-10-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Stepien | first=Garrett | title=WATCH: Austin Mack runs 40-yard dash at NFL combine | website=247Sports | date=2020-02-28 | url=https://247sports.com/Article/NFL-Combine-2020-Austin-Mack-40-yard-dash-Ohio-State-Buckeyes-football-144359091/ | access-date=2025-04-26}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
Mack signed with the [[New York Giants]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on April 25, 2020, shortly after the conclusion of the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baird |first=Nathan |date=April 25, 2020 |title=Ohio State football's Austin Mack to join New York Giants as undrafted free agent: Report |url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2020/04/ohio-state-footballs-austin-mack-to-join-new-york-giants-as-undrafted-free-agent-report.html |access-date=April 26, 2020 |website=[[The Plain Dealer]]}}</ref> He was waived on September 5, and was re-signed to the practice squad the following day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 5, 2020 |title=New York Giants announce 53-man roster |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-roster-2020-nfl-season-new-york-announce-53-man-roster-joe-judge |website=Giants.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 6, 2020 |title=Giants sign 14 to practice squad; 2 spots open |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-roster-sign-13-players-to-practice-squad-2-spots-open |website=Giants.com}}</ref> On October 3, Mack was elevated to the active roster, but he was listed inactive for the team's game the next day against the [[Los Angeles Rams]] and was subsequently reverted to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hickey |first=Kevin |date=October 3, 2020 |title=Giants elevate WR Austin Mack to the active roster |url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2020/10/03/new-york-giants-roster-moves-austin-mack-active-roster/ |access-date=October 4, 2020 |work=Giants Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> Mack was signed to the active 53-man roster on October 13, and made his NFL debut on October 18, catching one pass for one yard in a 20–19 win over the [[2020 Washington Football Team season|Washington Football Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 13, 2020 |title=Giants' Austin Mack: Ascends to active roster |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/giants-austin-mack-ascends-to-active-roster/ |access-date=October 13, 2020 |website=CBSSports.com |publisher=RotoWire}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Leonard |first=Pat |date=October 18, 2020 |title=Rookie Andrew Thomas benched for start of Giants win for being late to team meeting |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/football/giants/ny-giants-andrew-thomas-20201018-m3uvqx5qg5g6lkbaoxpelki6ae-story.html |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=[[New York Daily News]]}}</ref> On November 8, he caught four passes for 72 yards in a 23–20 win against Washington, including a 50-yard reception from [[Daniel Jones (American football)|Daniel Jones]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Botte |first=Peter |date=November 14, 2020 |title=Austin Mack impressing Giants with gritty play: 'Scrappy dude' |url=https://nypost.com/2020/11/14/austin-mack-impressing-giants-with-gritty-play-scrappy-dude/ |access-date=November 15, 2020 |work=[[New York Post]]}}</ref>

On August 31, 2021, Mack was placed on [[injured reserve list|injured reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen, Michael |date=September 1, 2021 |title=New York Giants announce 53-man roster |url=https://www.giants.com/news/new-york-giants-final-53-man-roster-2021-nfl-season-joe-judge |website=Giants.com}}</ref> He was released on September 7.

===Tennessee Titans===
Mack signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]]' [[practice squad]] on November 23, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=November 23, 2021 |title=Titans Make 13 Roster Moves – On the Active Roster, Practice Squad and Injured Reserve – On a Busy Tuesday |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-make-13-roster-moves-on-the-active-roster-practice-squad-and-injured-rese |access-date=November 23, 2021 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref> He was released by the Titans on November 30.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt, Jim |date=November 30, 2021 |title=Titans Place LB Monty Rice on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-place-lb-monty-rice-on-injured-reserve |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On December 6, 2021, Mack was signed to the [[San Francisco 49ers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 6, 2021 |title=49ers Sign a WR and LB to the Practice Squad; Waive Two Players |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-a-wr-and-lb-to-the-practice-squad-waive-two-players |website=49ers.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the 49ers on February 2, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2022 |title=49ers Sign 11 Players to Reserve/Future Contracts |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-11-players-to-reserve-future-contracts |website=49ers.com}}</ref> Mack was waived/injured on August 22, and placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 22, 2022 |title=49ers Sign S Tashaun Gipson Sr.; Waive WR Austin Mack |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-s-tashaun-gipson-sr-waive-wr-austin-mack |access-date=August 22, 2022 |website=49ers.com}}</ref> He was released by San Francisco on August 27.

===Montreal Alouettes (first stint)===
On May 4, 2023, Mack signed with the [[Montreal Alouettes]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Transactions – Football player trades and signings |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/ |access-date=May 19, 2023 |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]]}}</ref> On June 23, against the [[Hamilton Tiger-Cats]], he caught his first two touchdown passes and helped the Alouettes with a 38–12 win over the Tiger-Cats. In his [[2023 Montreal Alouettes season|first year]] in the CFL, Mack played in 17 regular season games where he had 78 receptions for 1,154 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 CFL League Maser Standings |url=https://d3ham790trbkqy.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/2023_CFL_League_Stats_Report_Week_21.pdf |access-date=January 3, 2024 |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]]}}</ref> He finished fifth in the league in receiving yards and was named a CFL All-Star for his outstanding first season in the league.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 8, 2023 |title=Austin Mack and Marc Antoine Dequoy named CFL All-Stars |url=https://en.montrealalouettes.com/2023/11/08/austin-mack-and-marc-antoine-dequoy-named-cfl-all-stars/ |publisher=[[Montreal Alouettes]]}}</ref> In the team's two playoff games, he had seven catches for 82 yards and one touchdown as the team qualified for the [[Grey Cup]] championship game. In the [[110th Grey Cup]], Mack led all receivers with six receptions for 103 yards and one touchdown as the Alouettes defeated the [[2023 Winnipeg Blue Bombers season|Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] 28–24.<ref name="playbyplay">{{Cite news |date=November 19, 2023 |title=110th Grey Cup |url=https://www.cfl.ca/games/6391/montreal-alouettes-vs-winnipeg-blue%20bombers/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231119234907/https://www.cfl.ca/games/6391/montreal-alouettes-vs-winnipeg-blue%20bombers/ |archive-date=November 19, 2023 |access-date=January 3, 2024 |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]]}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On January 10, 2024, Mack signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waack |first=Terrin |date=January 10, 2024 |title=Falcons sign 16 players to reserve/future contracts in 2024 |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/16-players-signed-reserve-future-contracts-2024-austin-mack-tyler-vrabel |access-date=January 10, 2024}}</ref> He was waived by the Falcons on August 12.

===Montreal Alouettes (second stint)===
On August 19, 2024, it was announced that Mack had re-signed with the Alouettes to a four-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CFL all-star receiver Austin Mack rejoins Montreal Alouettes after NFL stint |url=https://3downnation.com/2024/08/19/cfl-all-star-receiver-austin-mack-rejoins-montreal-alouettes-after-nfl-stint/ |publisher=3DownNation |date=August 19, 2024}}</ref> In his first game back, he recorded three receptions for 32 yards, but suffered an ankle injury and was placed on the six-game injured list.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Als move star WR Austin Mack to the six-game injured list |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2024/09/05/report-als-move-star-wr-austin-mack-to-the-six-game-injured-list/ |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=September 5, 2024}}</ref> He returned for the final two games of the regular season and had a total of ten catches for 145 yards in [[2024 Montreal Alouettes season|2024]].<ref name=CFLbio>{{Cite web |title=Austin Mack |url=https://www.cfl.ca/players/austin-mack/167550/ |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=January 29, 2026}}</ref>

In the [[2025 Montreal Alouettes season|2025 season]], Mack suffered ankle and hamstring injuries, causing him to miss six games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Mack non-participant in practice for Montreal Alouettes |url=https://3downnation.com/2025/07/29/austin-mack-non-participant-in-practice-for-montreal-alouettes/ |publisher=3DownNation |date=July 29, 2025}}</ref> In 12 regular season games, he had 73 catches for 674 yards and two touchdowns.<ref name=CFLbio/> He also played in all three post-season games, including the [[112th Grey Cup]] where he had no receptions and one defensive tackle in the team's 25–17 loss to the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]].<ref name=112th>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cfl.ca/games/6581/montreal-alouettes-vs-saskatchewan-roughriders/ |title=112th Grey Cup |date=November 16, 2025 |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=January 29, 2026}}</ref> He was released in the following off-season on January 26, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Montreal Alouettes release All-CFL receiver Austin Mack prior to offseason bonus |url=https://3downnation.com/2026/01/26/montreal-alouettes-release-all-cfl-receiver-austin-mack-prior-to-offseason-bonus/ |publisher=3DownNation |date=January 26, 2026}}</ref>

===Edmonton Elks===
Mack signed a two-year deal with the CFL's [[Edmonton Elks]] on January 29, 2026.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cfl.ca/2026/01/29/elks-sign-receiver-austin-mack/ | title=Elks sign receiver Austin Mack | publisher=[[CFL.ca]] | date=January 29, 2026 | accessdate=29 January 2026}}</ref>

'''Austin Edwards''' (born August 27, 1997) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He was signed by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2020 following his [[college football]] career with the [[Ferris State Bulldogs football|Ferris State Bulldogs]], where he was a first-team All-American selection and won the Gene Upshaw Award for Best D2 Defensive Lineman of The Year of 2019. He played in the 2019 East–West Shrine Game.

'''Austin Fort''' (born May 14, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Wyoming Cowboys]].

==Early life==
Fort attended [[Campbell County High School (Wyoming)|Campbell County High School]] in Gillette, Wyoming, where he played quarterback, punter, and placekicker. In his two-year career starting at quarterback for the Campbell County Camels, he totaled 4,667 yards with 45 touchdowns on only 4 interceptions and helped lead his team to the Wyoming 4A state championship in 2012. Fort was considered a first-team all-state selection at quarterback and kicker as both a junior and senior, was named the top football recruit in Wyoming as a senior, and was a Top 25 Rocky Mountain state selection. A 2-star recruit, Austin chose to stay in-state and played at [[University of Wyoming]] over offers from [[Air Force Football|Air Force]], [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado]], [[Colorado State Rams football|Colorado State]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois]], and [[Sam Houston State Bearkats football|Sam Houston State]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Austin Fort, Wyoming |url=https://gowyo.com/sports/football/roster/austin-fort/3090}}</ref>

==College career==
In 2014, Fort redshirted as a freshman at the University of Wyoming. The following spring, Fort was transitioned from quarterback to tight end. This decision prompted Fort to transfer to [[Chabot College|Chabot Community College]] to continue playing quarterback. In his one season at Chabot, Fort appeared in eight games, throwing for 282 yards on 20 pass attempts, with three touchdowns and one interception.<ref>{{cite web |title=2015-16 Football Statistics |url=https://athletics.chabotcollege.edu/sports/fball/2015-16/teams/chabot?view=lineup&r=0&pos=off |website=Chabot Athletics |access-date=8 September 2022}}</ref> Fort returned to Wyoming for the 2016 season as a tight end. He appeared in all of the team's 13 games, exclusively on special teams, where he recorded two tackles.<ref>{{cite web |title=Austin Fort, Wyoming |url=https://gowyo.com/sports/football/roster/austin-fort/3090}}</ref> In the 2017 and 2018 seasons, Fort started at tight end for the Cowboys and caught 17 passes for 229 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web |title=Austin Fort - Denver Broncos |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/team/players-roster/austin-fort/}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Denver Broncos===
After going undrafted in the 2019 draft, Austin Fort was invited to participate at the [[Denver Broncos]] training camp. Fort impressed the Broncos and he was signed to the team following training camp. He caught 87 yards and a touchdown in the preseason game against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], but tore his [[ACL tear|ACL]] after catching a 29-yard dive pass and landing on his knee. Fort was placed on injury reserve on August 9, 2019. On July 29, 2020, Austin Fort was promoted to the active roster. However, Fort agitated his previous knee injury during practice and was placed on injured reserve on August 14, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Denver Broncos TE Austin Fort tears ACL again |date=August 15, 2020 |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/broncos/news/broncos-te-austin-fort-suffers-setback-with-knee-requires-surgery}}</ref>

On August 31, 2021, Fort was waived by the Broncos.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos make series of roster transactions to reach 53-man limit|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-make-series-of-roster-transactions-to-reach-53-man-limit|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=August 31, 2021}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On September 14, 2021, Fort was signed to the [[Tennessee Titans]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Promote K Randy Bullock to Active Roster, Place S Amani Hooker on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-promote-k-randy-bullock-to-active-roster-place-s-amani-hooker-on-injured-|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=September 14, 2021}}</ref> After the Titans were eliminated in the [[2021–22 NFL playoffs|Divisional Round]] of the 2021 playoffs, he signed a reserve/future contract on January 24, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-11-players-to-reserve-futures-contracts|work=TennesseeTitans.com|title=Titans Sign 11 Players to Reserve/Futures Contracts|date=January 24, 2022|accessdate=January 24, 2022|first=Jim|last=Wyatt}}</ref> He was waived on May 2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Titans Waive Four Players|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/roster-moves-titans-waive-four-players|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=May 2, 2022}}</ref>

'''Austin Faoliu''' (born January 9, 1999) is an American [[American football|football]] [[nose tackle]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[Oregon Ducks football|University of Oregon]].

==Early life==
Faoliu attended [[Junípero Serra Catholic High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mosqueda |first=Justis |date=May 1, 2021 |title=Austin Faoliu NFL Draft 2021: Scouting Report for Dallas Cowboys DL |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2931795-austin-faoliu-nfl-draft-2021-scouting-report-for-dallas-cowboys-dl |access-date=April 15, 2023 |work=Bleacher Report}}</ref> As a sophomore, he had 48 carries for 351 yards and 4 touchdowns.

As a senior, he transferred to [[Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)|Mater Dei High School]] and was named a starter at [[nose guard]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fryer |first=Steve |date=February 1, 2017 |title=Mater Dei's Faoliu gets two last-minute offers, but stays with Oregon |url=https://www.ocvarsity.com/articles/faoliu-86440-dei-mater.html |access-date=April 15, 2023 |website=Orange County Register}}</ref> He tallied 32 tackles (9 for loss), 1.5 sacks and one forced fumble, while receiving All-County honors. He contributed to a second place in the CIF Southern Section Division 1.

==College career==
Faoliu accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Oregon]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Albano |first=Dan |date=January 21, 2017 |title=Football recruiting: Mater Dei's Austin Faoliu commits to Oregon |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2017/01/21/football-recruiting-mater-deis-austin-faoliu-commits-to-oregon/ |access-date=October 9, 2021 |website=Orange County Register}}</ref> As a freshman, he appeared in 12 games, starting the first two contests. He posted 22 tackles (2.5 for loss) and one sack. He had 3 tackles, one sack and one forced fumble against the [[University of Arizona]]. He made 4 tackles against [[Boise State University]].

As a sophomore, he appeared in 11 games with 6 starts. He totaled 44 tackles and 2 sacks. He had 7 tackles against [[Portland State University]]. He made 7 tackles against the [[University of Utah]].

As a junior, he appeared in 13 games with 8 starts. He registered 39 tackles (5 for loss), 2 sacks. He had 6 tackles and 1.5 sacks against [[Arizona State University]]. He made 8 tackles (1.5 for loss) and one quarterback hurry against [[Oregon State University]].

As a senior, the football season was reduced to 7 games due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]]. He started in 6 contests, while collecting 21 tackles (0.5 for loss). He had five tackles against [[Oregon State University]]. He finished his college career with 43 games, 124 tackles, 10 tackles for loss, 5 sacks and 3 forced fumbles.

He was released from his contract on May 15, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=XFL Transactions |url=https://www.xfl.com/xfl-transactions |access-date=May 18, 2023}}</ref>

=== Seattle Seahawks ===
On May 16, 2023, Faoliu signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=May 16, 2023 |title=Seahawks Sign NT Austin Faoliu |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-nt-austin-faoliu |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/[[physically unable to perform|PUP]] list on August 29, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Seahawks Make Roster Moves, Establish Initial 2023 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-establish-initial-2023-53-man-roster |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was activated on November 6, then waived the following day and re-signed to the practice squad. He was not signed to a reserve/future contract after the season and thus became a free agent upon the expiration of his practice squad contract.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Smith |first=Corbin K. |date=January 8, 2024 |title=Seahawks Sign Seven Practice Squad Players to Future Contracts |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/seahawks/news/seattle-seahawks-easop-winston-levi-bell-signed-future-contracts |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref>

'''Austin Deculus''' (born March 12, 1999)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Deculus Bio Information – NCAA College Football |url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-football/austin-deculus-player-bio |access-date=April 30, 2022 |website=FOX Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|offensive tackle]] for the [[Tennessee Titans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]].

== Early life ==
Deculus was born in [[Mamou, Louisiana]], but grew up in [[Cypress, Texas]], where he attended [[Cy-Fair High School]]. He was highly regarded as an offensive line prospect coming out of high school, being ranked the No. 5 offensive tackle prospect by [[ESPN]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=July 8, 2019 |title=Austin Deculus |url=https://lsusports.net/roster/austin-deculus/ |access-date=May 7, 2022 |website=LSU |language=en-US}}</ref>

== College career ==
In his freshman season at LSU in 2017, Deculus played in all 13 games on [[special teams]], appearing only twice on the offensive line due to injuries to the team's starters.<ref name=":0" />

In the second week of his sophomore season in 2018, Deculus had his first start at left tackle in a game against [[Southeastern Louisiana Lions football|Southeastern Louisiana]]. He shifted to right tackle the following week and started there for the remainder of the season. He finished the year with a total of 827 snaps played, including all 86 snaps in the [[2019 Fiesta Bowl (January)|Fiesta Bowl]].<ref name=":0" />

Deculus was considered the "most improved" offensive lineman at LSU in 2019 and started 13 games, missing two due to injury. He played every snap in the Tigers' [[2020 College Football Playoff National Championship|national championship]] win over Clemson, totaling 885 snaps over the whole season.<ref name=":0" />

Deculus started all ten games at right tackle in 2020, and was named to the 2020 [[Southeastern Conference]] Academic Honor Roll.<ref name=":0" />

Deculus took advantage of an extra year of eligibility due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] as he entered his fifth year playing for the Tigers. In 12 games in 2021, he played a total of 829 snaps, and recorded his only [[college football]] tackle in a game against [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]].<ref name=":0" />

'''Audric Estimé''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ɛ|s|t|ɪ|m|eɪ}} {{Respell|EH|-|stih|-|may|}}; born September 6, 2003) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] for the [[New Orleans Saints]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] and was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the fifth round of the [[2024 NFL draft]]. He has also been a member of the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].

==Early life==
Estimé was born in Atlanta, Georgia and grew up in [[Nyack, New York]].<ref name="TheBeast">{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |title=The Beast: 2024 NFL Draft Guide |url=https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2024/04/11162958/TheBeast2024_MasterFile-8.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240411212702/https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2024/04/11162958/TheBeast2024_MasterFile-8.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 11, 2024 |url-access=subscription |access-date=April 14, 2024 |website=[[The Athletic]] |pages=28}}</ref> Estimé attended [[Saint Joseph Regional High School]] in [[Montvale, New Jersey]]. As a senior, he had 1,857 rushing yards and 22 [[touchdowns]] and was the [[NJ.com]] Football Player of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lanni |first=Patrick |date=December 10, 2020 |title=Audric Estime of St. Joseph (Mont.) is N.J.'s football Player of the Year for 2020 |url=https://www.nj.com/highschoolsports/2020/12/audric-estime-of-st-joseph-mont-is-njs-football-player-of-the-year-for-2020.html |access-date=November 13, 2023 |website=NJ.com}}</ref> He originally committed to [[Michigan State University]] to play college football before switching to the [[University of Notre Dame]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Solari |first=Chris |date=December 18, 2020 |title=Michigan State football loses RB commit Audric Estime to Notre Dame |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2020/12/18/michigan-state-football-recruiting-audric-estime-notre-dame/6547289002/ |access-date=2024-06-22 |work=Detroit Free Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tartaglia |first=Greg |date=December 18, 2020 |title=Audric Estime, St. Joseph star running back, signs with Notre Dame |url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/high-school/football/2020/12/18/audric-estime-st-joseph-running-back-signs-notre-dame/3950310001/ |access-date=2024-06-22 |website=North Jersey Media Group}}</ref>

==College career==
Estimé spent his freshman year at Notre Dame in 2021 as a backup to [[Kyren Williams]] and had seven rushes for 60 yards.<ref>[https://www.ndinsider.com/story/sports/2022/03/31/notre-dame-running-back-audric-estime-wants-prove-himself-2022-college-football-marcus-freeman/7227067001/ Audric Estime has a chip on his shoulder. Can Irish RB use it to prove himself in 2022?]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hansen |first=Eric |date=June 10, 2021 |title=Estime brings a bigger body and big dreams to Notre Dame football freshman class |url=https://www.ndinsider.com/story/sports/football/2021/06/10/audric-estime-brings-bigger-body-big-dreams-notre-dame-football/7642283002/ |access-date=2024-03-04 |website=Notre Dame Insider}}</ref>

In 2022, his playing time increased.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Berardino |first=Mike |date=October 5, 2022 |title=Late-night texts help Audric Estime forgive himself for first Notre Dame fumble |url=https://www.ndinsider.com/story/sports/football/2022/10/05/notre-dame-football-audric-estime-moves-past-fumble-with-coachs-help-deland-mccullough-tommy-rees/69530604007/ |access-date=2024-03-04 |website=Notre Dame Insider}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Stires |first=Sean |date=August 21, 2022 |title=Audric Estime Brings Talent – And Hype – To The Notre Dame Backfield |url=https://www.si.com/college/notredame/football/notre-dame-football-audric-estime-brings-talent-and-hype-to-backfield-stires |work=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> He finished the regular season with 825 yards on 142 carries with 11 rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Audric Estime 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/audric-estime-1/gamelog/2022 |access-date=2024-06-23 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com}}</ref> On December 30, 2022, Estimé rushed for 95 yards on 14 carries in Notre Dame’s 45–38 victory in the TaxSlayer Gator Bowl versus [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gator Bowl - Notre Dame vs South Carolina Box Score, December 30, 2022 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2022-12-30-south-carolina.html |access-date=2024-06-23 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com}}</ref>

Estimé had 210 carries for 1,341 rushing yards and 18 touchdowns in the 2023 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Audric Estime 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/audric-estime-1/gamelog/2023 |access-date=2024-06-23 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com}}</ref>
