=== Denver Broncos ===
Estimé was drafted in the fifth round with the 147th overall pick by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the [[2024 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |date=2024-04-28 |title=Round 5, No. 147: Broncos draft Notre Dame RB Audric Estimé |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/nfl-draft-2024-rounds-4-7-order-picks-trades-grades/TSEmTpKuGVE1/ |access-date=2024-06-23 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on September 11, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos promote FB Michael Burton to active roster, place RB Audric Estime on IR|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-promote-fb-michael-burton-to-active-roster-place-rb-audric-estime-on-ir|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=September 11, 2024}}</ref> On October 12, he returned to the active roster.<ref name=":16">{{Cite web |last=Gabriel |first=Parker |date=2024-10-12 |title=Broncos put C Luke Wattenberg, WR Josh Reynolds on injured reserve, rookie RB Audric Estime set to return vs. Chargers |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2024/10/12/broncos-luke-wattenberg-josh-reynolds-injured-reserve/ |access-date=2024-10-12 |website=The Denver Post |language=}}</ref> In Week 16 against the Los Angeles Chargers, he scored his first NFL  touchdown.<ref name="a852">{{cite web | last=Nguyen | first=Joe | title=WATCH: Broncos’ Audric Estime runs in 1st NFL touchdown against Chargers | website=The Denver Post | date=2024-12-20 | url=https://www.denverpost.com/2024/12/19/watch-broncos-audric-estime-1st-nfl-touchdown/ | access-date=2025-01-01}}</ref> Prior to the Broncos' wild card matchup against the [[Buffalo Bills]], Estimé was benched and listed as inactive in favor of [[Tyler Badie]], who had recently been activated from injured reserve.<ref>{{Cite web |last=By |last2=Smith |first2=Michael David |last3=By |last4=Smith |first4=Michael David |date=2025-01-12 |title=Audric Estime inactive for Broncos vs. Bills |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/audric-estime-inactive-for-broncos-vs-bills |access-date=2025-08-28 |website=NBC Sports |language=}}</ref> 

Early in the 2025 offseason, Estimé competed with Badie in addition to [[Jaleel McLaughlin]], [[Blake Watson]], and second-round rookie [[RJ Harvey]]. Ahead of training camp, the Broncos also signed veteran running back [[J. K. Dobbins]]. By the beginning of the preseason, Estimé was fifth in the rotation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Evans |first=Luca |date=2025-08-10 |title=Broncos’ Audric Estime says he can be ‘three-down back’ in NFL. But will it be in Denver? |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/08/10/audric-estime-broncos-running-backs/ |access-date=2025-08-28 |website=The Denver Post |language=}}</ref> On August 25, 2025, he was waived by the Broncos.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Heath |first1=Jon |title=Broncos’ backfield might be set after the Blake Watson cut |url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/broncos/2025/08/25/broncos-news-running-backs-set-after-blake-watson-cut/85824688007/ |website=Broncos Wire}}</ref>

=== Philadelphia Eagles===
On August 29, 2025, Estimé signed with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jensen |first=Chad |date=2025-08-27 |title=Report: Former Broncos RB Signs With NFC Team After Being Cut |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/broncos/news/broncos-audric-estime-signs-eagles-practice-squad |access-date=2025-08-28 |website=Denver Broncos On SI |language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-29 |title=Eagles sign RB Audric Estime and DB Ambry Thomas to the practice squad, place G/C Willie Lampkin on IR |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-rb-audric-estime-and-db-ambry-thomas-to-the-practice-squad-place-g-c-willie-lampkin-on-ir |access-date=2025-08-28 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |language=}}</ref> He was released by the Eagles on October 14.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McPherson |first1=Chris |title=Eagles release WR Javon Baker, RB Audric Estime from the practice squad |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-release-javon-baker-audric-estime-from-the-practice-squad |website=philadelphiaeagles.com |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref>

=== New Orleans Saints ===
On October 21, 2025, Estimé was signed to the [[New Orleans Saints]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/velus-jones-jr-audric-estime-new-orleans-saints-roster-moves-transactions-2025-nfl-season |website=NewOrleansSaints.com |access-date=22 October 2025}}</ref> On November 5, he was promoted to the active roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/audric-estime-running-back-coziah-izzard-defensive-tackle-new-orleans-saints-roster-moves-transactions-2025-nfl-season-11-5-2025|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=November 5, 2025}}</ref> Estimé played his first game of the season on December 7, where he ran for 11 yards from three carries in an upset victory over the [[2025 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref> {{cite web |title=Saints 24 20 Buccaneers |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nfl/game/_/gameId/401772792/saints-buccaneers |website=espn.com |access-date=8 December 2025}}</ref> In a Week 17 win over the [[2025 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]], he recorded a career-high 94 rushing yards and one touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Saints' Audric Estimé: Career-high rushing total in win|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/saints-audric-estime-career-high-rushing-total-in-win/|access-date=April 17, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Estimé is of [[Haitians|Haitian]] descent.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=McFadden |first=Ryan |date=2024-08-11 |title=How Broncos RB Audric Estime’s special bond with cousin helped him overcome tragedy, realize NFL dream: "He made me see the light" |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2024/08/11/broncos-audric-estime-terrence-fede-tragedy/ |access-date=2024-08-26 |work=The Denver Post}}</ref> He has one brother, Khadar.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-12-15 |title=Audric Estimé |url=https://fightingirish.com/roster/audric-estime/ |access-date=2024-08-26 |website=Notre Dame Fighting Irish - Official Athletics Website}}</ref>

When he was ten years old, Estimé's mother died of [[sickle cell disease]]. Estimé and his brother were taken in by their aunt and uncle's family, which included their cousin [[Terrence Fede]], who played in the NFL as a defensive end. Fede acted as a mentor to Estimé over the course of his football career.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Legwold |first=Jeff |date=2024-08-01 |title=Could Audric Estime fix the Broncos' run-game woes? Why his punishing run style fits the team's 'vision' |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/nfl/story/_/id/40691712/audric-denver-broncos-rookie-running-back-notre-dame |access-date=2024-08-26 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

'''Austen Pleasants''' (born August 22, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|offensive tackle]] for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio Bobcats football|Ohio Bobcats]].

== Early life ==
Pleasants was born on August 22, 1997, in [[Ironton, Ohio]], son of Michael Wilburn and Jennifer Vanderhoof-Pleasants. Has one younger brother, Arik.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Austen Pleasants - 2019 - Football |url=https://ohiobobcats.com/sports/football/roster/austen-pleasants/612 |access-date=June 10, 2022 |work=Ohio University}}</ref> He attended [[Dawson-Bryant High School]] in [[Coal Grove, Ohio]], and was a four year [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[High school football|football]], [[basketball]], and [[Track and field|Track and Field]].<ref name=":0" /> He earned multiple honors while playing as an [[offensive lineman]] and [[defensive tackle]] and was a 2-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] as a lineman.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Austen Pleasants's Football Recruiting Profile |url=https://www.ncsasports.org/football-recruiting/ohio/coal-grove/dawson-bryant-high-school/austen-pleasants |access-date=June 10, 2022 |website=www.ncsasports.org}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Austen Pleasants, Dawson-Bryant , Offensive Tackle |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Austen-Pleasants-72197/high-school-125210/ |access-date=June 10, 2022 |work=247Sports}}</ref> He accepted a football scholarship offer from [[Ohio University]] over [[University of Akron]] and [[University of Toledo]].<ref name=":1" />

== College career ==
Pleasants [[redshirted]] his first college year for [[Ohio Bobcats football|Ohio]] but finished his career with 28 games and 20 starts.<ref name=":0" /> He earned Second-team All-[[Mid-American Conference]] honors in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MAC Announces 2019 All-MAC Teams & Postseason Awards |url=https://getsomemaction.com/news/2019/12/3/football-mac-announces-2019-all-mac-teams-postseason-awards.aspx |access-date=June 10, 2022 |website=getsomemaction.com}}</ref>

=== Jacksonville Jaguars ===
On April 25, 2020, Pleasants was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] after going undrafted in the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shipley |first=John |title=Jaguars 2020 Undrafted Free Agent Tracker |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jaguars/draft/jaguars-2020-undrafted-free-agent-tracker |access-date=June 10, 2022 |work=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> On September 7, he was re-signed to Jacksonville's [[practice squad]] after being waived the day before.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harvey |first=Demetrius |date=September 7, 2020 |title=Jaguars officially sign 15 players to practice squad |url=https://www.bigcatcountry.com/2020/9/7/21425756/jacksonville-jaguars-officially-sign-15-players-to-practice-squad-roster-2020 |access-date=June 11, 2022 |work=Big Cat Country}}</ref> On October 18, Pleasants was placed on the practice squad/[[COVID-19]] list.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austen Pleasants: Shifts to COVID-19 list |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/austen-pleasants-shifts-to-covid-19-list/ |access-date=June 11, 2022 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> He was activated off the list on October 22.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austen Pleasants: Comes off COVID-19 list |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/austen-pleasants-comes-off-covid-19-list/ |access-date=June 11, 2022 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> After being waived in September 2021, Pleasants was signed to Jaguars practice squad on October 9, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austen Pleasants: Signed to practice squad by Jags |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/austen-pleasants-signed-to-practice-squad-by-jags/ |access-date=June 11, 2022 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> On October 12, he was released from the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 12, 2021 |title=Jaguars do some shuffling with the practice squad |url=https://jaguarswire.usatoday.com/2021/10/12/jaguars-do-some-shuffling-with-the-practice-squad/ |access-date=June 11, 2022 |work=Jaguars Wire}}</ref>

=== Carolina Panthers ===
Pleasants was signed to the [[Carolina Panthers]]' practice squad on October 12, 2021, the same day he was released from the Jaguars.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 12, 2021 |title=Panthers sign OL Austen Pleasants to practice squad |url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/2021/10/12/panthers-ol-austen-pleasants-practice-squad/ |access-date=July 27, 2022 |work=Panthers Wire}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on November 27, and played his first career game in the Week 12 10–33 loss against the [[2021 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austen Pleasants (OT): Bio, News, Stats & more |url=https://www.panthers.com/team/players-roster/austen-pleasants/logs/ |access-date=July 27, 2022 |website=www.panthers.com}}</ref> On January 11, 2022, Pleasants signed a reserve/future contract with the team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Reserve/Futures Contracts: 1/11/22 |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2022/01/nfl-reserve-futures-contracts-1-11-22 |access-date=July 27, 2022 |work=Pro Football Rumors}}</ref> On August 22, Pleasants was waived by the Panthers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=August 22, 2022 |title=Panthers waive Austen Pleasants, Khalan Tolson |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/08/22/panthers-waive-austen-pleasants-khalan-tolson/ |access-date=January 9, 2023 |work=ProFootballTalk}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Chargers ===
On November 9, 2022, Pleasants was signed to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign Breiden Fehoko to Active Roster; Place Austin Johnson on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-sign-breiden-fehoko-to-active-roster |access-date=January 9, 2023 |website=www.chargers.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Los Angeles on January 17, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign 12 Players to Contracts|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-sign-12-players-to-contracts|website=Chargers.com|date=January 17, 2023}}</ref> On August 29, Pleasants was waived by the Chargers and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Reduce Roster to 53 Players|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-reduce-roster-to-53-players-2023|website=Chargers.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign 12 Players to Practice Squad|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-sign-12-players-to-practice-squad|website=Chargers.com|date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> He was released on September 12.

'''Austin Ajiake''' ({{IPAc-en|'|ɑ:|dʒ|i|k|eɪ}}, born June 30, 2000)<ref name="pfr">{{cite web |title=Austin Ajiake Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AjiaAu00.htm |access-date=September 8, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241205125943/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AjiaAu00.htm |archive-date=December 5, 2024}}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UNLV Rebels football|UNLV Rebels]] and was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2023.

==Early life==
Ajiake was born in [[Hayward, California]] and grew up in [[Fremont, California|Fremont]]. He attended [[Bellarmine College Preparatory]] in [[San Jose, California|San Jose]], where he was a two-sport athlete, competing in both football and [[track and field]].<ref name=UNLV>{{cite web |title=Austin Ajiake |website=UNLVRebels.com |url=https://unlvrebels.com/sports/football/roster/austin-ajiake/14965 |access-date=February 21, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221200956/https://unlvrebels.com/sports/football/roster/austin-ajiake/14965 |archive-date=February 21, 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
Ajiake played 10 games in the [[2018 UNLV Rebels football team|2018 season]], recording five tackles. He played all 12 games in the [[2019 UNLV Rebels football team|2019 season]], recording 14 tackles. He played all six games in the [[2020 UNLV Rebels football team|2020 season]], which was abridged due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], recording seven tackles. In the [[2021 UNLV Rebels football team|2021 season]], Ajiake appeared in only eight games due to injury, though he recorded 74 tackles and earned an honorable mention to the all-[[Mountain West Conference]] team.<ref name= "UNLV" />

Ajiake played all 12 games in the [[2022 UNLV Rebels football team|2022 season]]; his 132 tackles were the fifth-most in the country, and the 4th-most in UNLV school history. He also recorded four sacks, two interceptions, and a fumble recovery. Ajiake was chosen for both the [[2022 Hula Bowl]] and the [[2022 East–West Shrine Bowl]], and was named to the first-team all-MWC team.<ref name= "UNLV" /> Additionally, Ajiake earned the 2022–2023 Mountain West Male Scholar-Athlete of the Year award.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wright |first=Jarah |date=August 3, 2023 |title=Austin Ajiake named Mountain West Male Scholar-Athlete of the Year, signs with Denver Broncos |website=[[KTNV]] |url=https://www.ktnv.com/sports/unlv-sports/austin-ajiake-named-mountain-west-male-scholar-athlete-of-the-year-signs-with-denver-broncos |access-date=February 21, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241012154201/https://www.ktnv.com/sports/unlv-sports/austin-ajiake-named-mountain-west-male-scholar-athlete-of-the-year-signs-with-denver-broncos |archive-date=October 12, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Grimala |first=Mike | date=August 3, 2023 |title=Austin Ajiake named top MWC scholar-athlete |website=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2023/aug/03/austin-ajiake-named-top-mwc-scholar-athlete/ |access-date=February 21, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127084929/https://lasvegassun.com/news/2023/aug/03/austin-ajiake-named-top-mwc-scholar-athlete/ |archive-date=November 27, 2024}}</ref>

'''Austin McNamara''' (born February 24, 2001)<ref name=birthday /> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]] and [[kickoff specialist]] for the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech Red Raiders]].

==Early life==
McNamara was born in [[San Jose, California]], and grew up in [[Gilbert, Arizona]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://texastech.com/sports/football/roster/austin--mcnamara/12512|publisher=[[Texas Tech Red Raiders]]|title=Austin McNamara}}</ref> He attended [[Highland High School (Arizona)|Highland High School]] in Arizona where he played basketball and football.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/arizona-republic/143248738/|newspaper=[[Arizona Republic]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 19, 2018|page=C9|title=Highland's McNamara a tall order for foes|author=Scott, Dana}} {{Open access}}</ref> A [[placekicker]] and [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]], he averaged 42 yards-per-punt, made 12 [[field goal]]s and all 63 of his [[Conversion (gridiron football)|extra point]] attempts as a [[Senior (education)|senior]], being named first-team all-state.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/recruiting/2018/12/25/gilbert-highland-punter-austin-mcnamara-commits-texas-tech-football/2411939002/|newspaper=[[Arizona Republic]]|title=Highland punter Austin McNamara commits to Texas Tech|date=December 25, 2018|author=Obert, Richard}}</ref> Ranked as the best punter recruit nationally, McNamara committed to play [[college football]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech Red Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.eastvalleytribune.com/sports/highland-s-austin-mcnamara-excited-for-opportunity-at-texas-tech/article_7f258480-0a2a-11e9-ac52-a34c2d912cb1.html|newspaper=[[East Valley Tribune]]|title=Highland's Austin McNamara excited for opportunity at Texas Tech|date=December 27, 2018|author=Alvira, Zach}}</ref>

==College career==
McNamara won the starting job at Texas Tech as a [[true freshman]] in 2019 and averaged 45.0 yards per punt, which was then fourth all-time in school history, second in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) that year among freshmen, and second in the [[Big 12 Conference]].<ref name="auto"/> He was selected a freshman [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] and a first-team All-Big 12 player.<ref>{{Cite web|date=January 13, 2020|publisher=[[KLBK-TV]]|url=https://www.everythinglubbock.com/sports/red-raider-nation/texas-tech-punter-austin-mcnamara-named-fwaa-freshman-all-american/|title=Texas Tech punter Austin McNamara named FWAA Freshman All-American }}</ref>

The following year, McNamara played nine games and punted 41 times while averaging 46.3 yards per punt, then second all-time in Texas Tech history and fifth in the [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|FBS]]; he was named first-team All-Big 12 again and second-team All-Texas by ''[[Dave Campbell's Texas Football]]''.<ref name="auto"/> In a game against [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia]] that season, he recorded a 87-yard punt which broke both the team and Big 12 records.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kcbd.com/2020/10/28/austin-mcnamaras-record-breaking-punt/|publisher=[[KCBD]]|title=Austin McNamara's record breaking punt|date=October 28, 2020|author=Christy, Pete}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2020/10/watch-texas-tech-punter-austin-mcnamara-bomb-a-preposterous-87-yard-punt|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|title=Watch Texas Tech punter Austin McNamara bomb a preposterous 87-yard punt|date=October 24, 2020|author=Schwartz, Nick}}</ref>

In 2021, McNamara set both the Texas Tech and Big 12 all-time record with a 48.2 yard punting average while playing all 13 games, additionally setting an NCAA single-game record during the year for most 50-yard punts in a game.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2022/07/05/texas-tech-big-12-football-austin-mcnamara-special-teams-record-setting-season/7785004001/|newspaper=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|author=Williams, Don|via=archive.is|title=Austin McNamara anchors Texas Tech special teams after record-setting season|date=July 5, 2022|access-date=April 1, 2024|archive-date=March 12, 2024|archive-url=https://archive.today/20240312235702/https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2022/07/05/texas-tech-big-12-football-austin-mcnamara-special-teams-record-setting-season/7785004001/|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2023/03/30/tech-football-notebook-record-setting-punter-planning-to-add-kickoff-duty/70066521007/|newspaper=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|title=Record-setting Tech punter planning to add kickoff duty|date=March 30, 2023|author=Williams, Don}}</ref> He was a second-team all-conference selection and was named first-team All-Texas by ''Dave Campbell's Texas Football'', also being named the best [[special teams]] player in the state by the publication.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/big-12/2022/06/28/austin-mcnamara-red-raiders-named-dctf-all-texas-college-team/7759806001/|newspaper=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|title=Texas Tech Roundup: Austin McNamara, Red Raiders named to DCTF All-Texas College teams|date=June 28, 2022}}</ref>

McNamara totaled 50 punts and averaged 44.3 yards as a senior in 2022, being named third-team All-Big 12 by [[Phil Steele]] and [[Pro Football Focus]].<ref name="auto"/> He returned for a final season in 2023, having received an extra year of eligibility due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2023/10/19/austin-mcnamara-back-in-familiar-spot-when-texas-tech-football-visits-byu/71163241007/|newspaper=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|author=Williams, Don|title=Austin McNamara back in familiar place when Texas Tech football visits BYU|date=October 19, 2023|via=archive.is|access-date=April 1, 2024|archive-date=October 19, 2023|archive-url=https://archive.today/20231019134307/https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2023/10/19/austin-mcnamara-back-in-familiar-spot-when-texas-tech-football-visits-byu/71163241007/|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref> He averaged 46.3 yards per punt in his last year, being named the Big 12 Special Teams Player of the Year, the first Texas Tech player to receive the honor, as well as first-team All-Big 12.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://texastech.rivals.com/news/texas-tech-s-top-5-players-of-2023|website=[[Rivals.com]]|title=Texas Tech's Top 5 Players of 2023|date=December 28, 2023|author=Ramirez, Jarrett}}</ref> He was one of two punters invited to play at the [[2024 Senior Bowl]], and the second Texas Tech punter all-time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.everythinglubbock.com/sports/red-raider-nation/mcnamara-accepts-senior-bowl-invite/|publisher=[[KLBK-TV]]|title=McNamara accepts Senior Bowl invite |date=November 30, 2023|author=Collier, David}}</ref>

'''Austin Mylek Keys''' (born April 3, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]] and [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]].

==Early life==
Keys attended Seminary High School located in [[Seminary, Mississippi]]. He was rated as a three-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] for the [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss Rebels]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Berry |first1=Zach |date=March 25, 2019 |title=3-star LB Austin Keys commits to Ole Miss3-star LB Austin Keys commits to Ole Miss |url=https://www.redcuprebellion.com/2019/3/25/18280775/ole-miss-football-recruiting-austin-keys-seminary-mississippi-linebacker-jeff-koonz-2020 |access-date=27 April 2025 |website=Red Cup Rebellion|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>

==College career==
=== Ole Miss ===
As a freshman in 2020, Keys took a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Green |first1=Tom |title=Ole Miss transfer Austin Keys ‘everything’ Auburn thought he’d be at linebacker |url=https://www.al.com/auburnfootball/2023/04/ole-miss-transfer-austin-keys-everything-auburn-thought-hed-be-at-linebacker.html |website=AL.com |access-date=27 April 2025}}</ref> In 2021, he recorded 12 tackles in six games before an injury cut his season short.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Clemente |first1=Christian |title=Auburn lands former Ole Miss LB Austin Keys |url=https://247sports.com/college/auburn/Article/Auburn-lands-former-Ole-Miss-LB-Austin-Keys-202610550/ |website=247Sports |access-date=27 April 2025}}</ref> In 2022, Keys notched 39 tackles with three and a half being for a loss, two sacks, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cohen |first1=Matt |title=Year 1 on The Plains: Meet Auburn transfer linebacker Austin Keys |url=https://www.al.com/auburnfootball/2023/07/year-1-on-the-plains-meet-auburn-transfer-linebacker-austin-keys.html |website=AL.com |access-date=27 April 2025}}</ref> After the season, he entered his name into the [[NCAA transfer portal]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rudolph |first1=Justin |title=Ole Miss linebacker Austin Keys enters NCAA transfer portal |url=https://www.on3.com/college/ole-miss-rebels/news/ole-miss-linebacker-austin-keys-enters-ncaa-transfer-portal/ |website=On3.com |access-date=27 April 2025}}</ref>

=== Auburn ===
Keys transferred to play for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stephenson |first1=Creg |title=Auburn ‘getting a great player’ in Austin Keys, Ole Miss’ Cedric Johnson says |url=https://www.al.com/auburnfootball/2023/07/auburns-getting-a-great-player-in-austin-keys-ole-miss-cedric-johnson-says.html |website=AL.com |access-date=27 April 2025}}</ref> He made his Auburn debut in the 2023 season opener, where he made the start, notching two tackles in a win over [[2023 UMass Minutemen football team|UMass]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cohen |first1=Matt |title=Auburn LB Austin Keys not on field during open practice period |url=https://www.al.com/auburnfootball/2023/09/auburn-lb-austin-keys-not-on-field-during-open-practice-period.html |website=AL.com |access-date=27 April 2025}}</ref> In week 11, Keys put up three tackles, a pass deflection, and a forced fumble versus [[2023 Vanderbilt Commodores football team|Vanderbilt]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Silva |first1=Richard |title='Hunting mentality': How the return of Austin Keys has elevated Auburn football's defense |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2023/11/07/auburn-football-austin-keys-linebacker-hugh-freeze/71435688007/ |website=Montgomery Advisor |access-date=27 April 2025}}</ref> He finished the 2023 season, playing in eight games due to injury, where he recorded 30 tackles with three for a loss, two sacks, and a forced fumble.<ref>{{cite web |last1=King |first1=Nathan |title=Austin Keys reunites with former Ole Miss coach D.J. Durkin on Auburn defense |url=https://247sports.com/college/auburn/article/dj-durkin-austin-keys-auburn-football-2024-229385778/ |website=247Sports |access-date=27 April 2025}}</ref> During the 2024 season, Keys tallied 39 tackles and two pass deflections.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rauterkus |first1=Peter |title=3 players who stood out at Auburn football’s Pro Day |url=https://www.al.com/auburnfootball/2025/03/3-players-who-stood-out-at-auburn-footballs-pro-day.html |website=AL.com |access-date=27 April 2025}}</ref>

'''Austin Brinkman''' (born June 20, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[long snapper]] for the [[Houston Texans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia Mountaineers]] and was signed by the Texans as an [[Free agent#Undrafted free agent|undrafted free agent]] in 2025.

==Early life==
Brinkman is from [[Bel Air, Maryland]].<ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.wvnstv.com/goldandbluenation/austin-brinkman-showing-signs-of-future-nfl-long-snapper/?nxsparam=3|publisher=[[WVNS-TV]]|title=Austin Brinkman showing signs of future NFL long snapper |date=November 21, 2024|author=Decker, Ryan}}</ref> He began playing [[American football|football]] and learned [[Long snapper|long snapping]] at a young age from his father, who later served as his coach in high school.<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.journal-news.net/journal-news/brinkman-earning-acclaim-as-wvu-long-snapper/article_9098a253-3be1-5d2d-acf0-aadec5d33ff7.html|newspaper=[[The Journal (West Virginia newspaper)|The Journal]]|via=[[archive.today]]|title=Brinkman Earning Acclaim As WVU Long Snapper|date=November 22, 2024|author=Redd, Derek|archive-url=https://archive.today/20250625014412/https://www.journal-news.net/journal-news/brinkman-earning-acclaim-as-wvu-long-snapper/article_9098a253-3be1-5d2d-acf0-aadec5d33ff7.html|archive-date=2025-06-25}}</ref> He attended [[The John Carroll School]], where he played football as a [[quarterback]], [[defensive back]], [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]] and long snapper.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2021/01/05/john-carroll-alum-austin-brinkman-closes-out-freshman-football-season-at-west-virginia/|newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|via=[[archive.today]]|title=John Carroll alum Austin Brinkman closes out freshman football season at West Virginia |date=January 5, 2021|author=McRoberts, Randy |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250625014344/https://www.baltimoresun.com/2021/01/05/john-carroll-alum-austin-brinkman-closes-out-freshman-football-season-at-west-virginia/ |archive-date=2025-06-25}}</ref> He also competed in [[basketball]], [[lacrosse]] and [[track and field]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://wvusports.com/sports/football/roster/austin-brinkman/17758|publisher=[[West Virginia Mountaineers]]|title=Austin Brinkman}}</ref> Brinkman served as John Carroll's long snapper for three seasons and was also named first-team All-Harford as a [[Senior (education)|senior]] at punter.<ref name="auto3"/> After high school, he decided to play [[college football]] for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia Mountaineers]].<ref name="auto3"/>

==College career==
Brinkman [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] as a [[true freshman]] at West Virginia in 2020.<ref name="auto"/> He then won the starting long snapper job in 2021 and appeared in all 13 games, being placed on [[Athletic scholarship|scholarship]] prior to the last game of the season.<ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wtrf.com/goldandbluenation/wvu-puts-austin-brinkman-on-scholarship/|publisher=[[WTRF-TV]]|title=WVU puts Austin Brinkman on scholarship |date=December 11, 2021|author=Decker, Ryan}}</ref> Brinkman played in all 12 games in 2022, all 13 games in 2023, and 12 games in 2024.<ref name="auto1"/> In his last year, he was named third-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] by [[Phil Steele]], a semifinalist for the [[Patrick Mannelly Award]] as best long snapper nationally, and first-team All-[[Big 12 Conference]] by Phil Steele.<ref name="auto1"/> Brinkman finished his collegiate career having appeared in 50 of the 51 games across his four seasons as a starter.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wboy.com/goldandbluenation/wvu-football/austin-brinkman-signs-with-houston-texas-following-nfl-draft/|publisher=[[WBOY-TV]]|title=Austin Brinkman signs with Houston Texas following NFL Draft |date=April 26, 2025|author=Redfern, Kevin}}</ref> He was also named first-team Academic All-Big 12 in 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024.<ref name="auto1"/> He was invited to the [[2025 Senior Bowl]].<ref name="auto2"/>
